body:
Weekly launchd job that reclaims REGENERABLE dev cruft so the host never hits a mid-build "No space left on device" wall (it did 2026-06-28 at 99%% on a 460Gi disk).

**Safety (unattended deleter, conservative by design):** allowlist-only paths under `~/Library`, each re-validated (prefix + no `..` + exists) before any rm; age-guarded per-child reaping (never races a live build/test); native cleaners (brew/pip/npm/simctl) + age-based regenerables always, heavy re-download caches (playwright/Chrome) only under pressure (<30Gi); **never touches** Archives/UserData/`~/Downloads`/`~/code`; `DISK_CLEANUP_DRY_RUN=1` deletes nothing.

Reuses fix-sweep `remove_hard`. Weekly plist (Sun 04:00). **12 safety checks green** (allowlist + `..` refusal, age-spare-fresh, dry-run-no-delete, purge_cache refuses non-cache).

author: 007byte
body:
## Summary

Cluster 7 / P1 HIGH-RISK: bind the KDF transcript into derived keys and add AEAD associated data (AD) to the MEK wrap, the verify-marker, and the index, so a ciphertext cannot be transplanted between headers or silently downgraded across versions. Also transcript-binds the hybrid KEM session key (ephemeral X25519 pub + ML-KEM ciphertext).

All new behavior is gated behind a **NEW vault version V6** (`MAGIC_V6 = "USBVLT06"`, same 24576-byte layout as V4/V5). NEW vaults are written as V6; everything else is opt-in only.

## Backward-compatibility guarantee

Existing **V2/V3/V4/V5 vaults open via the UNCHANGED legacy path** — this was the absolute invariant for this change:

1. `MAGIC_V6` is new, so no existing on-disk file ever matches version 6.
2. `read()`/`write()` only ADD a version-6 arm reusing the V4/V5 byte layout; parsing of existing vaults is untouched.
3. `unlock()`/`create_new()` branch on `self.version`: anything `<= 5` calls the EXACT existing `derive_kek` + plain `wrap_mek`/`unwrap_mek` + plain verify-marker + plain index decrypt with zero behavioral change.
4. `compute_hmac` binds the version byte first under a V6 domain tag, so a V6->V5 magic-flip downgrade recomputes a different MAC and fails closed (mirrors the existing, passing V5->V4 downgrade test).
5. `derive_kek`, `wrap_mek`, `unwrap_mek`, `cipher::encrypt/decrypt`, index `encrypt/decrypt`, and hybrid v1 `seal/open` are NOT modified — only new functions are added alongside. No struct fields were added, so the 27 existing `VaultHeader { .. }` literals are untouched.

No on-disk migration is forced; V4/V5 are deliberately NOT auto-upgraded to V6 (V6 needs the password to re-derive the transcript-bound KEK, unavailable at commit time).

## What changed

**Rust (`usbvault-crypto`)**
- `kdf.rs`: `build_kdf_transcript` (frozen canonical layout), `derive_kek_v6` (Argon2id -> HKDF-SHA256 expand over the transcript), `wrap_mek_ad`/`unwrap_mek_ad`.
- `vault/header.rs`: `MAGIC_V6`/`HEADER_SIZE_V6`, V6 read/write arms, V6 `compute_hmac` domain branch, `wrap_ad_v6`/`verify_ad_v6`/`index_ad_v6` AD builders, V6 `create_new` (default for new vaults) + version-gated `unlock`.
- `vault/index.rs`: `encrypt_with_ad`/`decrypt_with_ad`.
- `pqc/hybrid.rs`: `combine_shared_secrets_bound` + `hybrid_seal_v2`/`hybrid_open_v2` (version-byte prefixed; transcript = `eph_x25519_pub || ml_kem_ct`). v1 left byte-identical.

**Web/TS mirror (`usbvault-app`)**
- `native.ts`/`bridge.ts`: `buildKdfTranscript`/`buildWrapAD`/`buildVerifyAD`/`buildIndexAD` + `deriveKekV6` — byte-exact mirrors of the Rust builders.

## Cross-impl KAT (byte-for-byte proof)

`usbvault-crypto/tests/kdf_ad_interop_kat.rs` and `usbvault-app/src/crypto/__tests__/kdfAdInterop.kat.test.ts` share FIXED hex vectors for all four AD/transcript builders **and a full `derive_kek_v6` output** (Argon2id 65536/3/4 + HKDF). Both sides assert the identical hex — including the live web `deriveKekV6` (hash-wasm Argon2id + @noble HKDF) matching the Rust `derive_kek_v6` output `8a510dcf…`. Plus a Rust-only hybrid v2 roundtrip + "v1 cannot open a v2 box" negative guard.

V6 vault *files* are intentionally NOT byte-identical across web/Rust (the web fallback wraps the MEK with AES-GCM, Rust with XChaCha20), so the cross-impl guarantee is at the PRIMITIVE level — which is what V6 unlock correctness depends on.

## Tests run

- `cargo build`: clean, 0 warnings.
- Rust: 109 lib tests + format_compatibility / vault_lifecycle / integration / kdf_ad_interop_kat / share_interop_kat / nist_test_vectors / sharing / srp suites — all green. The 37-min property suite is left to CI.
- Web: `tsc --noEmit` clean; `kdfAdInterop.kat.test.ts` (5), `shareInterop.kat.test.ts`, `native.test.ts`/`bridge.test.ts` (80) — all green; eslint --fix applied to touched TS.

## opsFollowups

- The FFI index encrypt/decrypt entrypoints (`usbvault_vault_encrypt_index`/`_decrypt_index`) take only `(master_key, json)` and have no header context (version/salt/active_slot). Wiring V6 index AD through them is an ABI change spanning the TS bridge and all callers — out of scope for this V-gated, additive change. The `index_ad_v6` primitive is implemented and KAT-proven; the wrapped-MEK + verify-marker AD (the parts that gate unlock) ARE wired through `create_new`/`unlock`. A V6 vault's index is currently encrypted with the legacy no-AD path until that ABI is extended; follow-up to thread `index_ad_v6(version, salt, active_slot)` into the orchestrator.

author: ronniejay22
body:
## Summary

A plain `pytest` run in a worktree **hangs past 10 minutes** because `.worktreeinclude` copies the real `backend/.env`, so the credential-gated integration tests see live creds and execute against **Supabase / Claude / Firecrawl / QStash**. This adds an opt-in **offline mode** that runs only the fast, network-free unit tests.

## What changed

- **`backend/conftest.py` (new)** — adds `--offline` (also `KNOT_OFFLINE_TESTS=1`). In `pytest_configure` (before collection) it blanks every external-credential constant in `app.core.config`, so each `is_*_configured()` returns `False` and the existing `requires_*` guards skip their integration tests. A report header announces offline mode. Default behavior is unchanged when the flag/env aren't set.
- **Gated two previously-ungated integration groups** that failed/errored once creds were blanked:
  - `test_step_3_11_ios_integration.py` — 4 iOS onboarding classes now carry `@requires_supabase`
  - `test_supabase_connection.py::TestEnvironmentConfig` — gated (it only asserts creds are present)
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — documents `pytest --offline` in the worktree-testing note.

## Validation

| Mode | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest` (before) | hung >10 min on live calls |
| `pytest --offline` | **1245 passed, 622 skipped, 0 failed — 9.3s** |
| `pytest --collect-only` (default) | 1867 collected, unchanged |

Use `--offline` for quick iteration; run the full live suite before shipping a change that touches an integration path.

## What

A `docs-reviewer` substance pass over `PHASE_STATUS.md` (the canonical chronological tracker) surfaced doc-drift that accumulated after the `v2.0.0-phase8` tag shipped (2026-06-23). This PR fixes every confirmed issue and adds a deterministic guard so the highest-severity one (defense-layer counts) cannot recur.

All edits verified against ground truth: `compute/warehouse/flag_registry.py`, the live git tags, and `CLAUDE.md`.

## Fixes

| § | Was | Now | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Current state | `36 declared / 9 active vetoes` | `38 declared / 10 active vetoes` (+`stale_filing_hard`) | **HIGH — factual** |
| Next deliverables | "the next tag is **v2.0**" (shipped) | "v2.0.0-phase8 shipped 2026-06-23; next tag is **v2.1**" | HIGH |
| Next deliverables | "No more phase-pinned tags" (vs the live `-phase8` suffix) | clarified "…**after v2.0**" | MEDIUM |
| Lane B #544 | "Needs RATIFY-SHADOW … only Slice-8 / v2.0 gate left" | "RATIFY-WITH-CONDITIONS 2026-06-23 (DOCS-ONLY); post-v2.0 deferred → Q3 audit" | MEDIUM |
| Release ladder | `v1.4.0-phase4.6` hash `bbca9cac` | `a820caee` (real tag SHA) | MEDIUM |
| Release ladder | Slice-8 issue refs `#540/#542` | landed PRs `#548/#564` | LOW |
| Phase table row 8 | `🟡 IN PROGRESS` + "Next = Slice 8 …" | `✅ DONE — 2026-06-23 (v2.0.0-phase8)` | LOW |

## Error→regression ratchet

The defense-count drift is a **mechanical class** (a count), so per `CLAUDE.md` §Conventions it is determinized in the same PR: `tools/check_defense_layer_counts.py` now also anchors the `PHASE_STATUS.md` §Current state rows (`**N declared boolean flags**` + `| Active vetoes | **N**`). These phrases appear **only** in the current-state table, so the chronological-log `defense UNCHANGED at 36` snapshots do **not** false-positive. The §Current state row previously escaped the guard because it was unanchored.

## Scope / safety

- **Docs + a CI-guard extension only** — no `compute/**` / `frontend/**` / schema change.
- Rankings / scores / output **BYTE-IDENTICAL**; the defense flag SET is **UNCHANGED** (38/10 all along — the PHASE_STATUS headline was stale, now matches the registry).
- Lockstep: `PHASE_STATUS_INFLIGHT.md` entry added (CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md carry no related drift, so no substance diff needed there).

## Verification

- `python tools/check_defense_layer_counts.py` → PASS (now covers PHASE_STATUS.md)
- `python tools/check_agent_hook_consistency.py` → PASS
- `ruff check .` → PASS
- `python tools/preflight.py` cheap rungs (ruff · doc-count · model-pin · agent/hook · defense-layer) → PASS. pytest/tsc skipped — the remote sandbox lacks `pandas`/Node; CI runs the full suite. The 119 local pytest collection errors are all `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pandas'` (env), unrelated to this diff.

## Not in this PR (owner decision)

§Current state "Production run" still points at the 2026-06-11 cron (`65bfd335`) with a 2026-06-11 "RATIFY-B verification pending" note. Whether to advance the pointer or confirm RATIFY-B cleared needs owner knowledge — left untouched.

author: araray
body:
## Release Story

This is intentionally a small release. The branch explored shared token counters and capability descriptions, then reverted both changes to keep Confy focused on its core responsibility: configuration loading and overrides. The net result is a boundary test that prevents future ecosystem helpers from drifting back into the config library.

## Highlights

- Adds `tests/unit/test_domain_boundaries.py` to lock Confy's config-only scope.
- Documents the architectural decision that token counting belongs in LLMCore, not Confy.
- Documents the architectural decision that shared capability descriptions should stay outside Confy.
- Keeps the public runtime package unchanged after reverting the exploratory helper APIs.

## Impact

Downstream packages should not depend on Confy for token estimation, model capability metadata, or agent/runtime descriptions. Confy remains the minimal configuration foundation used by the ecosystem, and this test protects that boundary explicitly. There is no expected runtime behavior change.

## Review Notes

- Baseline: merge base `efa65b0a73af` with `origin/main`.
- Includes `release_notes.md` in the branch.
- Secret-pattern scan found no credential-shaped additions.

## Validation

- Not rerun in this pass; changes added here are release notes only on top of the existing feature branch.

## Reviewer Focus

- The domain-boundary test and whether it captures the intended package ownership rule.
- Confirming that no token or capability helper modules remain exported from Confy.

## Automated Status Summary
#### Scope
Two numeric trust boundaries accept non-finite / out-of-range input and fail open instead of closed:

1. **Performance metrics & conflict resolution** — `src/inv_man_intake/performance/metrics.py:95`
   reads `monthly_returns = [point.value for point in payload.monthly.points]` with no finite check; a `NaN`
   point yields `annualized_volatility=nan`, `sharpe_ratio=nan`, and `max_drawdown=0.0` (the

   `abs(nan - other) > _FLOAT_TOLERANCE` is false, so a `nan` source value reports `conflict_count=0` while the
   resolved point stays `nan`. (codex-verified by execution.)
2. **Threshold policy config** — `src/inv_man_intake/extraction/confidence.py:78` parses

score-/routing-bearing code.

author: stephenthecold
body:
## The gap (HIGH, audit finding — auth hot zone)

The login TOTP challenge had **no attempt cap, lockout, or throttle**. After primary auth a session is `twoFactorPending`; the only remaining gate is a 6-digit TOTP (~1e6 wide). With no cap, an attacker who already has the user's primary password could **brute-force the second factor**. Every *other* code-entry path is capped — break-glass (`MAX_ATTEMPTS=5`) and portal SMS-OTP (`OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS=5`); this one was the outlier.

## Fix

- **Schema (additive migration):** `User.totpFailedAttempts Int @default(0)`, `User.totpLockedUntil DateTime?`.
- **`verifyLoginChallenge`** now mirrors the break-glass lockout:
  - reject while `totpLockedUntil > now` **without checking the code** (audited `user.totp.login_locked`);
  - on each wrong code, **atomically** `increment` the counter — correct under a concurrent guess burst, where a read-then-write would lose updates and let the cap be slipped;
  - trip a **15-minute** lock at **5** attempts;
  - **clear** counter + lock on a successful verify.
- The `/2fa` form shows a distinct "too many attempts" message when locked.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm test` — 793 passing, incl. new pure-helper tests (`isTotpLocked`, `totpLockUntil`)
- `npm run test:integration` (real Postgres) — new test proves: the lock trips at the cap; a **currently-valid** code is rejected while locked (short-circuits before verification); a good code after cooldown succeeds and **resets** the counter
- `npm run lint` — clean
- `prisma migrate dev` created `20260629004719_totp_login_lockout` and applied it to the live DB

## Scope / blast radius

Auth hot zone, but the change is contained: additive columns (forward-only, no data transform) + lockout logic in the single login-challenge path (one caller, `app/2fa/actions.ts`). Enrollment/disable, the 2FA proof, and break-glass are untouched. Worst case if mis-tuned is over-aggressive lockout of a legitimate user — mitigated by mirroring the proven break-glass cap, an auto-expiring 15-min cooldown, and reset-on-success. Backup codes remain available once the short lock clears.

author: mvillmow
body:
## What

Bump `pixi-version` in CI from `v0.67.2` to `v0.70.2` across both workflows:
- `.github/workflows/_required.yml` (7 pins)
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` (2 pins)

No other changes.

## Why

CI pins setup-pixi to **v0.67.2**, which can only read pixi lock-format **v6**. Any v7 lock fails the install step with:

```
Error: × Lock-file version 7 is newer than supported
  help: Maximum supported version: 6 (pixi v0.67.2)
        Cannot continue with --locked or --frozen mode as the lock-file cannot be read.
```

Open PRs **#263, #271, #273, #276** intentionally ship **v7** pixi.lock files (multi-platform macOS/Windows + large mcp/otel dep trees). With the current pin, their entire pipeline dies at `pixi install` — every job reds. This bump unblocks all four.

## Ecosystem consistency

Sibling repo **Agamemnon** already runs **pixi v0.70.2** on main with v7 locks successfully. This is the consistent fix.

## Safety: does not red main

main's own `pixi.lock` is still **v6**. pixi v0.70.2 is backward-compatible. Verified locally with the exact CI command:

- `pixi install --locked` against main's v6 lock → **exit 0** (warn-only: "older format (v6)"; the lock is **not** rewritten, stays v6).
- `pixi install --locked` against #263's v7 lock → **exit 0**, no version error.
- For contrast, v0.67.2 against the v7 lock reproduces the failure above.

So this change is safe on main and unblocks the v7 PRs.

author: matiaszanolli
body:
… #31)

#20 (NH-04): two contradictory noise-period helpers existed. The module-level get_noise_period indexed an identity NOISE_PERIOD_TABLE without inverting, so a higher MIDI note produced a higher period index = lower pitch (backwards), while PitchProcessor._get_noise_period inverted correctly. Drop the identity table, make get_noise_period the single inverting MIDI->4-bit-index mapper (higher note -> lower index -> higher pitch, clamped to 0-15), and have _get_noise_period delegate to it so both stay in lockstep.

#31 (NH-07): the sweep units ($4001/$4005) were never written at init, so power-on garbage could leave a sweep enabled and continuously bend or silence a pulse channel (APU_PULSE_REFERENCE §1, §5 cond. 2). Disable both sweeps (lda #$08, enable clear) in all three init paths: the macro engine's audio_init (audio_engine.asm), the standalone reset proc, and the direct init_music.

Adds regression tests for noise direction/unification and the sweep writes.

author: butterflysky-ai
body:
## Summary

Closes the file-ops policy gap: Claude Code's file tools (Write, Edit, Read) bypass Bash entirely and were previously unpoliced by prodagent-tool-gate. The hook silently exited with no opinion for any non-Bash tool.

This PR adds:

- **`prodagent-policy::file_ops`** — new module with `FileOpsPolicy`, `FilePathRule`, `FileToolKind` types and `evaluate_file_tool()` function. Write/Edit classified as Mutating (default: Ask), Read as ReadOnly (default: Allow). Supports ordered path-glob rules with optional tool-kind scoping.

- **Config integration** — `FileOpsPolicy` added to `PolicyConfig`, with overlay support in `PolicyOverlay`. Path rules from higher-tier configs are prepended (evaluated first). TOML config supports `[[policy.file_ops.path_rules]]` entries with `path`, `decision`, and optional `tools` fields.

- **Monotonicity enforcement** — project configs cannot use file-ops path rules to weaken user-level policy. Unscoped and mixed-tool rules are compared against the mutating default (strictest applicable floor). Read-only-scoped rules compare against the read_only default.

- **Hook routing** — `prodagent-tool-gate` now routes Write/Edit/Read tools through the new evaluator instead of silently skipping them. Decision logging covers file ops with the target path.

- **7 new config-level tests** covering TOML round-trips, tool scoping, overlay prepend semantics, monotonicity enforcement (both tightening and weakening), and loader integration.

- **15 new policy-level tests** covering effect classification, path matching (exact, glob, double-star, partial-prefix rejection), rule ordering, tool-scoped rules, deny rules, and normalization.

- **6 new tool-gate tests** covering default decisions, path rules, deny paths, and missing/empty path handling.

Example config:
```toml
# Allow writes under ~/dev/ and /tmp/
[[policy.file_ops.path_rules]]
path = "~/dev/*"
decision = "allow"

[[policy.file_ops.path_rules]]
path = "/tmp/*"
decision = "allow"

# Block writes to /etc/
[[policy.file_ops.path_rules]]
path = "/etc/*"
decision = "deny"
tools = ["write", "edit"]
```

## Test plan

- [x] All 816 tests pass (`cargo nextest run`)
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets` — zero new warnings (two pre-existing)
- [x] `cargo fmt` — clean
- [ ] Manual integration test with Claude Code hook

author: shortstackengineer
body:
## What

Adds **Layer 0: static pre-execution checks** — `loopgen lint` plus a run-path workspace preflight — so a misconfigured spec fails in milliseconds instead of after hours of agent work.

Motivated by a real batch run that burned ~4h: the workspace resolved to `$HOME` (compounded relative paths) and stateful evaluators raced on one dev DB. Both are now caught **before any agent turn**.

## `loopgen lint <spec|batch>`

Static rule engine (no execution). `--base`, `--strict`, `--json`; exit `2` on errors, `1` on `--strict` warnings, else `0`. Selected rules:

- **`SPEC-WORKDIR-NOT-PROJECT`** *(error)* — resolved workspace isn't a git repo / has no stack markers but the spec expects an existing project (catches the `../..`-twice → `$HOME` bug).
- **`SPEC-EVAL-BINARY-MISSING` / `SPEC-EVAL-FILE-MISSING`** — a check's binary/script doesn't exist where it runs.
- **`SPEC-EVAL-DESTRUCTIVE-ENV`** — a check mutates a DB without a test env.
- **`SPEC-EVAL-SHARED-RESOURCE`** — multiple stateful checks that can race.
- **`SPEC-SMOKE-SELF-FULFILLING`** — a smoke that creates records but never drives a real endpoint.
- **Batch rules** — `BATCH-MAXITER-OVERRIDE`, `BATCH-NEEDS-AS-ORDERING`, `BATCH-FAILFAST-CHAIN`.

## Run-path preflight (0b)

Every `run` now prints the resolved absolute workspace and runs the error-severity workspace checks as preflight (skippable with `--skip-preflight`). Greenfield specs are unaffected (the project-expecting rules only fire on a clear signal: project-local binstubs or `snapshot: git`).

## Tests / gates

Full suite green, coverage ≥85% (lint files 96–100%), mutation ≥60 (lint module ~70%).

body:
`_run_refresh` never applied `excludeTagName` — excluded scenes and performers were still scored and written on every refresh. `_run_dry` and `_run_full` both correctly called `stash_io.filter_excluded()`; refresh had no equivalent logic. Compounding this, `SCENE_LIGHT_FRAGMENT` didn't fetch `tags { id }`, making scene filtering impossible without a schema change.

## Changes

- **`stash_io.py`**
  - Add `tags { id }` to `SCENE_LIGHT_FRAGMENT`
  - Add `tag_ids` to `map_scene_light` result dict

- **`restash.py` — `_run_refresh`**
  - Resolve `exclude_id` via `stash_io.resolve_tag_id` at the start of refresh
  - Filter excluded scenes from `corpus` before scoring (using tag data now available in `light_by_id`)
  - Filter excluded performers before scoring
  - After writes, clear `restash_*` fields from any entity newly carrying the exclude tag — mirrors the drop/clear logic already present in `_run_full`

```python
# Before: corpus built with no exclude check
corpus = {sid: c for sid, c in cached_scenes.items() if sid in light_by_id}

# After: exclude tag applied
exclude_id = stash_io.resolve_tag_id(stash, settings.exclude_tag_name)
corpus = {sid: c for sid, c in cached_scenes.items()
          if sid in light_by_id and not _scene_excluded(sid)}
```

author: shortstackengineer
body:
## What

Runs evaluators **sequentially by default**, fixing the root cause behind the batch run's flakiness: evaluators were executed with `Promise.all` (unbounded parallel), so checks sharing external state (several `bin/rails` checks against one SQLite DB) raced and deadlocked into false failures.

## Changes

- **New spec field** `evaluation.concurrency` (default **1** = sequential). Raise it only for genuinely independent checks that are safe in parallel.
- **Engine**: `runEvaluators` now uses an order-preserving `mapWithConcurrency` helper honoring `evaluation.concurrency` (≥ count behaves like full parallel; `1` is fully sequential). Per-evaluator error handling unchanged; threaded through both the baseline and per-iteration calls.
- **Lint**: `SPEC-EVAL-SHARED-RESOURCE` now fires only when `evaluation.concurrency > 1` (the opt-in case), since sequential is the safe default.
- **README**: documents the default and the new field.

## Behavior change

Default evaluator execution goes from parallel → sequential. This is a correctness-over-speed default; independent checks can opt back into parallelism.

## Tests / gates

Test-first (probe-evaluator overlap tests + `mapWithConcurrency` unit tests). Full suite green (201 tests), coverage 95%/89%, mutation 65.6% (≥60).

## Stack

Top of the stack, stacked on `feature/loopgen-lint`. Targets `feature/loopgen-lint`.

author: baladao
body:
## Summary

Replaces the hand-tuned `/mata-mata` bracket with a CSS-grid layout where the L-shape connectors actually meet at the next column's card center. Adds inline per-team scores, a yellow accent on the Final, and a scroll-anchor that automatically lands the user on the next not-yet-played round.

### What changed
- **Layout**: each round is a 16-row CSS grid; cards span 1/2/4/8/16 rows. The connector elbow is positioned from the same row-height variable as the cards, so the L from two siblings always meets the next column's card center exactly.
- **R32 ordering**: cards reordered to match the actual `W2 vs W5` / `W1 vs W3` ... topology from `knockout_matches`, so siblings sit next to each other instead of by `match_number`.
- **Card content**: scores moved inline with team flag/name (no more separate score chip); the empty `"x"` placeholder is hidden when there's no score yet.
- **Typography**: 16px team names, 14px floor everywhere else.
- **Final round** gets a yellow-accented card border.
- **Geometry knobs** (row height, column width, gap, elbow) are CSS variables on the scroll container — one place to tune.

### Mobile UX
- `touch-action: manipulation` so horizontal pan inside the scroller and vertical page scroll coexist.
- Pinch-zoom hint banner instead of "arraste para o lado".

### Scroll anchor
On open, the bracket scrolls so the **first round with any unplayed match** (future kickoff OR no scheduled date yet) is flush with the left edge:
- All R32 dates in the past → opens on **Oitavas**.
- Oitavas done too → opens on **Quartas**.
- ...through Final. Default state (pre-tournament) → R32 stays leftmost.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open `/mata-mata` desktop — bracket renders left-to-right with R32 → Final, connectors meet cleanly, 3º lugar sits below
- [ ] Mobile (375px width) — horizontal drag pans the bracket, vertical drag scrolls the page, pinch-to-zoom works
- [ ] During R32 with at least one future kickoff — opens with R32 on the left
- [ ] Simulate all R32 in the past (mock matches) — opens with Oitavas flush left

author: developery
body:
How it works:
1.
Confidence Threshold:
◦
When a barcode is scanned, the app checks the Open Beauty Facts (OBF) response for completeness.
◦
If OBF has the Brand, Name, AND Ingredients, it considers it a "High Confidence" hit and skips AI entirely (as before).
◦
If OBF has the Brand/Name but is missing Ingredients, the app now identifies this as an "Incomplete Hit."
2.
Enrichment State:
◦
Instead of skipping to success, the app proceeds to the Capture Review screen.
◦
It preserves the verified OBF data as "Enrichment Context."
◦
The UI shows a "Database hit: [Brand] [Name]" badge in the Review screen, giving you visual confirmation that the primary details are already locked in.
3.
Targeted AI Extraction:
◦
When you tap "Finalize," the app sends a specialized prompt to Gemini.
◦
It tells the AI: "We already know this is [Brand] [Name]. Focus your visual analysis on extracting the MISSING ingredients and instructions from these photos."
◦
This significantly increases the AI's accuracy because it no longer has to "guess" the product identity from a potentially blurry logo.
This hybrid approach ensures that every product entry is as complete as possible, combining official manufacturer data with visual evidence from the actual packaging.

author: ericgriffin
body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in toggle to the Sites map that overlays markers for the app's built-in (bundled) dive-site database (~3,250 sites with coordinates) alongside the user's own sites. Built-in markers use a distinct, recessive style so the user's sites stay the focus, and tapping one lets you import it into your library.

- **Toggle** (globe icon) in the map's action row, off by default, in-memory (matches the heat-map toggle convention).
- **Recessive markers**: hollow slate-grey teardrop pins, smaller than your filled circles, clustered in a *separate* layer rendered below your sites so a cluster bubble is never an ambiguous mix.
- **Tap to add**: a built-in pin opens an info card with "Add to my sites", which imports via the existing site-create path; on success the new site appears as your colored marker and the built-in pin is deduped away.
- **Dedup**: built-in sites within 150 m (the matcher's balanced inner radius) of one of your sites are hidden, so each real-world site appears once. Uses a coarse lat/lng grid so it stays near-linear over the full bundled set.
- Wired into **both** map widgets — the full-page `/sites/map` (`SiteMapPage`) and the embedded master-detail pane (`SiteMapContent`).

## Design / plan

- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-28-builtin-sites-on-map-design.md`
- Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-28-builtin-sites-on-map.md`

Built-in selection is held in each map widget's local `State` rather than the shared `mapListSelectionProvider` (which is keyed to your own sites and shared across map sections like dive-centers) — a deliberate, more additive divergence from the spec's typed-selection idea, documented in the plan.

## Testing

- 11 new tests (data accessor, grid-bucketed dedup incl. a grid-vs-naive equivalence check, providers, toggle, marker layer, info card, and integration into both maps).
- Full suite green: **9,428 passing / 0 failing**, whole-project `dart format` and `flutter analyze` clean. Pre-push hooks passed.
- Manual macOS device verification: pending.

author: simonhull
body:
## What

Reverses #913's native **501 stub** with a real, hand-rolled `multipart/form-data` parser, so the Kotlin/Native server runtime serves uploads (backup restore, ABS import, cover upload) at parity with the JVM. Part of the Phase 5 "everything native, full parity with JVM" arc.

## Why a hand-rolled parser

Ktor's CIO **server** can't parse multipart through its `receiveMultipart` transform on native ([KTOR-7361](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/KTOR-7361)). But only that higher-level transform is broken — a de-risking spike confirmed `call.receiveChannel()` (the raw body) round-trips a 200 KB POST body byte-for-byte on a real native CIO server. So the native actual reads the raw channel and decodes the wire format itself.

## How

- The `streamFirstFilePartTo` `expect/actual` seam stays. **JVM keeps Ktor's `receiveMultipart`** (production-proven — untouched). The **native actual** now parses: it pulls `boundary` from the Content-Type header and feeds `receiveChannel()` to the new parser.
- New commonMain `io/MultipartFormData.kt` — `streamFirstFilePart(channel, boundary, limit, …, openSink)`: a buffered hold-back scanner over `ByteReadChannel`. It streams each part through a small fixed buffer (the body never lands in memory), holding back only the last `delimiter.size - 1` bytes per fill so a boundary that straddles two reads is still found. A part is a file part iff its Content-Disposition has `filename=`; the sink is opened lazily, only when the first file part is found (no destination created for a fileless body).
- The dead `MultipartUploadUnsupported` + its `501` status-pages branch are removed. The parser's `MalformedMultipartException` → **400** and `MultipartPartTooLargeException` → **413** replace it (more correct than the old fall-through-to-500 would have been).

## Tests

- **`MultipartFormDataTest`** (commonTest → runs on the JVM Kotest runner, 14 cases): single file part; skips form fields before the file; first-of-many; no-file-part → `false` and the sink is never opened; empty part; **near-boundary body bytes** (`\r\n--BOUNDAR`, `z--BOUNDARY`) not mis-split; size-limit throws; exact-limit accepted; no-boundary throws; and **5 random-body round-trips at tiny buffer capacities (13/17/31/64/257)** to stress the straddling scanner a 64 KiB production buffer never would.
- **`MultipartUploadNativeTest`** (linuxX64Test) flipped from asserting 501 to driving a real `embeddedServer(CIO)` and asserting a 50 KB uploaded file lands on disk byte-for-byte.
- Full gate green: `:sharedLogic:jvmTest`, `:server:jvmTest`, `:server:linuxX64Test`, `spotlessCheck`, `detekt`, `:androidApp:assembleDebug`.

author: franciscotbjr
body:
## Resumo

Adiciona o preset **`rust-design-system`** — um Project Definition pré-preenchido, terso e **toolkit-agnóstico**, para um crate Rust de *design system* nativo. Atende a oportunidade de backlog **O-007** (a segunda dos dois presets destilados da análise do `stand-in` na iteração 018; o primeiro, `rust-gpui-app` / O-006, saiu na iteração 019).

O preset é deliberadamente **distinto dos irmãos**: herda a higiene genérica de crate de `rust-library` e delega a composição de aplicação a `rust-gpui-app`, restando apenas os *deltas* de design system.

## O que muda

```
A  presets/rust-design-system.md                            (novo preset, 226 linhas)
M  presets/README.md                                        (+linha no índice de presets)
M  CHANGELOG.md                                             (+entrada em [Unreleased] > Added)
M  templates/project/project-definition.md                 ("design system" como exemplo de Category)
A  .stateful-spec/history/020-rust-design-system-preset.md  (iteração 020 — tracking)
M  .stateful-spec/memory.md                                 (estado da sessão + fold de Engrama 010)
M  .stateful-spec/history/.archived/memory.md               (Engrama 010 preservado verbatim)
```

**Documentation-only** — nenhum código de aplicação, build tooling ou CI fora de `packages/`.

## Conteúdo do preset (concerns O-007)

Cobre os concerns de design system:

- **Token canon único:** ramp cru → aliases de tema → estados semânticos OKLCH; dark/light compartilham um primary; override de primary em runtime re-deriva do mesmo canon.
- **`Density` / `ColorMode` como enums tipados** dirigindo ~5 variáveis derivadas.
- **Tipografia de duas fontes** embutidas via `include_bytes!`.
- **Ícones-como-shape** em catálogo fechado (enum), não arquivos de asset.
- **Contratos de componente via builder:** `Widget` stateless vs `DsStatefulWidget<State>` + trait auxiliar `DsWidget`; **um arquivo por componente**.
- **Motion centralizado** (tabela única de timings/easings).
- **Theming por um único `apply_theme`** + accessor `tokens()` via contexto.
- **Boundary anti-facade** por clippy `disallowed-methods`, com exatamente **um** escape hatch sancionado (`raw::`).
- **Contraste WCAG + gates de acessibilidade**, com a matemática de contraste **embarcada no crate**.
- **Testes** render-without-panic por componente + geometria diferencial.
- **Empacotamento** `publish = false` com path deps (+ switch documentado para torná-lo publicável).
- **`rust-toolchain.toml`** commitado na raiz.
- **Galeria/storybook** companheira opcional.

Toolkit-agnóstico via placeholders `[e.g., egui | GPUI]` e callouts marcados `> **Toolkit-only:**`.

## Como foi construído

Autoria via workflow multi-agente de 5 fases (Study → 2 drafts → Judge-merge → 5 lentes de revisão adversarial → Revise; 13 agentes). A revisão levantou 22 findings; os 3 *majors* foram corrigidos no passe final:

- entradas de `apply_theme` (o `Theme` carrega `ColorMode` + `Density` + override de primary);
- consistência do escape hatch `raw::` vs a lint `disallowed-methods`;
- testes de render usando contexto headless (sem janela viva).

## Verificação

- Repo documentation-only → o quality gate é revisão manual.
- Preset confere com o template, cobre todos os critérios de aceite da iteração 020, sem leakage de projeto/produto real e sem sobreposição com `rust-library` / `rust-gpui-app`.

## Notas

- Avisos LF→CRLF no commit são benignos (normalização do git no Windows).
- Pequenas edições de tracking pós-commit (hash + Session Log no arquivo da iteração 020) serão incorporadas no commit de fechamento (`/end-session`).

## Checklist

- [x] Critérios de aceite O-007 atendidos
- [x] Índice de presets + CHANGELOG + exemplo de Category atualizados
- [x] Documentation-only (sem código/CI fora de `packages/`)

author: sentry[bot]
body:
This PR addresses an N+1 query performance issue within the `app.tasks.flakes.ProcessFlakesTask`.

**Problem:**
Previously, the task would fetch `ReportSession` objects (uploads) and then, for each upload, execute a separate database query to retrieve its associated `Testrun` objects. This resulted in an N+1 query pattern. Additionally, when flakes reached their expiry condition, individual `flake.save()` calls were made, leading to further unnecessary database operations.

**Solution:**
1.  **Batch-fetching Testruns:** The `Testrun` objects for all relevant `ReportSession`s are now fetched in a single batched query using `upload_id__in`. These are then grouped in memory and passed to `process_single_upload`.
2.  **Bulk-updating Expired Flakes:** Instead of calling `flake.save()` individually, expiring flakes are collected into a list and updated in a single `Flake.objects.bulk_update()` call after processing all uploads.

These changes significantly reduce the number of database queries, improving the performance and efficiency of the `ProcessFlakesTask`.

author: aidanallchin
body:
## Problem

`run_worktrees` was keyed `(run_id, repo_id)` — one worktree per repo per run. Reviewing two PRs in the same repo (multi-PR interactive runs) needs two checkouts on different branches, which that key can't express.

The re-key alone does **not** fix concurrency, and the gap is reachable today: the bare clone is shared across runs (keyed by `owner/repo`), and the PR checkout's bare-local branch ref was named **per-PR, not per-worktree** — `triagefactory/pr-N` for forks, the head branch name itself for own-repo PRs. Git refuses to fetch into (or `worktree add`) a local branch already checked out in another live worktree of the same bare, so a second concurrent run on the same PR fails at materialization. This is hit whenever one PR has two tasks (e.g. `ci_check_failed` + `review_changes_requested`), on re-delegation while a run is still live, and (once bare-cache org-keying lands) across orgs. The per-repo mutex only serializes the two calls; it can't make the semantic conflict go away. It fails loudly (clear error, reservation released, retryable) — not corruption — but it blocks legitimate concurrent work.

Folds in the live half of TFAC-87 (concurrent PR runs).

## Change

Re-key `run_worktrees` to `(run_id, repo_id, ref)` and namespace every PR checkout's bare-local branch by run, with a unified per-run push remote.

- **Schema (A)** — drop the vestigial `feature_branch` column; add `ref` (`@default` / `pr-<N>` / slugified `--ref` branch) as the PK discriminator **and** the worktree path-slug subdirectory. The push gate reads the worktree's live current branch, so `feature_branch` carried no authority. Single forward SQLite migration (`DROP TABLE` + recreate — the table is ephemeral, leaf, CASCADE'd, orphan-swept); PG baseline edited directly (multi-mode is net-new, no release cut). Domain, SQLite/PG stores, conformance suite, and the agenthost IPC seam (`GetRunWorktreeByRepoRef` / `DeleteRunWorktreeByRepoRef`) all re-keyed.

- **Per-run bare-local branch (B)** — `triagefactory/<runID>/pr-<N>` for **fork AND own-repo** PRs (own-repo previously attached the head branch name and collided the same way). The fetch refspecs inherit that uniqueness → no more "refusing to fetch into branch … checked out at …".

- **Unified per-run push remote (C)** — one `tfpush-<runID>-<N>` remote (URL = the fork's for a fork PR, origin's for an own-repo PR) with an explicit push refspec `refs/heads/triagefactory/<runID>/pr-N:refs/heads/<realHead>`, so `git push` (no remote arg) lands on the contributor's fork branch / the upstream head respectively. Per-**run** (not per-PR) so a finishing run reclaims its own remote without yanking it out from under a concurrent same-PR run. Deleted-fork PRs stay read-only.

- **Inline cleanup on both teardown paths (D)** — `CleanupPRConfig` takes the run id and reclaims the per-run branch + remote; folded into both the eager defer and the lazy `workspace add` teardown loops, so the bootstrap sweep is now a pure crash backstop (it reconstructs the per-run remote from the branch marker). No `head_branch` column needed — the unified per-run branch makes cleanup derivable from `(runID, prNumber)`.

- **Materialize + delegate (E/F/G)** — `materializeWorkspace` + the InRoot create funcs land worktrees at `{runRoot}/{owner}/{repo}/{ref-slug}`; the eager GitHub PR path records `ref=pr-<N>`.

- **Multi-PR review anchor (H)** — `add-review-comment` resolves the reviewed PR's worktree HEAD via the `(run, repo, pr-ref)` registry instead of trusting cwd; falls back to cwd HEAD when ambiguous/unresolvable (single-PR runs unchanged).

- `workspace list` surfaces `ref`.

**Out of scope:** per-org bare-cache keying (the stale `SKY-406` TODO in `repoDir`) — B/C fix the collision whether or not the bare is shared, so it's left as a separate ticket.

## Scope / verification

```
go build ./...                 # clean
goimports / go vet ./...       # clean
go test ./internal/worktree/... ./internal/delegate/... \
        ./internal/db/... ./cmd/exec/...   # all green (-count=1)
```

- New TFAC-87 regression tests: `TestCreateForPR_ConcurrentSamePR_OwnRepo` and `…_Fork` — two concurrent runs on the same PR both materialize on distinct run-namespaced branches; each push lands on the right head (own-repo: upstream head; fork: the contributor's fork branch, not upstream).
- Updated worktree bootstrap/checkout tests for the per-run branch/remote names and ref-slug paths; store conformance gains distinct-refs-coexist + delete-by-ref cases.
- SQLite forward migration applies in the migration runner + the test schema bundle; PG baseline RLS test updated to `ref`.
- Postgres-touching changes ran under the pgtest path; local Docker was unavailable so the testcontainer suite skips cleanly here (the PG store compiles and the baseline test exercises the new column).

## Tests

`TestCreateForPR_ConcurrentSamePR_*` are the core acceptance: pre-fix the second `CreateForPR` on the same PR failed; now both succeed on `triagefactory/<runID>/pr-N` branches, and the own-repo case asserts the push refspec targets the upstream head while the fork case asserts the fork branch advances and upstream gains no stray branch.

Resolves [TFAC-502](https://linear.app/sky-ai-eng/issues/TFAC-502)

body:
## Conversion audit — round 21

Multi-agent audit of MSG and PST/OST → EML conversion (12 finder angles → 3-lens adversarial verification to weed out hallucinations). Ten confirmed defects fixed; two findings correctly **refuted** and left alone (PST unreadable-embedded stub and duplicate regular-attachment filenames — both locked by existing tests as intentional).

Every fix is **gated on the source property being present**, so existing vendored fixtures are byte-identical; `./gradlew check` (tests + Checkstyle + Spotless) is green.

### Fixes

| # | Driver | Defect | Fix |
|---|--------|--------|-----|
| 1 | MSG | Body kept CP1252 when only `PR_MESSAGE_CODEPAGE` set (no `PR_INTERNET_CPID`) → mojibake; subject decoded fine; PST had the fallback | Body (plain + binary HTML) falls back to the message codepage |
| 2 | shared | `cid:` rewrite used a LITERAL `replaceAll`, corrupting a sibling whose Content-ID is a prefix of another | Token-aware rewrite reusing the `isContentIdChar` guard |
| 3 | both | Appointment/meeting **reminder** silently dropped | Emit a DISPLAY `VALARM` (`PidLidReminderSet`/`Delta`, 0x5AE980FF→15 min) |
| 4 | both | **Follow-up flag** dropped | `PidLidFlagRequest` → `X-Message-Flag` (gated on `PR_FLAG_STATUS`) |
| 5 | PST | One-off distribution-list member with a name but no address dropped (MSG kept it) | Drop only when name **and** email blank |
| 6 | PST | Embedded `.eml` `name=` not sanitized — `:`/`/` leaked (MSG sanitized) | Run base through `EmlSerializer.sanitizeFilename` |
| 7 | both | **Free/busy status** dropped → every event read as Busy | `PidLidBusyStatus` → `TRANSP` + `X-MICROSOFT-CDO-BUSYSTATUS` |
| 8 | both | Optional (Cc) attendees exported as required | Cc → `ROLE=OPT-PARTICIPANT`; To/ORGANIZER byte-identical |
| 9 | both | **Message expiration** dropped | `PR_EXPIRY_TIME` → `Expiry-Date` (sentinel-filtered) |
| 10 | both | **Voting response** dropped | `PidLidVerbResponse` → `X-MS-Exchange-Vote-Response` |

### Tests
New tests in `ICalendarGeneratorTest`, `EmlSerializerTest`, `MsgToEmlConverterTest`, `PstToEmlConverterTest`, and pst-parser `MessageTest`; `MsgFixtureBuilder` extended to synthesize the new named/regular MAPI properties. Each test fails on the old behavior and passes with the fix. `journal_report_pst_export.eml` sample updated to reflect the sanitized embedded name.

author: matthew-carroll
body:
[Super Editor][Chat] - Workaround for nuanced bottom insets calculation bug in keyboard panel scaffold (Resolves #3070)

In a client app, a KeyboardScaffoldSafeArea ends up running build at a time when localToGlobal() returns an invalid value, because at that moment we're probably in the middle of layout. We previously added some code to avoid completely blowing up when this happens, but a remaining problem is that when the current layout and paint is done, our insets continue to report 0 because build doesn't run again. This results in very wrong bottom insets because they shouldn't be 0 in the client app.

To deal with this we:

 1. When we fail to lookup localToGlobal(), schedule another build so we can update with the correct insets, and
 2. When we fail to lookup localToGlobal(), instead of returning 0, return the previous insets, because those are more likely to be correct.

## MISC
We also accumulated a bunch of `print()` statements at some point along the way. I removed those in this PR. The important part of this PR is only a few lines long.

body:
## Graduate workflows into core; remove the extension system

The workflow builder, run engine, and run monitor lived in a gitignored
`workflows.local` extension wired into the app through generic seams. With the
feature shipping in the open-source app there's no reason to keep it at arm's
length, and the extension system had exactly one tenant — so this rolls
workflows into core and removes the extension machinery entirely.

### Frontend
- New `src/workflows/` feature folder:
  - `builder/` — the Workflows settings builder
  - `run/` — orchestration engine, run monitor, the "Workflow" composer, hooks
  - `storage.ts` / `types` / `workflows.css`
- Mounted directly (no seams):
  - a built-in **Workflows** settings section (after Custom agents)
  - an inline **Workflow** toggle on the new-agent page (shown once ≥1 workflow exists)
  - workflow runs as **sidebar rows** + a **main-pane monitor**, selected via the
    store's `selectedRunId`. Run rows mirror agent rows (with a workflow prefix
    glyph) and can be **stopped** like agents.

### Backend
- `src-tauri/src/workflows.rs` exposes the `workflow_*` Tauri commands
  (definition CRUD, run persistence, git side-effects), registered in `lib.rs`.
- Schema folded into the core migration set as `0012_workflows.sql`.

### Removed
- `src/extensions/` (types/registry/backend)
- `src-tauri/src/extensions.rs` (`ext_invoke` / `Registrar` / `_ext_migrations`)
- the `build.rs` `#[path]` glue and the `extensions/` dir
- the `extensions/*.local/` gitignore rule

The `fork_base` spawn capability stays (already merged separately, #244).

### Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `cargo check` — clean

Not yet runtime-tested: this is a relocation/rewiring refactor, so tsc + cargo
verify the wiring, but the live app (builder render, launching/stopping a run)

author: realcodywburns
body:
## Summary

Greens **staging's entire Tier-1 (testEssential) gate**, which had been red since the #1373 typed-Pekko / Scala-3 modernization merge. The investigation found that of the ~28 red Tier-1 specs, **only one cluster was a real production regression** — #1373 deleted a heal optimization. **Everything else was #1373's mechanical rewrite damaging the *tests*** (stale assertions, a `null`-sender NPE, a fewer-braces parse bug) plus one build.sbt exclusion #1378 inadvertently dropped. Staging's production heal/sync code was sound; the gate was red from test damage. This lands a clean green base for the #1374 (moving-root delta-heal) port.

Each cluster was diagnosed + fixed under the forge/herald protocol and validated independently (forge implementation + `eye` adversarial byte-safety review on the one production change).

## Clusters

**1. B2 — pruned descend-and-stop oracle (PRODUCTION regression). `d67f7d29b`**
#1373 deleted the `prunedStore` val + `pruneIfSubtreeComplete()` method and its three `rebuildFrontierBFS` guards, so the verification walk descended unconditionally and `prunedSubtreeCount` stayed 0 (engagement gauge 0, seeded-prune 0). Also restored `frontierPersistenceEnabled = true` in `CleanRebuildEarlyCompletionSpec`'s fixture (dropped by #1373) so `markComplete()` fires. Re-added the oracle faithfully (Scala-3 syntax). **Byte-for-byte heal-safe**: changes only *descent* (a pure local read + an `AtomicLong` metric), never which nodes are fetched/written; never-false-prune invariant holds. `eye` verified all four safety claims; ETC consensus N/A (SNAP layer). Fixes `PrunedHealVerificationSpec` / `CleanRebuildEarlyCompletionSpec` / `SubtreeCompleteSeedingSpec` (was 6/5 → 11/11).

**2. Heal #1371 seed-guard test contracts (TEST damage). `5a3e9bbe4`**
#1373 mechanically reverted 4 heal specs to their *pre-#1371* assertions, contradicting the MERGED, proven-live #1371 seed-guard (absent walk-root → `HealingRootUnservable` lazy handoff, not seed). Production was correct throughout — **no production change**; restored the #1371 test contracts (drain `HealingRootUnservable`; assert it + `pendingTasks==0` for the absent-root case) and the `ScopedVerificationFallbackSpec` fixture flag. `TrieNodeHealingCoordinatorSpec` + `ScopedVerificationFallbackSpec`: 38/4 → 42/0.

**3. PeerManager RC/reconnect (TEST damage). `b3ae23792`**
#1373 converted Classic `AddMaintainedPeer(uri)` → typed `AddMaintainedPeerCmd(uri, replyTo)` but the test passed `Actor.noSender` (= `null`), NPEing the actor on `replyTo ! …` before it did its work — failing 7 RC-race / reconnect specs. Production correct (`StdNode` passes `deadLetters`); **test-only** — added a `discardReplyRef` probe. `PeerManagerSpec`: → 50/50.

**4. `DisabledTest` exclusion (BUILD config). `623c72224`**
#1378's "SyncTest only" change dropped the `-l DisabledTest` exclusion, re-enabling the lone `DisabledTest`-tagged test (a timing-flaky RegularSync status poll) in the gate. Restored `-l DisabledTest` in `testEssential`/`testStandard` — the tag exists to keep such tests out of the gate.

**5. B1 — MerkleProof "perf" specs (TEST harness bug). `b5f124f60`**
The 8 "complete within N seconds" specs failed not on perf and not on correctness, but on a Scala-3 significant-indentation bug in the test helper `runWithTimeout`: the trailing `None` bound to the outer `try` instead of the catch-case, so the helper **always returned `None`**. The verifier is correct and fast (4096-account verify = 42ms; the `ProofTrieInserter`/`StackTrie` fix is already present — the spec's "architectural fix not applied" comment was a red herring). **Test-only** helper fix. `MerkleProofVerifierPhase3Spec`: 24/8 → 32/0.

## Testing

- Per cluster (forge/herald/eye): all target specs green; HealingFrontierResumeSpec stays 9/9 (no #1378 regression).
- `eye`: `sbt compile-all` clean (all modules); adversarial byte-safety review of the B2 oracle — no critical issues.
- `sbt scalafmtCheckAll; scalafmtSbtCheck` — clean.
- Full `sbt testEssential` (whole Tier-1 gate) — running; result will be posted.

## Notes / follow-ups (pre-existing, out of scope)

- B2's production pruning currently engages only for the state root — `pendingSubtreeRecords` seeding (spec-005 C3b) isn't wired yet (`discoverMissingChildren` never stages candidates). This PR restores the *mechanism* (specs prove it); full engagement is a separate follow-up.
- The 4096-account MerkleProof fixtures take ~17–27s to *build* (immutable MPT), outside the verify deadline — pre-existing fixture cost, not a verifier issue.

## Summary

Fixes #34511.

Child workflow engines inherit the parent `GraphRuntimeState.execution_context`, but the child `Graph.init(...)` call creates node instances before the engine starts running. LLM node construction can load model/provider configuration during that init step, which requires the captured Flask app context.

body:
## Summary

Implements the **Pomodoro Timer** — previously a "coming soon" placeholder under **Productivity → Time** — as a fully working tool. The timer runs timed focus sessions interleaved with short and long breaks, tracks completed sessions, and is fully configurable.

## What's included

**New feature module** (`Features/Pomodoro/`):

- **`Models/PomodoroModels.swift`** — `PomodoroPhase` (focus / short break / long break) and `PomodoroSettings`, the user-tunable settings (durations, rounds-before-long-break, auto-start, sound & haptics) persisted as JSON in `UserDefaults`.
- **`ViewModels/PomodoroTimerViewModel.swift`** — the countdown engine. Time is tracked against a target end-date rather than by decrementing a counter, so backgrounding the app never causes drift. Handles automatic phase advancement, manual skip/select, completed-session tracking, and a sound + haptic alert when a phase ends.
- **`Views/PomodoroView.swift`** — the main screen: a progress-ring countdown, a phase picker, start/pause/reset/skip controls, a round indicator and a completed-sessions stat. Phase tint follows the app's sage/forest green palette.
- **`Views/PomodoroSettingsView.swift`** — a settings sheet with steppers and toggles bound directly to the persisted settings.

**Wiring & localization:**

- Added the `.pomodoro` route to `ToolsCatalog` and `ToolDestinationView`, so the tool now opens from Tools browsing and appears in Home quick access automatically.
- Added English + Khmer translations for all new strings in `LocalizationManager`.

## Notes

- Follows existing conventions: feature-based folders, `@StateObject` view model owned by the view, `AppColor` palette, `LocalizationManager` keys, `TimeFormat.mmss` and the `.logPage` modifier.
- The Xcode project uses file-system-synchronized groups, so the new files are picked up without editing `project.pbxproj`.
- Targets iOS 15+; no iOS 16-only APIs were used.

## Testing

No Swift toolchain is available in this environment, so the changes were verified by code review against the project's conventions and the iOS 15 deployment target rather than by building.

author: a710128
body:
## Summary

Fixes #71.

When `enforce_eager=True`, `BaseModelRunner.__init__` skips `capture_cudagraph()`, so the runner **never** gains a `graphs` attribute. However, `run_model` unconditionally read `self.graphs` **before** the `enforce_eager` short-circuit, so any request carrying an active LoRA context crashed with:

```
AttributeError: 'VoxCPM2Runner' object has no attribute 'graphs'
```

(See the traceback in #71, raised at `model_runner.py` `run_model`.)

## Root cause

- `self.graphs` is assigned only inside `capture_cudagraph()`.
- `capture_cudagraph()` runs only when `not self.enforce_eager`.
- `run_model` computed `has_lora_graph = has_active_lora and bool(self.graphs.get("lora"))` before reaching the `enforce_eager` branch that would otherwise route to the eager `self.model(...)` path.

So `enforce_eager=True` + active LoRA hit the missing attribute on every step.

## Fix

Guard the lookup with `getattr(self, "graphs", {})`. In eager mode this yields `has_lora_graph = False`, which makes the existing `(has_active_lora and not has_lora_graph)` condition route to the eager `self.model(**inputs)` path — exactly the intended behavior when CUDA graphs are disabled. Non-eager behavior is unchanged.

```diff
-        has_lora_graph = has_active_lora and bool(self.graphs.get("lora"))
+        has_lora_graph = has_active_lora and bool(getattr(self, "graphs", {}).get("lora"))
```

## Tests

Added `tests/unit/test_model_runner_enforce_eager_lora.py`, a CPU-only regression test that:

1. Builds a `BaseModelRunner` via `object.__new__` with `enforce_eager=True` and **no** `graphs` attribute (mirroring eager-mode runtime state).
2. Installs an active LoRA context for one decode token.
3. Asserts `run_model` falls back to the eager `self.model(...)` path instead of raising `AttributeError`.

The test fails on `main` with the exact `AttributeError` from #71 and passes with this fix.

```
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_model_runner_enforce_eager_lora.py -q   # passes
uv run pytest tests/unit -q -k "model_runner or lora or runner"        # 74 passed
uv run black --check ...                                                # clean
```

author: ramgopalbhat10
body:
## Summary
- Hoist run-stable, cross-run-repeatable context (slash-skill body, single-file target, profile-handoff continuation note) out of the model-only digest message (the cache-write-never-hit tail) into a new `stable` section of the system prompt, placed after workspace instructions and before the volatile `mcp`/`memory`/`skills`/`profile` sections. This puts that content inside the cached system prefix so it is cache-hit across all steps of a run and across runs when the same skill/workspace is reused, instead of being reprocessed fresh every turn.
- Only the per-turn-volatile digest (session context, workspace context, dropped-history) stays in the model-only assistant message. As a side benefit, the stable text no longer consumes message-byte budget, so more conversation history fits within `maxInputBytes` when a `/skill` is invoked.
- Cap the slash-skill body at 8000 chars (full body still available via `read_skill`).
- Add a `stableContextTokens` field to the context-composition audit and the run-details API/serializer so the trace UI renders a new "Stable run context" row.
- Update base-prompt and single-file-edit profile wording to reflect the new context location.

## Approach notes
- The `system` join filters empty sections, so runs with no stable context produce a byte-identical system prompt to before this change (no cache impact for normal runs).
- `extractWorkspaceContextText` already keys off the `"Model-only context for this run:"` header, which now naturally covers only the smaller volatile digest, so the prompt-cache audit needed no logic change and becomes a more accurate signal for free.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes
- [x] `pnpm lint` passes
- [x] `pnpm build` passes
- [ ] Manual: invoke the same `/skill` in two consecutive turns in one session; confirm `cachedInputTokens > 0` and a stable `systemPromptHash` (modulo the volatile tail) in the run trace / `data-run`.
- [ ] Manual: a `single-file-edit` turn confirms the resolved target path appears in the system prompt's stable section and no longer in the model-only message.
- [ ] Manual: a normal `general-chat` turn with no skill/plan confirms the digest message still carries the session/workspace digest and behavior is unchanged.

## Risk
This relocates existing context (no new model-facing content). The only behavioral change for the model is where the stable context appears (system prompt vs. an assistant message), which is cosmetic to semantics and covered by the wording updates.

author: nwparker
body:
## What

Gate the rich-markdown editor's Table-of-Contents parse on whether the TOC panel is actually open.

## ELI5

Every time you pause while typing in a markdown note, the app quietly rebuilds the whole "table of contents" outline by re-parsing the entire document — **even when the TOC panel is closed and nobody can see it**. The result is thrown away immediately. On a large doc that rebuild is heavy enough to cause a visible typing stutter. This PR only does that work when the panel is open (the default is closed).

## The waste

`RichMarkdownEditor.tsx` ran `buildMarkdownTableOfContents(content)` — a full `unified().use(remarkParse).use(remarkGfm).use(remarkFrontmatter).parse()` over the whole document, plus two recursive walks — in a `useMemo` keyed only on `content`. The serialize path is debounced at 300ms, so this fired ~3×/sec during sustained typing, with cost scaling linearly with document size. The panel defaults to closed (`showTableOfContents = false`), so the result was discarded in the common case.

## Measurement / benchmark

`config/scripts/markdown-toc-parse-benchmark.mjs` mirrors the real remark workload and reports per-content-change cost while typing:

| doc size | headings | per-change median | burst total over ~1 min typing |
|---|---|---|---|
| 44 KiB | 50 | ~14 ms | ~2.9 s |
| 175 KiB | 200 | ~65 ms | ~13.2 s |
| 351 KiB | 400 | ~137 ms | ~27.5 s |

With the fix, every row costs **~0 ms while the panel is closed** — the parse is skipped and a stable empty array is returned.

## The fix

Gate the memo on `showTableOfContents` (via a small testable seam `selectMarkdownTableOfContents`), returning a stable shared `EMPTY_TOC` while closed. `showTableOfContents` is in the deps, so the outline rebuilds the moment the panel opens — no stale TOC.

## Degraded UX

**None while the panel is closed.** When you open the TOC, the parse runs once on open (same render pass that mounts the panel) and then per content change exactly as today.

## Tests

`markdown-toc-visibility-gate.test.ts`: proves the parse is skipped (and a stable empty-array reference returned) while closed, and still builds a real outline when open. Existing TOC tests unchanged and green.

## Verification

Independent adversarial review: **SAFE** — confirmed `tableOfContentsItems`/`flatTableOfContentsItems` have no consumer that isn't gated by `showTableOfContents` (the navigate handler is user-click-only), no stale-TOC window on open, and `EMPTY_TOC` is never mutated.

## Summary Multi-window fix for the dock/taskbar focus bug reported in #195: clicking the dock/taskbar icon brought the **first** window to front instead of the one you were actually using. Also hardens the per-window title differentiator so multiple windows can be told apart. ## Changes - Track windows in a most-recently-focused order (`focusOrder`) instead of a single `lastFocusedWindowId`. The order is seeded when a window is created (new windows get focus) and updated on every `focus` event, so it's never stale. - `showPrimaryWindow()` now restores (if minimized), shows, **and explicitly focuses** the genuinely active window. `show()` alone does not reliably re-raise an already-visible window. When the focus history points at a closed window it falls back to the **most recently opened** window — never the first one (that fallback was the original symptom). - Extracted the title and focus-selection logic into a pure, electron-free module `window-presentation.ts` (`computeWindowTitles`, `pickFocusTarget`) so it can be unit tested. - Title differentiator behavior preserved and covered by tests: `Data Peek`, `Data Peek — mydb`, `Data Peek — mydb — 1/2` for shared connections, and `Data Peek — 1/2` for multiple unconnected windows. - Added `window-presentation.test.ts` (13 cases) covering both the focus-target selection and title generation. ## Related Issues Fixes #195 ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix ## Checklist - [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines (prettier + eslint clean) - [x] I have performed a self-review - [x] I have tested my changes (`pnpm test` → 899 passing incl. new suite; `pnpm typecheck:node` clean) - [ ] I have updated documentation if needed (no user-facing docs affected) ## Notes On Windows/Linux each window already gets its own taskbar button handled natively by the OS; the single-icon macOS dock is the case that routed through `app.on('activate')` → `showPrimaryWindow()`, which this PR fixes.
> Want tembo to make any changes? Add a comment with `@tembo` and i'll get back to work!

- Confirms the current runtime supports one active generic OIDC provider via env.
- Defers platform-owned email/password auth, fake login, and true active multi-provider login.
- Calls out that provider switching requires deliberate identity migration/linking because provider subject IDs differ.
- States future multi-provider support belongs in a separate architecture PR with provider selection, callback disambiguation, and controlled account-linking rules.

author: mfacenet
body:
## Summary

Records the **resource identity model** we settled on: resources are **addressed by their natural key (name)** everywhere a human or machine interacts (UI, `keleustesctl`, the REST contract, `kubectl`), while a **durable ULID** — minted by the engine, **keyed by source path + target cluster**, held in NATS KV and cached in CRD status, and **never written to the customer's Git** — is the background identity that keys audit, cross-CRD references, and history.

It closes a real gap: SKA-322's audit envelope (`action.subject.ulid`) and SKA-324's partition/`audit-index` keying both **depend on** a stable per-resource ULID but neither said where it comes from. This ADR specifies that origin and refines ADR 0003 (identity is derived state, not desired state in Git) and ADR 0005 (the registry lives in the NATS KV tier).

## The rename question (the forcing function)

Kubernetes names are immutable — a "rename" is delete-old + create-new (new `uid`). So any identity not carried *through* the rename is lost, and we ruled out the obvious carrier (the customer's Git). The resolution: key the ULID by **source path + target cluster** (the deployment unit / matrix cell), which a rename doesn't change.

- **Rename only** (same path + cluster) → same ULID → continuous history.
- **Path move / cluster retarget** → new ULID → new identity, **by design** — carrying continuity across a path move is the team's responsibility, documented as a deliberate boundary.
- **Best-effort durability** — NATS KV backed by the event log; a control-plane reset may re-mint (accepted).

## Changes

- `docs/adr/0008-resource-identity-model.md` — the ADR (options A–D incl. `metadata.uid` and Git-write-back, both rejected; rename semantics; consequences with honest negatives).
- `docs/plans/2026-05-jetstream-subject-and-stream-layout.md` (SKA-324) — new **§4.5** "Origin of `subject.ulid`" + the `resource-identity` KV bucket.
- `docs/plans/2026-05-audit-event-schema.md` (SKA-322) — `action.subject.ulid` annotated with its origin; ADR 0008 added to Related.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md` — ADR 0008 row; SKA-322/324 cross-refs; penciled ADR projections bumped to 0009–0014 (0008 now taken).

## Notes

- Docs-only; `reuse lint` passes (186/186). No code paths change yet — implementation tickets (minting + immutability + bucket provisioning) noted as MVP-1 follow-ups in the ADR.
- The UI design spec (PR #26) §2.5 already describes this model; I'll add a `see ADR 0008` pointer there once #26 lands (avoids a cross-branch edit now).

author: cole-zoom
body:
## Summary
Add CKAN `package_id` to `raw.documents` as a permanently NULLABLE best-effort link: ingest now writes the parent dataset UUID on every row, the Terraform schema gains the column, and an idempotent operator-run script walks `package_search` to re-attach any rows whose CKAN parent appears/reappears in the portal.

## Context
The semantic layer is keyed by CKAN package (one row per parent dataset, not per resource), and the catalog only had resource-level identity. Computing the package collapse in BigQuery without a `package_id` column would mean title-clustering forever — strictly worse than a one-time schema migration plus a forward-compat ingest change. The live backfill on open.canada.ca achieved 14,251 / 14,407 loaded-row coverage (98.9%); the 156 residuals are real orphans (CKAN package deleted between ingest and backfill, or harvested from a non-CKAN portal) and informed the decision to keep the column permanently NULLABLE rather than promote it to REQUIRED.

## Implementation

### Step 1 — ingest forward-compat
`DocumentRow.package_id: str` populated from `Dataset.id` on every emitted row (success, quarantine, failed). The CKAN client already parses the top-level `"id"` field; the change threads it through to `DocumentRow` and serialises automatically via the existing `dataclasses.asdict` runlog writer.

On the warehouse-load side, `RawRunlogRow.package_id: str | None = None` accepts the field. `"package_id"` lands in `DOCUMENTS_OWNED_BY_LOADER` and `_row_to_payload`, so the MERGE SQL generator threads it into both the INSERT column list and the UPDATE assignments without any further edit.

### Step 2 — Terraform schema (NULLABLE)
`package_id STRING NULLABLE` between `source_url` and `gcs_uri`. The description documents the column as a best-effort link with explicit NULL semantics: deleted CKAN packages and non-CKAN harvested resources legitimately produce NULLs. In-place schema addition; existing rows get NULL without a rewrite.

### Step 3 — Backfill script
`services/warehouse-load/scripts/backfill_package_id.py` paginates `/package_search?q=*:*&rows=1000` to fetch every dataset on the portal in batches, builds an in-memory `{resource_url: package_id}` map, then joins it against `(SELECT document_id, source_url FROM raw.documents WHERE package_id IS NULL)` and writes the matches back via parameter-bound batched UPDATEs.

Subtleties worth a reviewer's attention:

- **`package_search` vs. `package_show`.** First implementation walked one `package_show` per package. Live run revealed open.canada.ca carries ~47K packages (PRD's 3,693 estimate came from a subject-filtered sample, not the full portal), and the per-package approach would have taken 4+ hours. Switched to `package_search?rows=1000` pagination: same data quality, ~48 calls, ~5 min wall time including the UPDATE batches.
- **Path-only resource URLs are absolutised** against the portal origin (`urljoin`) so they match `raw.documents.source_url` byte-for-byte — same normalisation the ingest CKAN client does. Without this, every datastore-hosted resource would be a miss.
- **First-writer-wins on URL collisions.** CKAN-side URL sharing across packages does happen; the script logs `backfill_url_collision` and keeps the first owner. Empirically several hundred collisions across the portal (Lithoprobe survey files, NRCan tactile-symbol bundles, Census reference pages) — the structured event is the audit trail; operator picks the winner if it matters.
- **Two separate retry policies.** CKAN gets 5 attempts (open.canada.ca returns timeouts under load); BigQuery keeps the warehouse loader's 3-attempt budget.
- **Batched parameter-bound UPDATE pattern.** The script joins against `UNNEST([STRUCT(@d_0 AS document_id, @p_0 AS package_id), ...])` so a 15K-row backfill collapses to ~30 BQ statements instead of 15K. The `t.package_id IS NULL` guard is belt-and-braces against any concurrent writer.
- **Idempotent and self-healing.** `fetch_targets` filters `WHERE package_id IS NULL`, so re-running picks up only the rows still un-linked. A package that gets restored in CKAN after a deletion automatically re-attaches on the next backfill — no manual intervention.
- **Lives under `scripts/`, not `src/`.** Stays out of the import-linter graph and the `mypy --strict` surface of the package proper. The one `src/` surface change it forces is `BqClient.execute_with_params`, a parameter-bound DML variant the warehouse loader will reuse for curated promotions.

### Added
- `services/warehouse-load/scripts/backfill_package_id.py` — paginated CKAN walker + parameter-bound UPDATE writer (~330 lines).
- `services/warehouse-load/tests/integration/test_backfill_package_id.py` — 10 tests covering happy path, misses, idempotency, pagination across pages, URL collisions, dry-run, reset, path-only URL absolutisation, mutex flag rejection, and identifier-injection rejection.
- `BqClient.execute_with_params` on Protocol + `RealBqClient` + `FakeBqClient`.
- 3 ingest-side pipeline tests asserting `package_id` flows through on success, quarantine, and failed paths.
- 2 warehouse-load `RawRunlogRow` tests for the new optional field.
- `requests` (runtime) and `requests-mock` (dev) in `services/warehouse-load/pyproject.toml`.

### Changed
- `services/ingest/src/ingest/types.py` — `DocumentRow.package_id: str`.
- `services/ingest/src/ingest/core/pipeline.py` — `package_id=dataset.id` on both `DocumentRow` construction sites.
- `services/warehouse-load/src/warehouse_load/types.py` — `RawRunlogRow.package_id: str | None = None`.
- `services/warehouse-load/src/warehouse_load/core/documents_merge.py` — `DOCUMENTS_OWNED_BY_LOADER` and `_row_to_payload` carry the new column.
- `infra/terraform/schemas/raw_documents.json` — `package_id STRING NULLABLE` between `source_url` and `gcs_uri`.
- `services/warehouse-load/tests/conftest.py::make_row` — accepts an optional `package_id` parameter so existing tests keep working without modification.

## Key Decisions

1. **`package_id` is permanently NULLABLE.** The live backfill recovered 98.9% of loaded rows; the 156 residuals are real orphans (CKAN package deleted between ingest and the most recent backfill, or harvested from a non-CKAN portal). Fabricating sentinel UUIDs would leak fake datasets into the semantic layer's enumeration and embeddings; deleting orphan rows would discard bytes still held in GCS. Permanent NULLABLE with `WHERE package_id IS NOT NULL` as the downstream filter pattern is the only option that preserves data, surfaces orphans honestly, and self-heals when CKAN restores a deleted package.
2. **`package_id` is a catalog-layer column, not a join key on `raw.rows`.** `raw.rows` stays clustered on `document_id`; the semantic layer joins to it via `raw.documents` as the bridge. Denormalising onto `raw.rows` would save one join at query time but cost a ~280M-row table rewrite now and ongoing per-row write overhead forever.
3. **Walk `package_search` pagination, not per-package `package_show`.** First implementation walked one `package_show` per package and timed out at ~6K of 47K packages after 2+ hours on live data. The PRD's API choice was based on a 3,693-package estimate from a subject-filtered sample, and `package_search?q=*:*&rows=1000` returns the same dataset shape (top-level `id` per dataset, full `resources` array) ~1000-at-a-time. ~48 HTTP calls total vs. 47K. Same data quality.
4. **`RawRunlogRow.package_id` stays Optional.** Historic runlogs lack the key and rows whose CKAN parent has been deleted will continue to produce NULL `package_id` from the ingest path going forward (today they don't — the field is REQUIRED on the ingest side because every CKAN dataset carries a UUID — but Optional in the loader keeps it forward-compat for the non-CKAN sources milestone 4 will add).

## Out of Scope
- `semantic.datasets`, `semantic.columns`, the enrichment service, the retrieval harness — the next PRD's deliverables.
- Promotion to REQUIRED on the BigQuery side

author: samw2k00
body:
## What & why

Makes the workflow AI assistance actually reliable, speeds up branched flows, and surfaces compliance review. Driven by a tight feedback loop fixing real failures (broken graphs from Apply, sequential branches, sandbox errors, unrendered edges).

### AI builder & Improve flow
- **Improve → Apply** now streams suggestion-by-suggestion with a **live progress bar** on the canvas. Each step applies small **edit operations** (not whole-graph rewrites), so large/fragile node configs (HTML/CSS-laden prompts) are preserved byte-for-byte — this was the cause of silent "applied but nothing changed" failures.
- After the steps, a **verify-fix loop (max 3, token-bounded)** physically validates the graph (orphans, dangling edges, `{{token}}` ids that don't exist) and repairs them; the result is reported as verified or flagged.
- Apply now actually implements the **listed suggestions** (previously it re-derived its own).
- The **AI Assist chat builder** validates + auto-fixes its returned graph before it reaches the canvas.
- A strong shared **DATA WIRING CONTRACT** in the prompt: this is *not* n8n — data flows via `{{<nodeId>.field}}` using **real ids from the latest graph**; documents each node's output fields and code-node rules (don't wrap tokens in quotes; sandbox module whitelist).

### Nodes & engine
- New **real-time Web Search node** (keyless provider chain) + optional page-content enrichment.
- `web_search`: **exact equity quotes** via a keyless finance API (handles the Yahoo UA 429 gotcha) + DDG instant answers. LLM node strips outer code fences; `write_file` coerces dict output to readable text.
- **Code node sandbox**: whitelisted stdlib imports (`datetime`, `json`, `re`, `math`, …; `os`/`sys`/`subprocess`/network blocked), with common modules pre-injected.
- **Engine wave scheduler**: independent branches now run **concurrently**; join nodes still wait for all upstreams. (3 parallel 3s waits → 3s total instead of 9s.)
- LLM node gets a hard **1M-token budget** so research loops can't run away.

### Compliance & settings
- **Executions tab**: a compliance review panel (risk level, score vs threshold, rationale, category breakdown) for reviewed AI outputs.
- The workflow AI helpers use the **platform LLM** (same model as the Manager), configured on the System Settings page.
- AI Assist **chat history persists** with the workflow.

### Organisation
- ReactFlow **edges no longer vanish** (seed measured dimensions) — connections render and save.

## Reviewer notes
- The compliance review panel shows the rich scored card only when a Risk & Compliance agent exists; otherwise an "unchecked" card.
- Tracked `.pyc` files changed too (already in repo) — included to keep the tree clean.
- Verified incrementally via live API + browser preview throughout; the AI quality still scales with the configured model, but flows are now validated/auto-repaired rather than silently broken.
