author: dsl2022
body:
## Fix the 4b activation crash — decouple the provisioning `simulate` flag per vertical

**Root cause (confirmed on the live apply).** `eop.provisioning.simulate` gated **both** simulators. Setting it `false` for 4b turned the onboarding real bean on (`GraphProvisioner`, exists) but turned the **access** simulator off — and its real impl (`GroupMembershipProvisioner`) is 5b, which doesn't exist yet. So `AccessProvisioningService` had an unsatisfied dependency → context init failed → task crash-loop. The old `simulate=true` task kept serving (no outage), but real provisioning never activated. **CI was green** because tests run with the `matchIfMissing=true` simulated defaults — `simulate=false` wiring is only exercised on a real deploy.

## Forward-fix (ADR-0018)
- **Split `simulate` per vertical** — `eop.provisioning.onboarding.simulate` / `eop.provisioning.access.simulate`; each simulator/real-provisioner keys on its own flag, so a vertical whose real impl doesn't exist stays simulated (wired) regardless of the other. Schedulers split the same way.
- **Schedulers run in the deployed task regardless** (service env); activation is *only* the per-vertical `simulate` flip — so the access demo path keeps completing (simulated) — no regression.
- **TF:** `provisioning_real` → `onboarding_provisioning_real` (true now) + `access_provisioning_real` (false until 5b); each flips only its `EOP_PROVISIONING_*_SIMULATE`. `dev.tfvars` updated.
- **Regression guard:** `ProvisioningWiringTest` boots the full context in the **exact crashing combo** (onboarding `simulate=false`, access simulated; `WifAssertionService` mocked) and asserts the right beans wire — so CI catches this flag-only deploy-wiring class now, not a live apply.

**60 tests green.** RUNBOOK §9 + ADR-0018 updated.

## To recover the stuck rollout (your gated actions)
Forward-fix, no rollback needed (old task still serving):
1. Merge this PR → `app-deploy` builds the new image (renamed flags).
2. Run the gated **`infra` apply** (env=dev, approve) → new task boots with `ONBOARDING_SIMULATE=false` + both schedulers, access simulated. The crash-looping `:7` is replaced by a clean task.
3. Verify the three 4b live checks (advanced-query `$filter` 200; list under `OwnedBy`; onboard→approve→ACTIVE with a real client ID, no dup on re-provision).

## Summary
Spec for using agents to attack the 15 `not-assessed` conformance rows, with a hard, structural honesty invariant: **an agent run never sets a row to `met`.**

- **Part A — static rows (CAN reach met):** 5 fail-closed gates — `security.no-critical-vulns`, `semantic.commonmark`, `html.validator-clean` (vnu), `integrity.slsa-provenance`, `compatibility.baseline`. Independent PRs; ~12→17/27 with no external party.

- **Part C — guest-room trial-runner (sketch):** run the agent pre-screens/personas in a capability-scoped guest-room so "agents never gate" is enforced by *capability* (no door to the evidence file), not convention.

## Why
Generalizes the COGA honesty discipline to every human-gated row, and lays out the real (gate-backed) path to closing the static rows.

Spec only — `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers inline (lone evidence-schema mapping; unmet-vs-not-assessed on agent-found failures; guest-room door capabilities). No code/gate change.

body:
Closes #2489

## What

Relabel the two GSC aggregate cards in the office-hours `ProjectSignalsPanel`
so they read `top-pages clicks (est.)` and `top-pages impressions (est.)`
instead of `total clicks` / `total impressions`.

## Why

Issue #2489 was a review nit on PR #2464: the `signal-samples` time-series
`gscClicks`/`gscImpressions` scalars were summed from a different GSC source
(`gsc.topQueries`) than the dashboard panel displayed (`gsc.topPages`).

The data-layer half of that divergence was already resolved by sibling issue
#2488 (commit `dfbe5302`, PR #2558), which switched both reducers in
`functions/src/project-signals.ts` to sum `gsc.topPages` and updated the
corresponding tests. The stored sample and the panel now derive from the same
source.

The residual was the panel wording: the two `<Metric>` cards summed only the
top-25 `topPages` rows but were labeled `total clicks` / `total impressions`,
presenting a partial count as a true site-wide total — misleading regardless of
which source feeds it. This PR fixes that label so the cards communicate the
top-pages-estimate nature of the value.

## Changes

- `office-hours/src/components/ProjectSignalsPanel.tsx`: relabel the two
  `topPages` aggregate `<Metric>` cards.
- `office-hours/test/ProjectSignalsPanel.test.tsx`: add a regression assertion
  pinning the new wording (renders `fullSnapshot`, asserts the new label
  strings appear and the old `total clicks`/`total impressions` strings do not).

## Verification

- `npx vitest run --project office-hours --root .` — 441 tests pass.
- `npx tsc --noEmit --project office-hours` — clean.

author: jiazhenz026
body:
## Summary

The desktop Electron process spawns the Python backend (`scistudio gui --bundled`) as a child. When Electron exits **without** sending SIGTERM — force-quit, crash, or the `app.exit()` relaunch paths — POSIX reparents the backend to init (PID 1) and it runs forever as an orphan, accumulating one stray process per launch. The frontend can then reconnect to a stale orphan that never scanned the active project's `blocks/` dir, so freshly authored drop-in blocks fail to appear in the palette.

## Change

- New `scistudio/desktop/parent_watchdog.py`: a POSIX-only daemon-thread watchdog that polls the parent PID and shuts the backend down (graceful SIGTERM, then hard-exit fallback) once orphaned.
- `cli/main.py` `gui` starts it in bundled + POSIX mode only; dev/non-bundled runs are unaffected.

Because it lives in the backend source tree, it ships via the **OTA hot-patch** and stops orphan accumulation on existing installs **without a reinstall**, regardless of how Electron dies.

## Scope boundary

The Electron-side spawn-lifecycle bugs (the `scistudio:relaunch` handler skipping `stopRuntime()` via `app.exit(0)`, and the missing single-instance lock) live in `desktop/main.js`, are **not** OTA-deliverable, and are tracked separately for the next app build.

## Tests

`tests/desktop/test_parent_watchdog.py` — orphan-detection truth table + watchdog fires on parent loss / stays quiet while parent is alive.

Gate record: .workflow/records/1865-guided-1865-backend-orphan-self-reap.json

Closes #1865

author: zhangori000
body:
## Problem

The owner new-order email couldn't tell you how an order was paid. The template only special-cased **Venmo** — every other order, including **pay-at-pickup**, fell into the `else` branch and printed:

> Stripe PaymentIntent: Not recorded

So an unpaid pickup order (money collected at handoff) looked **identical** to a Stripe order whose charge failed to record. At the market stand you can't glance at the email and know whether you still need to collect money.

(Real example: order #2 is `manualPaymentMethod = in_person` / Pay at pickup, but the email just said "Stripe PaymentIntent: Not recorded".)

## Fix

Extract a pure, testable `getOwnerPaymentSummary(order)` helper that mirrors the **same three checkout paths the customer confirmation email already distinguishes** (`sendCustomerOrderConfirmation.ts`), so the two emails stay consistent:

| Order type | Subject | Payment lines |
|---|---|---|
| **Pay at pickup** (`in_person`) | `…new pickup order #N` | `Payment method: Pay at pickup` / `Payment status: UNPAID — collect payment when you hand over the order.` |
| **Card / Stripe** | `…new paid order #N` | `Payment method: Card (paid online via Stripe)` / `Payment status: PAID` / `Stripe PaymentIntent: …` |
| **Venmo** | `…venmo order reported #N` | unchanged (reported by customer, verify before treating as paid) |

The subject line itself now carries the answer ("new pickup order" vs "new paid order"), which is the first thing visible in the inbox.

### Before → After (pay-at-pickup order)
```
- Stripe PaymentIntent: Not recorded
+ Payment method: Pay at pickup
+ Payment status: UNPAID — collect payment when you hand over the order.
```

## Notes

body:
## Summary

Adds two **foundational** Solana agent skills that fill gaps on the community wishlist (`IDEAS.md`). The catalog is rich in protocol integrations but thin on core primitives — these target that gap.

### `token-2022` — SPL Token Extensions
Create and manage Token-2022 mints with extensions: transfer fees, interest-bearing, non-transferable (soulbound), metadata pointer + on-chain token metadata, default account state, permanent delegate, mint close authority, and transfer hooks. Emphasises the critical "init all extensions **before** `initializeMint`" ordering, rent sizing for variable-length metadata, the freeze-authority requirement for default-frozen mints, and always passing `TOKEN_2022_PROGRAM_ID`.

### `priority-fees-and-transaction-building`
Compute budgets & priority fees, CU estimation by simulation (raising the limit first so heavy txs report true `unitsConsumed`), versioned (v0) transactions, address lookup tables, a duplicate-ComputeBudget normalizer (strips limit/price by first-byte discriminator, preserves `requestHeapFrame`), and a reliable send/confirm/retry helper with blockhash-expiry handling.

## Structure
Each skill ships `SKILL.md`, `resources/`, `examples/`, `templates/`, and `docs/troubleshooting.md`, and is registered in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (alphabetical; `node scripts/validate-marketplace.js` passes).

## Testing
- All example/template `.ts` typecheck clean under **strict** TypeScript against `@solana/spl-token` 0.4.14, `@solana/spl-token-metadata` 0.1.6, and `@solana/web3.js` 1.98.4 — every API verified against the installed `.d.ts`.
- Reviewed for agent-followability with Claude Code and cross-reviewed for correctness.
- **Honest caveat:** the examples are type-correct and follow the documented Token-2022 / web3.js patterns, but were **not executed end-to-end against a live cluster** (no funded devnet run). On-chain runtime behavior (exact fee accrual, hook execution, etc.) is not live-verified.

## Checklist
- [x] Follows the template structure
- [x] Instructions are clear and unambiguous
- [x] Examples cover common use cases
- [x] Security best practices followed (authority mutability, permanent-delegate & transfer-hook risks, devnet vs mainnet)

author: cscherban
body:
## What

Adds a compact search input at the top of the facet drawer (the Datadog-style left panel from #64) that filters the displayed facet **values** as you type — case-insensitive substring match, like Datadog's facet panel when a facet has many values.

- Typing narrows which values are shown; facets with no matching values are hidden, and matching facets auto-reveal their values so hits are visible.
- Typing a facet **name** (e.g. `method`) reveals all of that facet's values — keeps it intuitive.
- **Clear button (×)** and **Escape** reset the filter.
- Reuses the main search-bar's input chrome (search icon, focus-within accent border, mono text), sized down for the dense overlay — looks native, small footprint.

## Why

Facets like `route`/`name` can have many values; scanning them is slow. A live filter makes the panel usable at scale, matching the Datadog mental model.

## Display-only — query behavior unchanged

Filtering is purely a display concern over the already-derived facets. A new pure helper `filterFacets(facets, search)` in `utils/facets.ts` returns the narrowed list; the component renders from it. **Unchanged:** query-building, per-value counts, click-to-toggle, OR-merge, the `+N more` value cap, and the persisted open/closed collapse state (search reveals matches via a render-time override, it does not mutate stored state).

## How tested

- **Unit:** `filterFacets` covered in `utils/__tests__/facets.test.ts` (substring/case-insensitivity, name-match keeps all values, drops non-matching facets, empty search is a no-op, no input mutation).
- **Full suite green:** `pnpm build` / `test` / `typecheck` / `lint` all pass.
- **Live (new `pnpm dev` harness):** verified against seeded facets — typing `GET` narrows values to only GET-matching entries across Method/Route/Name; clicking a filtered value still applies the correct `method:GET` token to the search bar; clear button and Escape reset; no-match shows "No facet values match …".

Screenshots (baseline + filtered) captured during verification.

author: wyberai
body:
The "round and round" loop on large apps had a concrete bug: the auto-heal cap ("3 per unique error") was reset on **every files change** — and `tryToFix()` changes files — so the cap never bit and a build that failed for any reason auto-fix couldn't resolve looped forever (`PreviewPanel.tsx:265`).

Fix: a **total** heal budget (3) per user-initiated generation that survives auto-fix's own file writes and only resets on a new user generation. After it's spent, the loop stops and shows the error screen instead of spinning. Pairs with the missing-import stubber (#7), which removes the most common first failure.

Note for re-audit: the prior audit hit **stale edge-cached HTML/JS** (sitemap fix showed as PASS but the same-commit "Six products" showed as FAIL — only possible if static pages were cached stale). Re-audit with a hard refresh after this deploy.

## Summary
Brings the free tier back to parity with the legacy "Bingo Card Generator Pro" (Weebly, one-time purchase), per audit findings. This is a **preview-only** PR — not intended to be merged until owner review.

- **Remove the free-tier card cap (P0)**: the print PDF generator, the share/ZIP export, and the shared print/share count input/stepper now all allow up to 999 cards on every plan (was capped at 10 for free users).
- **Unlock free-space customization for free (P0)**: custom free-space label and Center/Random placement are no longer Pro-locked — old Pro always had this.
- **Accept comma-separated word lists (P1)**: the word-list parser now splits on newlines *or* commas, matching the legacy tool's input format.

## Judgment call to flag (not unilaterally decided)
Legacy Pro was PDF-only and never had digital sharing, so the brief left it open whether the **digital Share/PNG/ZIP export** cap could stay as a Pro perk. Flagging for your decision, not deciding it.

author: thkt
body:
## 概要

ADR-0060 (agent-friendly CLI 設計) の **Phase 1** として、hook専任のformatterに「構造化 degradation signal」と「次の手 (`next_step`)」を適用し、フォーマット失敗をエージェントが機械可読に扱えるようにする。`refs #6`。

本CLIは **hook専任を維持** (CLI表面は新設しない) 方針を前提とする。

## 変更内容

- **report.rs**: `Report` に `degraded` / `next_step` / `notes` を追加。`emit` (中立記録) と `emit_degraded` (劣化時は `FORMATTER_VERBOSE` 無しでも人間可読行として常時可視) の2経路に分離。中立記録は `{file, formatter, action}` の3キー形状を維持
- **oxfmt.rs**: parse失敗・spawn失敗を `emit_degraded` で `next_step` 付き報告 (`fix the reported error...` / `ensure oxfmt is installed...`)
- **eof_newline.rs**: read/write 失敗を `emit_degraded` で報告
- **main.rs**: oxfmt有効かつ整形可能だが未選択 (=バイナリ不在) の場合のみ `skipped` を報告。config で oxfmt を無効化したケースは意図的opt-outとして無報告 (Codexレビュー指摘の修正)
- **README.md**: Structured Output に Degraded outcomes 節を追記

## Design Decisions

- **`emit` / `emit_degraded` の2経路分離**: 可視性 (中立はverbose時のみ / 劣化は常時) と出力モード選択という2つの振る舞い軸が異なるため分離。設計レビューで「深いモジュール」と確認済み
- **`next_step` 定数はドメインモジュール所有**: remediation 文言は oxfmt/eof_newline 各モジュールが所有。DRY違反ではなく知識の所在に従う

## ADR-0060 監査結果 (3分類)

10項目を hook契約への適合性で分類した。

### Group A — hook互換 / 適用候補
| 項目 | 判定 |
| --- | --- |
| 構造化 degradation signal (`degraded`/`notes`) | ✅ Phase 1 適用 |
| エラー JSON に `next_step` | ✅ Phase 1 適用 (`candidates` は非適用) |
| BrokenPipe handling | 🔜 Phase 2 候補 |
| stdin 統一 (`IsTerminal` + `-`) | ⏸ 優先度低 (hookは常にstdin JSON) |

### Group B — CLI表面を前提 / 非適用 (方針決定)
| 項目 | 判定 |
| --- | --- |
| グローバル `--json` + stdout/stderr 分離 | ⛔ 非適用 (serde出力・stderr分離は実装済み) |
| Noun-Verb サブコマンド | ⛔ 非適用 (単一hook) |
| parse-time `conflicts_with` | ⛔ 非適用 (引数パーサ無し) |
| Shorthand expansion + safety rail | ⛔ 非適用 |
| `--dry-run` on mutating ops | ⛔ 非適用 (dry-run相当は既存) |

### Group C — hook契約と矛盾 / N/A
| 項目 | 判定 |
| --- | --- |
| sysexits.h 準拠 exit code | ❌ N/A — hookは exit 0/2/その他のみ区別 ([出典](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md)) |

**`candidates` 非適用理由**: 単一フォーマッタ (oxfmt) のhookには提示すべき離散的代替集合が無く、`next_step` の単一 remediation で十分。

## テスト

- `cargo test`: 73 + 2 + 3 passed
- `cargo clippy --all-targets`: クリーン
- report.rs に8テスト追加 (3キー形状維持・next_step/notes・特殊文字エスケープ・人間可読出力)、main.rs に `skip_next_step` の3テスト追加

## 既知のフォローアップ

- README.ja.md は Structured Output / Dry Run 節を欠く既存の乖離があり、本PRでは英語側のみ更新 (2節まるごとのバックフィルはスコープ外)。別途追従
- 監査結果の issue #6 への反映 (コメント / チェックボックス) は外向き操作のため未実施。本PR body に集約

body:
## What

Stands up `elixir/dialectic_live` — the Phoenix/LiveView **UI-platform beachhead** (one-pane strangler) for the live dialectic surface. A new standalone OTP app alongside the sibling BEAM apps (Bandit `:8790`, `127.0.0.1`, `--no-ecto`; Python keeps the DB).

This is the deliberate platform bet: a standing LiveView UI to evaluate against the buildless JS dashboard, **not** a shortcut to live data — the broadcaster and canonical state stay in Python (`:8767`), and this app is a *consumer* of them (like Sentinel).

## Modules
- **`DialecticLive.Firehose`** — `Mint.WebSocket` consumer of the broadcaster firehose (`/ws/eisv`) re-published onto `Phoenix.PubSub`. Adapted from the Elixir Sentinel's `eisv_web_socket.ex` (reconnect-after-any-failure, no heartbeat). Gated on `GOVERNANCE_START_FIREHOSE` so the app boots even when upstream is down.
- **`DialecticLive.Governance`** — `Req` client for dialectic `list`/`get` over `POST /v1/tools/call`. Bearer token held **server-side**, never sent to the browser (strictly better than the JS dashboard's in-browser authFetch).
- **`DialecticLiveWeb.DialecticLive`** — root pane; subscribes to `dialectic:events`, doorbell→refetch + 10s floor; `awaiting_facilitation` badge + float-to-top.
- **Ops** — `scripts/start.sh` + `scripts/ops/com.unitares.dialectic-live.plist.template` (no `RunAtLoad`; operator-promoted, mirroring wave3a-handlers).

## Strangler status
- **B0** (platform up) + **B1** (pane on existing data): done, boot-verified (200 + pane renders + firehose logged `connected to ws://127.0.0.1:8767/ws/eisv`; 6/6 tests).
- **B2** (true per-turn streaming): blocked upstream — engine emits no `dialectic_*` events yet (#1167 Ask 1). The topic + doorbell are wired and ready.
- The `awaiting_facilitation` badge activates once that field is exposed in `dialectic(list)` (#1220 / migration 053).

## Notes
- Owns no data, no Postgres, no metered-API deps.
- Two UIs run concurrently during the strangler; the buildless dashboard stays live+sole until a pane proves out here.

author: kvfxkaido
body:
## Problem

Branch-on-first-prompt (#1240) was too aggressive: it forked a new work branch off sessions the user had **deliberately started on an existing branch**, not just sessions on `main`.

Two compounding causes:
1. **Uncertainty bias.** The gate did `(currentBranch ?? defaultBranch) === defaultBranch` — an *unknown* current branch was treated as "on the default branch" and branched. A test literally pinned this (`missing currentBranch → true`).
2. **Premature collapse.** Every call site fed `current_branch || default_branch`, so a not-yet-loaded branch was rewritten to the default **before the gate ever saw it**. The gate couldn't tell "actually on main" from "branch metadata hasn't loaded."

Net effect: a session on a feature branch whose branch metadata lagged got force-forked off it.

## Fix

Flip the bias to **positive confirmation** — only branch when the current branch is *known and equal* to the default.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `lib/first-prompt-branch.ts` | Gate requires `currentBranch` defined **and** `=== defaultBranch`. Unknown → don't branch. |
| `sections/WorkspaceSessionScreen.tsx` | Pass the **raw** `current_branch` (dropped `\|\| default_branch`) so "unknown" reaches the gate as `undefined`. Downstream consumers already re-apply `?? defaultBranch`. |
| `hooks/chat-prepare-send.ts` | Placeholder pre-check aligned to the same gate (avoids the empty-spinner desync). |
| tests + decision doc | Flipped the stale assertion; added unknown-branch, non-default-default, and placeholder-stays-immediate cases; documented the on-default-only trigger. |

No protection lost: the commit-time fail-safe still blocks an actual commit landing on the default branch.

## Validation

- `first-prompt-branch.test.ts` + `chat-prepare-send.test.ts` — 30/30
- Full `src/hooks` + `src/sections` suites — 679/679
- `npm run typecheck` — clean

## Follow-up

This narrows *when* the phantom-branch problem occurs but doesn't fully cure it — a legit `main`-start still creates a local-only branch that dies with the sandbox. The durability fix (restore-from-snapshot on sandbox start) ships separately.

body:
## Qué cambia
Suite e2e de humo con **Playwright** que **navega y envía formularios de verdad** (invoca server actions), no solo `build` + `curl`-GET.

Esta semana, el smoke de `build` + GET dejó pasar **tres bugs de invocación de acción** (un re-export de tipos en `"use server"` → `"X is not defined"`; un desajuste de normalización de teléfono): ambos solo se disparaban cuando corría una server action. Esta suite es esa red de seguridad.

- **`e2e/donor.spec.ts` (siempre activo)** — landing (hero + CTA "Ver solicitudes activas"), `/solicitudes` con tarjetas semilladas, y la hoja de detalle interceptada (`role="dialog"` "Detalle de solicitud") al pulsar "Ver detalle". Falla ante cualquier `pageerror` o overlay de error de Next.
- **`e2e/center.spec.ts` (GATED)** — login (teléfono → OTP → Verificar) y registro (Comenzar → datos → OTP), que **invocan las server actions**. Cubre la clase de bug que se nos escapó. Se **salta limpiamente** mientras `TEST_OTP_CODE` esté sin definir.
- **`playwright.config.ts`** — viewport móvil 390px, `webServer` = `pnpm build && pnpm start`.

# Local (donor smoke, siempre activo):
pnpm test:e2e            # build + start + corre la suite a 390px

# Para habilitar el center/auth e2e (gated):

TEST_OTP_CODE=123456 TEST_CENTER_PHONE=4241234567 pnpm test:e2e

Sin `TEST_OTP_CODE`, los tests de center se reportan como *skipped* (no fallan).

- [x] `pnpm lint` verde

Verificar también que existan `TEST_CENTER_PHONE`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `POSTGRES_URL`, `POSTGRES_URL_NON_POOLING`.

author: juanjobarroeta
body:
## Qué resuelve

Estado de resultados y Balanza mostraban "Sin movimientos" porque sólo leen el libro **posteado** (`AccountingEntry`), y postear es manual ("Cerrar mes"). Este PR hace dos cosas: muestra un **preliminar desde CFDIs** cuando el mes no está cerrado, y **auto-postea de forma SEGURA**.

## Hallazgo de seguridad (importante)

`postMonth()` borra **todas** las entradas del periodo excepto `fuente=APERTURA` antes de re-insertar → **borraría los ajustes manuales** (`fuente=MANUAL`) y otras fuentes. Por eso NO se cableó un auto-post crudo. En su lugar:
- `postMonthIfDraft()` sólo actúa en periodos **faltantes o DRAFT** (nunca POSTED/CLOSED), **se rehúsa** si el periodo ya tiene entradas `MANUAL` (devuelve `HAS_MANUAL_ENTRIES`), y salta meses sin CFDIs.
- No se tocó la lógica posteada (math correctitud-crítico intacto). **Follow-up flag:** si se quiere refrescar meses con ajustes manuales, `postMonth` debería borrar sólo `CFDI/NOMINA/BANCO` y preservar `MANUAL`; hasta entonces esos meses quedan en preliminar.

## Cambios

- **Preview (sin escribir libro):** `estadoResultadosPreview()` + `balanzaPreview()` (`posting.ts`) calculan desde `Invoice` STAMPED reusando la clasificación CFDI→cuenta existente; `saldoInicial` sale del libro posteado real. Las rutas devuelven `preliminar: true` cuando el periodo falta/está DRAFT, cifras reales cuando POSTED.
- UI: banner "Preliminar — el mes aún no se ha cerrado. Cálculo directo de tus CFDIs; cierra el mes para generar las pólizas." en ambos paneles.
- **Auto-post conservador:** `postMonthIfDraft()` cableado best-effort (no bloqueante) al final del SAT sync por periodo con CFDIs nuevos; nuevo `POST /api/contabilidad/post-pending` + botón "Cerrar/actualizar meses pendientes" (reporta cuántos se saltaron por tener ajustes manuales).

## Verificación

- `tsc --noEmit` limpio · `next build` correcto · `vitest` 167/167 (4 tests nuevos de preview) · merge limpio con main.

body:
## Overview

Brings the Space Lens flow to feature-parity with the CleanMyMac-style reference design, fixes a few interaction gaps, and makes the intro's scan-location picker real and honored by the scan.

## What changed

### Review sheet (`SpaceLensReviewSheet`)
- Rebuilt "Review files before removal" as a two-column card: the 3D lens hero on the left, left-aligned title + item list + footer on the right (was a centered vertical stack with a `sparkles` symbol).
- Pink rounded (squircle) checkboxes. The reviewed items are snapshotted on appear so unchecking a row keeps it visible (dimmed) and re-checkable, instead of vanishing.
- Footer reads `983K Items selected | 296 GB` with an abbreviated count.

### Review transition (`SpaceLensView`)
- Opening/closing Review now uses the same slide-and-fade as the left-nav section transitions: the explorer slides up and out, then the review window slides up into place (and reverses on close). The explorer is swapped out of the hierarchy so nothing shows behind the window.

### List + bubbles (`SpaceLensListPanel`, `SpaceLensBubbleView`, `DiskScannerViewModel`)
- Left-panel checkbox restyled to the rounded squircle, consistent with the bubble and review-sheet checkboxes.
- New shared `highlightedNodeID` focus state: hovering a row rings its bubble and vice versa, in lockstep. A row click drills into the folder without toggling the removal checkbox (the checkbox is a separate control).
- Protected-item info tooltip now works: a custom dark callout hoisted above the scrolling rows (via a preference key, so it isn't clipped), with context-aware copy ("This is an essential system item…" / home-folder variant).

### Intro (`SectionPresentation`, `SectionIntroView`, `SpaceLensVolumePicker`)
- Updated the Space Lens intro tagline and feature rows to the reference text: **Visual Storage Map**, **Hidden Files Uncovered**, **Large Folders Overview**.
- Added a real scan-location picker (new `SpaceLensVolumePicker`) listing the Mac's mounted volumes plus a **Choose folder…** option. The selection lives on `DiskScannerViewModel.selectedVolumeURL`, which `beginScan()` now uses as the scan root (previously hardcoded to `/`). The footer gauge reports the scanned volume's capacity via the now URL-parameterized `SpaceLensVolumeUsage.current(for:)`.

## Tests
- `test_beginScan_usesSelectedVolumeAsScanRoot` — proves the picker selection drives the scan root.
- `SpaceLensProtectionMessageTests` — protected-item tooltip copy by category.
- Full unit suite green (1,218 tests). App target builds clean.

## Reviewer notes
- The intro feature-row **icons** are my best read of the low-res mock (all valid SF Symbols); easy one-line swaps if you want different glyphs.
- When scanning a **non-boot** volume or an arbitrary folder, `SpaceLensProtection` (defined in absolute boot-volume paths) marks nothing protected, so everything is removable there. Reasonable for external drives, but flagging in case you'd prefer to scope the picker to the boot volume only.
- UI was verified via build + unit tests; the visual transitions and the `NSOpenPanel` folder picker couldn't be screenshotted from the terminal and are worth a quick manual check.

author: mohamedabdelaziem123
body:
This PR resolves an issue where the RETURN_RECEIVED event was being emitted unconditionally during return creation, even when the return was only requested (receive_now was false or omitted). This caused downstream subscribers—such as refund processors and inventory managers—to act prematurely on returns that hadn't physically arrived yet.

To fix this, I refactored the createAndCompleteReturnOrderWorkflow. The parallelize wrapper was removed. Now, RETURN_REQUESTED is emitted sequentially and unconditionally, while the RETURN_RECEIVED event is wrapped in a when() operator so it only executes when input.receive_now === true.

I also added comprehensive integration tests backed by a real local Postgres database to prove the event bus correctly drops the received event when receive_now is false.

Checklist
 I have added a changeset for this PR (patch)
 The changes are covered by relevant tests
 I have verified the code works as intended locally (build, typecheck, lint, and full integration tests)
 I have linked the related issue(s) if applicable
Closes #15851

## Pull Request Description Adds a fully self-contained animated toast notification component with 4 variants (Success, Error, Warning, Info), smooth entrance/exit animations, auto-dismiss with a progress bar, manual close, simultaneous stacking, and light/dark theme support. --- Closes #27987 --- ## Type of Change - [ ] ✨ New animation / hover effect - [x] 🧩 New component - [ ] 📝 Documentation improvement - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix in an existing submission - [ ] Other (describe below) --- ## Submission Checklist - [x] All changes are inside `submissions/examples/toast-notification-mp/` - [x] Includes `demo.html` — self-contained, opens in browser with no server - [x] Includes `style.css` — raw CSS for the proposed feature - [x] Includes `README.md` — what it does, how to use it, why it fits EaseMotion CSS - [x] **No changes to `core/`** - [x] **No changes to `components/`** - [x] One feature per PR (no bundled unrelated changes) --- ## Feature Description **What does this add?** A reusable animated toast notification component with Success, Error, Warning, and Info variants featuring smooth slide-in/out animations, auto-dismiss with a progress bar, manual close, simultaneous stacking, and full light/dark theme support. **How does a developer use it?** ```html

Changes saved

Your profile has been updated successfully.

``` **Why does it fit EaseMotion CSS?** Toast notifications are one of the most repeated UI patterns in modern web apps, yet they are rarely done with intentional motion. This submission treats animation as a first-class concern: a spring-eased slide-in (bottom slide-up on mobile), a height-collapsing exit so remaining toasts reflow without a jump, and an icon micro-animation that gives each variant personality. Every timing and easing value was chosen to feel purposeful rather than decorative, which is exactly EaseMotion's philosophy of making CSS motion human-readable and meaningful. --- ## Demo - [x] Demo added (`demo.html` works by opening directly in a browser) The demo includes a live duration slider (2–10 s auto-dismiss), a dark mode toggle, a "Clear all" button, and all 4 variant triggers — no server or CDN required. --- ## Browser Testing - [x] Chrome - [x] Firefox - [x] Edge - [ ] Safari *(optional but appreciated)* --- ## Notes for Maintainer - All CSS class names use the `-mp` suffix to avoid naming conflicts (e.g. `toast-mp`, `toast-success-mp`, `toast-container-mp`). - The `@keyframes` names also carry the `-mp` suffix (`toast-slide-in-mp`, `toast-slide-out-mp`, `toast-progress-mp`, `toast-icon-pop-mp`) so they won't collide with any existing or future EaseMotion keyframes. - On mobile (≤ 480 px) the container anchors to the bottom of the screen and the entrance/exit animations switch to a vertical slide — feel free to adjust breakpoint. - `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` disables all animations; toasts still appear and dismiss, just with a plain opacity fade. - Dark theme works both via `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` and a manual `.dark-theme` class on any ancestor — whichever you prefer to standardize on is fine. - Happy for you to rename classes to the `ease-*` convention during integration.

author: nicolas-geysse
body:
## Motivation

On **2026-06-29** the Railway `rabbitmq_deposium` service was redeployed **without a volume**, wiping the entire RabbitMQ topology on **prod and staging** (queues/exchanges/bindings). n8n could no longer activate its workflows (`QueueDeclare … 404 NOT-FOUND no queue 'run_0_0'`) and ingestion halted. Recovery required a manual definitions re-import + app restart.

This is consolidation item **C1** from the incident runbook: make a wipe *survivable* by having the broker rebuild its own topology on boot.

## Changes

- **`conf.d/15-definitions.conf`** — `definitions.import_backend = local_filesystem` (+ `skip_if_unchanged`), importing `/etc/rabbitmq/definitions.json` on every boot.
- **`definitions.json`** — baked, **auth-stripped** topology (generated from the live broker, `jq 'del(.users,.permissions,.topic_permissions,.global_parameters)'`). Recreates the 3 exchanges, the 5 quorum `run_*` queues with exact args, **both** `run_1_1` bindings (`runs.cutting` + the incident-critical **`runs.fusion`** that the app's `assertQueues` structurally cannot express), the `deposium.events.n8n` classic bus, `indexation_queue` and the DLQs — **before** n8n/app connect. Import is additive + idempotent, never deletes runtime state.
- **`docker-entrypoint-wrapper.sh`** — now (1) pre-creates a **stable `.erlang.cookie`** to kill a blank-volume race where the node and the seed competed to create it, intermittently crashing prelaunch (`.erlang.cookie: eacces`); and (2) **seeds the login user idempotently** from `$RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_*`. The seed is required because, with import enabled, a **blank node skips default user/vhost creation** (official RabbitMQ behavior) — otherwise a wiped volume would rebuild the topology but have no login user (`ACCESS_REFUSED`). No secret is baked into the image.
- **`.github/workflows/validate-definitions.yml`** — CI guard: valid JSON, **no** auth keys, `/` vhost present, `run_1_1` has both bindings, 5 quorum `run_*` queues, `deposium.events.n8n` classic.
- **`README.md`** — self-provisioning semantics + the `definitions.json` regeneration runbook + queue-arg-immutability caveat.

## Test plan (done locally, Docker)

- **Blank volume × 3** (= the wipe scenario): deterministic boot, full topology (14 queues incl. `runs.fusion`), seeded login works — **3/3**.
- **Warm volume restart**: boots, topology intact, **runtime-created user survives** (import is additive), `skip_if_unchanged` logs *"Hash value of imported definitions matches current contents"* (no churn), login user idempotently re-seeded.
- All CI assertions pass locally.

## ⚠️ Deploy note — do not merge blind

Merging triggers a Railway **rebuild + restart** of the prod/staging broker. A broker restart detaches the Solid app's ingestion consumers, which today do **not** self-re-attach (the F3 failure from the incident → an app restart is required). **Land the app-side consumer self-heal (C3) first, or merge during a maintenance window with an app restart planned.** A persistent `/var/lib/rabbitmq` volume is still required — this makes a wipe survivable, not impossible.

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent duplicate checklist instances being generated for the same template/date/owner by adding explicit occurrence metadata and idempotency checks. 
- Keep historical checklist rows intact while providing canonical recurrence keys for deduplication and querying. 
- Improve checklist UX and visuals and make checklist instance lifecycle updates (archive/delete/progress) more robust. 
- Surface the low-token banner on the Checklists page so users can top up before generation is interrupted.

### Description
- Add occurrence metadata to the data model by introducing `due_date`, `recurrence_key`, and `archived_at` in the DB types and generated migration `20260629120000_checklist_instance_recurrence_idempotency.sql`, including backfill and indexes. 
- Implement idempotent generation and active-instance de-duplication in `useChecklists.ts` by building recurrence keys (including a legacy fallback), checking for existing instances in `generateFromTemplate`, filtering `in_progress` results with `filterActiveChecklistInstances`, and using `useAuth` to derive owner context. 
- Harden cron generation in `supabase/functions/agent-task-runner/index.ts` to compute `recurrence_key`/`due_date`, skip or dedupe existing occurrences (with a legacy key check), and handle concurrent insert uniqueness gracefully. 
- Update UI and behavior: refine `ChecklistInstanceView.tsx` and `Checklists.tsx` styling, update toggle flow so `updateInstanceItem` completes before updating `updateInstance` and logging, set `archived_at` when archiving, add a confirmed delete flow, and show the low-balance `TokenBalanceBanner` on the Checklists page.

- Ran TypeScript typecheck with `tsc --noEmit`, which completed successfully.

author: zuizui0223
body:
## What changed
- Adds `legitimate_contact_fraction`, `expected_legitimate_contacts`, and model-scale `stigma_pollen_deposition` to nectar-guide and scenario outputs.
- Allows design-power checks to use composable route specifications such as `visit + handling` as both the virtual truth and a candidate.
- Adds a synthetic recovery test and runnable example comparing visits-only, visits-plus-contact, and visits-plus-deposition panels.
- Documents the biological meaning and measurement boundary of each new intermediate observable.

## Virtual validation
The regression test declares `visit + handling` as the truth and compares it with `null`, `visit`, and `handling` candidates.

- With an exact visits-only observation, `visit` and `visit + handling` remain compatible, so unique recovery is exactly zero.
- With finite virtual noise at 40 effective units, adding either legitimate-contact fraction or effective stigma-pollen deposition is required to achieve a unique-truth recovery rate above 0.85 in the declared benchmark.

## Boundaries
`stigma_pollen_deposition` is an effective deposition pressure in the model, not automatically a raw pollen-grain count. The normal design-power noise is a planning approximation; field analysis needs a predeclared binomial/contact, pollen-count, and hierarchical observation model matched to the assay.

author: lesyanich
body:
## What

Phase 3.3 of the **Code Cleanup & Security Hardening** epic (MC `c081de36` · `2a8b06a4`).
Audits every service-role holder for unauthenticated reachability. Findings doc only.

## Edge functions (19 active)

Webhook functions are **properly guarded**: `telegram-webhook`/`telegram-ai` (`x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token`),
`loyverse-receipt` (HMAC-SHA256). `verify_jwt:true` functions are platform-gated.

## Findings

- **F1 (MED–HIGH)** — `loyverse-sync`, `parse-receipts`, `update-receipt-job` are `verify_jwt:false`
  + **service-role** with **no inbound auth** (only method/CORS). Callable by anyone with the public
  anon apikey. `parse-receipts` triggers LLM calls → **cost-abuse** vector. Fix: `x-internal-secret`
  header guard (mirror `telegram-ai`) or `verify_jwt:true`.
- **F2 (PROCESS)** — `import-menu-photos`, `menu-photo-sync`, `landing-photo-sync`, `bundle-pos-setup`
  are deployed but have **no source in the repo** (edge-fn drift) → guard unauditable locally. Pull
  via `get_edge_function`, commit, add anti-drift CI.

`/api` service-role is contained (Phase 3.2): only `_lib/apiCostLog.ts`, never on an unauth route.

Full detail: `docs/security/service-role-isolation-audit-2026-06-29.md`.

author: greenheadhq
body:
## Summary

- `/run-da`·`/parallel-audit`가 과거 의사결정(commit/PR/issue, 있으면 CIR/ADR·로컬 세션 로그)을 조회해, 새 세션이 과거에 의도적으로 내린 결정을 근거를 모른 채 되돌리는 회귀(decision regression)를 잡도록 강화한다.
- git으로 버전관리되는 모든 저장소에서 동작한다. CIR/ADR 같은 기록 관습이 없어도 commit/PR/issue 히스토리만으로 점검하며, 보조 소스(CIR/ADR·세션 로그·계획 노트)는 있으면 활용하고 없으면 건너뛴다(graceful degradation).
- 회귀 점검 절차의 단일 진실 원천(SSOT)으로 `decision-regression-audit.md`를 신설하고, run-da·parallel-audit·create-pr이 링크로 참조한다.

## 기존 문제/배경

새 세션의 LLM은 과거 결정의 *도입 근거*를 모른 채 *현재 산출물*만 보고 판단하기 쉽다. 그 결과 과거에 의도적으로 내린 결정(방어 로직, 트레이드오프 선택, 기각한 대안)을 "군살"로 오인해 제거하거나, 이미 고쳐진 문제를 신규 문제로 재등록하는 회귀가 발생한다.

이런 회귀는 git diff나 현재 코드만으로는 드러나지 않는다 — 결정의 근거는 commit/PR/issue 산문과 (있으면) 세션 로그에 집중된다. 실제로 이 저장소에서도 drift 방지 장치를 "불필요한 군살"로 보고 제거하려다 도입 근거 확인으로 차단된 사례, 의도적으로 제거한 동작을 "기존 동작 파괴"로 오인해 복구하려 한 사례(이슈 #908 → PR #909 에서 "반복 관찰"로 기록)가 있었다. 기존 run-da/parallel-audit는 회귀를 점검하면서도 이 과거 의사결정 컨텍스트를 능동적으로 조회하지 않는 빈틈이 있었다.

## CIR (Change Intent Record)

- 발견 경위: 회귀 재도입을 사후에 잡는 것을 넘어, run-da/parallel-audit가 점검 단계에서 과거 의사결정을 능동 조회하도록 탐지 측을 강화하기로 했다.
- 범용성 우선: 이 스킬들은 nixos-config 외 임의의 git 저장소에서도 쓰이므로, 탐지가 CIR/ADR 같은 프로젝트 특수 기록 관습에 의존하지 않도록 설계했다. commit/PR/issue를 필수 소스로, 그 외를 보조 소스로 두는 계층 구조를 채택했다.
- 조사 주체: reviewer/auditor는 read-only sandbox에서 네트워크(`gh`)·홈 디렉토리(세션 로그) 접근이 막힐 수 있어, 메인 에이전트가 "의사결정 컨텍스트 팩"을 1차 수집·주입하고 reviewer/auditor는 git read-only로 보강하는 역할 분담으로 정했다.
- 발동 비용: 모든 호출에 무거운 조사(특히 세션 로그)를 강제하면 비용이 폭증하므로, 제거·단순화·되돌림·리팩터 또는 왕복 핫스팟에만 fail-closed로 강제하고 그 외에는 Review Intensity에 연동하는 게이트(`GATE-REMOVAL-SIMPLIFY`)를 Review Intensity와 독립 축으로 두었다.
- 처리 방식: 사용자가 과거 근거를 *알고도* 의도적으로 바꾸는 경우까지 막으면 마찰이 크므로, Arbiter가 과거 근거를 출처와 함께 제시하고 현재 의도와 충돌할 때만 사용자에게 질문하도록 했다(의도적 변경은 통과, 근거를 모르는 되돌림만 회귀로 본다).
- 중복 회피: 이 저장소의 SSOT 원칙에 따라 절차 본문을 신설 reference 한 곳에 두고 나머지는 링크했다. 발동 룰은 intensity-rules, verdict 매핑은 arbiter-prompt를 각각 정본으로 위임해 경계를 명확히 했다.
- 검토: 이 변경 자체를 강화된 run-da/parallel-audit로 자기검증(도그푸딩)하여, revert 탐지 git 명령의 실행 오류, 신설 SSOT 문서의 자기선언 위반, SKIP 경로의 게이트 우회 등을 발견하고 수정했다.

## ADR (Architecture Decision Record)

| 대안 | 설명 | 장점 | 단점 | 결정 |
|------|------|------|------|------|
| 기록(CIR/ADR) 의존 탐지 | 기록된 결정만 조회 | 구현 단순 | 기록 관습 없는 저장소에서 무력 | ❌ |
| git-universal 계층 | commit/PR/issue 필수 + CIR·세션로그 보조 | 모든 git repo 동작, graceful degradation | forge/세션로그 없으면 일부 신호 누락 | ✅ |
| reviewer 자율 조회 | 각 reviewer가 직접 `gh`/git 조회 | 관점별 탐색 | read-only sandbox에서 네트워크 차단 | ❌ |
| 메인 팩 주입 + reviewer git 보강 | 메인이 네트워크·세션로그, reviewer는 git read-only | sandbox 제약과 정합 | 메인 수집 부하 | ✅ |
| 항상 전체 조사 | 모든 호출에 강제 | 최대 recall | 비용·지연 폭증 | ❌ |
| 제거/단순화 fail-closed + Intensity 연동 | 위험 변경만 강제, 그 외 연동 | recall·비용 균형 | 게이트 분류 필요 | ✅ |
| 회귀 발견 시 무조건 차단 | 되돌림을 모두 차단 | 최대 안전 | 의도적 변경도 매번 마찰 | ❌ |
| 과거 근거 제시 후 사용자 판단 | 충돌 시에만 질문 | 의도적 변경 존중 | 판단 1회 추가 | ✅ |

## 구현 상세

| 파일 | 변경 | 내용 |
|------|------|------|
| `run-da/references/decision-regression-audit.md` | 신설 | SSOT: 4대 탐지 범위, 소스 계층, 조사 주체, Step A~D, 세션 로그 방법론, Non-goals |
| `run-da/SKILL.md` | 수정 | 핵심 invariant + 빠른참조 링크 |
| `run-da/modes/for_plan.md`·`for_pr.md` | 수정 | Step 1에 의사결정 컨텍스트 팩 수집 + SKIP 경로 게이트 예외 |
| `run-da/references/da-domains.md` | 수정 | Regression bundle에 decision regression(의도된 제거의 반대편)·cross-layer 속성 |
| `run-da/references/arbiter-prompt.md` | 수정 | "변경 연관성" 확장 + Decision regression 판정 섹션 |
| `run-da/references/intensity-rules.md`·`intensity-procedure.md` | 수정 | `GATE-REMOVAL-SIMPLIFY` 발동 게이트(Review Intensity와 독립 축) |
| `parallel-audit/SKILL.md` | 수정 | bundle 5 조사 대상 확장 + Step 1b + 속성 보존 점검 |
| `create-pr/SKILL.md`·`pr-template.md` | 수정 | 제거/되돌림 결정의 근거·출처 보존 + 인라인 `# CIR:` 권장 |

revert 신호 탐지 명령(모든 git 저장소 공통):

```bash
git log -i -E --grep='revert|회귀|regress|되돌|롤백' --oneline
```

## 참고 레퍼런스

- Issue #903 — run-da/parallel-audit 전수조사 epic
- Issue #904 — 세션 간 기각/결정 영속성 부재 (본 변경이 탐지 측에서 부분 대응)
- PR #909 / Issue #908 — 의도된 제거를 regression으로 오인 (본 변경의 decision regression 판정이 그 반대편을 보완)
- PR #910 — run-da/parallel-audit 비수렴 안전장치

## Human Test Plan

### 정상 동작
1. 제거·단순화 성격의 변경에서 `/run-da for_pr`를 실행한다.
   - 기대: `GATE-REMOVAL-SIMPLIFY` 발동 → 메인이 의사결정 컨텍스트 팩(commit/PR/issue) 수집 → reviewer/Arbiter 프롬프트에 주입.
   - 실패 시: `intensity-procedure.md` Step 6, `decision-regression-audit.md` 발동 조건 확인.
2. revert 탐지 명령을 직접 실행: `git log -i -E --grep='revert|되돌림' --oneline`.
   - 기대: revert/되돌림 커밋 목록 출력(fatal 없음).
   - 실패 시: `--grep=` 결합과 `-i -E` 분리 형태인지 확인.

### 엣지 케이스 / graceful degradation
3. CIR/ADR·세션 로그가 없는 저장소(또는 forge 미연결)에서 조사를 수행한다.
   - 기대: 보조 소스를 건너뛰고 commit 히스토리만으로 진행, 조사 실패로 처리하지 않음.
4. Review Intensity가 SKIP인데 제거성 변경인 경우.
   - 기대: SKIP이어도 종료 전 메인이 degraded로 의사결정·회귀 조사(Step A·B·D) 수행.
   - 실패 시: `for_plan.md` Step 0 SKIP 분기, `intensity-procedure.md` SKIP 절차 확인.

### Regression (인접 기능)
5. 신규 추가(제거 아님) 변경에서 실행한다.
   - 기대: `GATE-REMOVAL-SIMPLIFY` 미매치 → 기존 Review Intensity(FULL/LITE/SKIP) 흐름 그대로, decision regression 강제 발동 없음.
6. 기존 reviewer bundle / Arbiter / selective consistency 흐름이 변경 전과 동일하게 동작하는지 확인.

body:
## Summary

Adds a public starter workflow for SIGIL/PACA web publishing through GitHub Pages.

This is meant for developer integration and sharing: downstream repositories can adopt the template when they expose one explicit publish surface, either `scripts/pacaweb_build.sh`, `pacaweb/index.html`, or `public/index.html`.

## Added

- `pages/sigil-pacaweb.yml`
- `pages/properties/sigil-pacaweb.properties.json`
- `docs/sigil-pacaweb-integration.md`

## Behavior

The workflow:

- builds `build/pacaweb-deploy` from `scripts/pacaweb_build.sh` when present
- otherwise collects `pacaweb/` or `public/` only when either contains `index.html`
- fails fast with a GitHub Actions error if no explicit PACAWEB source is present
- touches `.nojekyll`
- validates `deploy-manifest.json` with `python -m json.tool` when present
- deploys the artifact with GitHub Pages Actions

## Why

Generic static Pages templates do not encode the SIGIL/PACA deploy contract. This template keeps the public web surface explicit, reusable, and reviewable for other developers without publishing an accidental placeholder.

## Validation

- `pages/properties/sigil-pacaweb.properties.json` parses with `python -m json.tool`
- remote compare against `main`: 3 added files, `behind_by=0`
- fetched the workflow and properties back from the branch after creation

## Notes for reviewers

This PR intentionally does not modify existing starter workflows. The template is not marked `preview`, so reviewers should decide whether it is ready for public starter-workflow visibility or whether a `labels: ["preview"]` follow-up is preferred before merge.

## Was

Bisher zeigte der Verweis-Graph nur **Namen** (Personen) und **Orte**. Dieser PR erweitert ihn auf **Bibelstellen allgemein**: **48 kuratierte zentrale Stellen** erscheinen als eigene Knoten — jeweils mit **Untertitel (Subtext) und Erklärung**.

Beispiele: Schöpfung (Gen 1), Zehn Gebote (Ex 20), Schma (Dtn 6), Psalm 23, Immanuel (Jes 7), Leidender Gottesknecht (Jes 53), Neuer Bund (Jer 31), Bergpredigt (Mt 5–7), Geburt Jesu (Lk 2), Joh 3,16, Pfingsten (Apg 2), Hohelied der Liebe (1 Kor 13), Aus Gnade gerettet (Eph 2), Christushymnus (Phil 2), Neuer Himmel & neue Erde (Offb 21) …

- **Neue Knoten-Art „Stellen"** — clay-farbene **Quadrate**, verbunden mit ihrem Buch. Eigener Filter-Toggle „Stellen".
- **Klick auf eine Stelle** öffnet ein Detail-Panel mit **Titel · Untertitel · Erklärung**, einem **Stellen-Link** (Bible.com) und einer Verknüpfung zum **Buch**.
- Das **Buch-Panel** listet jetzt auch die verknüpften Stellen (zusätzlich zu Orten/Personen).
- Die **Suche** schließt Stellen ein (nach Titel oder Referenz).

## Wie

- Neuer Datensatz `src/data/passages.ts`: pro Stelle `id, ref, book (OSIS), de/en (Titel), subDe/subEn (Untertitel), textDe/textEn (Erklärung)`.
- `GraphView.tsx`: Knoten-Art `passage` (Quadrat-Form, eigene Farbe), Sichtbarkeits-Filter, Such-Einbindung, Klick→Panel.
- Bücher ohne kartierte Orte (z. B. Galater, Philipper, Hebräer) erhalten einen Knoten, sobald eine Stelle auf sie verweist.
- `i18n.ts`: neuer Key `graphPassages` (DE „Stellen" / EN „Passages").

## Erweiterbar

Der Datensatz ist eine bewusste, lehrreiche Auswahl — kein Anspruch auf Vollständigkeit. Weitere Stellen lassen sich mit einem Eintrag (eindeutige `id` + vorhandenes OSIS-Buch) jederzeit ergänzen.

## Test

- `npm run build` (Typecheck + Vite-Build) grün.
- Per Playwright verifiziert: Hinweiszeile zeigt „48 Stellen"; das Buch-Panel listet verknüpfte Stellen (z. B. 4. Mose → „Der aaronitische Segen"); Klick auf eine Stelle (Psalm 22) öffnet das Detail-Panel mit Untertitel „Mein Gott, warum hast du mich verlassen?" und Erklärung — keine Konsolenfehler.

author: silence8013
body:
## Summary

Two related K8s/AgentBox pod configuration gaps for production deployments: there was no way to (1) supply the memory indexer's embedding endpoint, or (2) constrain which nodes AgentBox pods schedule onto. Both are now configurable via the runtime env and surfaced through the Helm chart.

### Problem

In K8s mode the runtime spawns one AgentBox pod per agent, but the pod spec was effectively fixed:

- **Embedding endpoint** — Portal's `config.getSettings` serves only providers, the agentbox only auto-writes `{ providers }` to `settings.json`, and its config volume is an `emptyDir` with no ConfigMap mount. With memory enabled but no embedding config, `getEmbeddingConfig()` returns null and memory silently degrades to FTS-only (no vector recall).
- **Node scheduling** — the pod spec carried no `nodeSelector`, so operators couldn't pin agent pods to a dedicated/labeled node pool (e.g. an SSD or GPU pool); pods landed on whatever node the scheduler picked.

### Solution

- **Embedding** — add infrastructure env overrides (`SICLAW_EMBEDDING_BASE_URL` / `_MODEL` / `_DIMENSIONS` / `_API_KEY`) in `loadConfig()`, forward them from the runtime into every spawned AgentBox via the k8s-spawner allowlist, and expose a `runtime.embedding` block in the chart. `SICLAW_EMBEDDING_API_KEY` stays in the sanitize-env blocklist so it never leaks into child shell processes. An empty embedding key now only inherits the default LLM provider's key when the embedding endpoint is the **same origin** as that provider; a cross-origin self-hosted endpoint stays unauthenticated so the LLM credential is never sent to a different trust domain.
- **nodeSelector** — add an optional `nodeSelector` to `K8sSpawnerConfig`, written onto each pod spec when non-empty. Forwarded via a JSON `SICLAW_AGENTBOX_NODE_SELECTOR` env var (malformed input is warned and ignored, never crashes startup), and exposed as an `agentbox.nodeSelector` Helm block rendered with `toJson`. An empty map omits both the env var and the pod field, so default behaviour is unchanged. This targets **labeled** node pools; pinning to a *tainted* pool (which additionally needs `tolerations`) is out of scope for this PR.

## Test Plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `npm test` (197 files, 3965 passing)
- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `helm template` render with and without each option set
- [x] Embedding verified live in-cluster (9/9 chunks embedded with Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B)

body:
# 🚀 Protocol Module Registry Framework

## 📋 Overview

This PR implements a centralized Protocol Module Registry for the Axionvera Network (Issue #209). 

**Problem Solved**: As the protocol expands with new vaults, reward engines, governance modules, and third-party integrations, relying on hardcoded dependencies creates friction. A decentralized registry improves interoperability, simplifies upgrades, and creates a single source of truth for all active modules.

**Solution**: A secure, admin-controlled Soroban smart contract acting as the protocol's module registry.

## ✨ Features Implemented

### 🔍 Centralized Registry
- **Strict Access Control**: Only the initialized admin can register modules or change their status.
- **State Management**: Prevents duplicate module name or address registrations.
- **Module Discovery**: Exposes views for `get_module_address`, `is_module_active`, and `list_modules` for easy interoperability across contracts.

### 📡 Standardized Event Emission
- Emits standard registry events (`ModuleRegisteredEvent` and `ModuleStatusChangedEvent`) through the central `axionvera-events` crate.
- Introduced `RegistryEventEmitter` in the `interfaces` crate to standardize event publication logic.

## 📁 Files Added/Modified

### New Files
```
contracts/registry/
├── Cargo.toml            # New registry crate definition
├── src/lib.rs            # Registry contract logic
├── src/storage.rs        # Registry data schema and persistent storage access
└── src/test.rs           # Rust unit tests
tests/integration/
└── registry.test.ts      # TypeScript integration tests for the registry
```

### Modified Files
```
contracts/events/src/lib.rs      # Added ACT_MOD_REGISTER, ACT_MOD_STATUS_UPDATE, and payload structs
contracts/interfaces/src/lib.rs  # Added RegistryEventEmitter trait
Cargo.toml                       # Registered contracts/registry in workspace members
```

## 🧪 Testing

- **Rust Unit Tests**: Validated the complete lifecycle of module registration, ensuring non-admins cannot interact and duplicate registrations panic correctly.
- **Integration Tests**: Added the E2E structure for verifying registry state via TypeScript in `registry.test.ts`.

## ✅ Validation Criteria
- [x] Defined registry interface
- [x] Registered protocol modules
- [x] Protected against duplicate registrations
- [x] Supported module discovery
- [x] Emitted registry update events
- [x] Validated registration lifecycle via tests

`closes #209`

author: jfhair
body:
## Problem

Over an iOS `PlatformView` (e.g. a map), any glass surface that resolves to a `LiquidOval` renders a **rectangular blur halo** when `platformViewBackdrop` routes it to the frosted `BackdropFilter` fallback. This includes the **default shape of `GlassButton`/`GlassIconButton`**, the collapsed search trigger and dismiss pill (`tab_bar_searchable_internal.dart`), the bottom-bar collapsed indicator, and the `GlassBottomBarExtraButton` — i.e. the rectangular blur background reported in #79.

Root cause: Flutter's clip forwarding (#177551, 3.41+) only forwards `ClipRRect` clip data to the iOS PlatformView mutator stack — **not** the `ClipPath` that `LiquidOval` (and `LiquidRoundedRectangle`) use. So the descendant `BackdropFilter` is left unclipped over the PlatformView and leaks a square. `_ShapeClip` already special-cased superellipses to `ClipRRect` for exactly this reason; ovals/rects fell through to `ClipPath`.

## Fix

In `_ShapeClip`, when the clipped subtree is over a PlatformView (`platformViewBackdrop`), route any shape with an expressible border radius (`LiquidOval` → circle/stadium via `circular(9999)`, rounded rects, vertical variants) through `ClipRRect` instead of `ClipPath`, reusing the existing `AdaptiveGlass._borderRadiusFromShape`. Visually identical (a full-radius RRect renders the same circle/stadium), but the clip is now forwarded, bounding the frost to the shape.

The swap is gated on `platformViewBackdrop` — off a PlatformView, ovals keep their exact `ClipPath` (true ellipse). `_FrostedFallback` passes the flag through to both its `_ShapeClip` calls (the blur body and the content clip).

## Why central (not per-call-site)

`GlassButton`/`GlassIconButton` **default** to `LiquidOval`, so any consumer passing `platformViewBackdrop` with the default shape leaks — and that can't be fixed from a call site. Fixing `_ShapeClip` once covers every current and future caller.

Follow-up to #128 / #129, and fixes the rectangular-blur on `GlassBottomBarExtraButton` reported in #79.

## Testing

Verified on device (iPhone 16 Pro Max, Flutter 3.41) with a Mapbox `MapWidget` behind a `GlassSearchableBottomBar(platformViewBackdrop: true)`: the collapsed search button's blur now clips cleanly to the circle, matching the (already-superellipse) over-map controls. Off-PlatformView rendering is unchanged.

author: skbs-eng
body:
## Summary

When the Research Logs panel hits its 500-entry DOM cap, the prune now prefers to drop the least-actionable categories first (info → milestone → warning → error) instead of flushing the oldest entries blindly. On long research runs, the panel keeps its most diagnostic entries — warnings and errors — even when the cap is blown by a flood of routine info entries.

## Why

This is part 3 of the 4-PR breakdown in #4897. The previous implementation dropped entries from the head of the DOM in age order, so old warnings and errors were the first to be flushed when the cap was blown — exactly the opposite of what a user navigating back to a stale error would want.

## Changes

A new `pruneToCap(container, cap)` helper in [`logpanel.js`](src/local_deep_research/web/static/js/components/logpanel.js) is shared by both prune paths:

1. **Batch-load path** in `loadLogsForResearch` — replaces the `while (logContent.children.length > MAX_LOG_ENTRIES) logContent.firstElementChild.remove()` loop.
2. **Live-insert path** in `addLogEntryToPanel` — replaces the indexed `entries[i].remove()` loop and the manual `updateLogCounter(-toRemove)` adjustment (now derived from before/after counts).

The helper walks the cap-excess slots in priority order:

1. `info` entries (least diagnostic)
2. `milestone` entries
3. `warning` entries
4. `error` entries (most diagnostic — last to be dropped)

Re-queries the children NodeList each loop so removal doesn't iterate stale entries. Defensive fallback drops the head if none of the four categories match (unreachable in practice).

## Tests

5 new tests under `describe('pruneToCap — per-category ordered prune', ...)`:

- `drops info entries before any other category` — 3 info + 1 warning + 1 error, cap=2 → all 3 info dropped, warning/error survive.
- `drops milestone entries after info is exhausted` — info/milestone/warning/error mix, cap=2 → info, info, milestone dropped in that order.
- `preserves old warnings and errors even when the cap is blown by a flood of info` — 1 early error, 1 early warning, 1000 info, cap=200 → all 802 drops are info entries; the early warning/error survive.
- `falls back to dropping warnings then errors when no info/milestone are left` — 2 warnings + 1 error, cap=1 → both warnings dropped, error survives.
- `is a no-op when already under the cap`.

The helper is exposed as `window.logPanel._pruneToCap` for unit tests. All 744 JS tests pass.

## Related

- Issue: #4897
- Part 1: #4898 (per-category counters)
- Part 2: #4899 (info filter no-op)
- Follow-up: #4901 (skip dedup for non-info)

## What
A `proj:<name>` (alias `dir:<name>`) spawn prefix launches the session in an existing `SPAWN_CWD/<name>` subdirectory — the real checkout, no worktree. Mirrors the `worktree:`/`wt:` prefix.

```
proj:car-ship-prototype <your task>
```

## Why
cwd-keyed tooling pools every plain spawn under the single `SPAWN_CWD`. Example: claude-mem shards memory by directory, so it labels everything one project. `proj:` gives each project its own cwd — without a worktree's throwaway branch (right for isolated builds, wrong for normal interactive work on the real checkout).

## How
Parse `^(?:proj|dir):(\S+)\s+` off the topic, strip it, resolve `resolve(SPAWN_CWD, name)` (error if the dir is missing). Mutually exclusive with `worktree:`; plain spawns are unchanged.

## Assumptions
I assume that the `tsproxy` package name is appropriate as a central package that is independent of `handler` and `server` for shared logic. I also assume that simply wrapping `slog.Error` satisfies the immediate debt, keeping it wired to the central function for later (e.g., Sentry) integration.

## Alternatives Not Chosen
- Adding `ReportError` directly into `cmd/ts-proxyd/` or a handler package to avoid creating a new `tsproxy` package. This was not chosen because a standalone `tsproxy` or `util` package creates a cleaner import graph for cross-package use.

If `ReportError` should belong to another package (e.g., `pkg/utils` or `pkg/telemetry`), simply rename the `pkg/tsproxy` directory and update the imports across the `root.go`, `http.go`, `tcp.go`, and `supervisor.go` files using `gofmt` or `goimports`.

author: srobroek
body:
## Problem

`apm install <bundle>@srobroek-agentic` fails for **every first-party bundle that has transitive deps** (`core`, `data-ai`, `language-typescript`, `debugging`, `frontend`, `review`, `project-lifecycle`, …) with:

```
Invalid APM dependency {'name': '<pkg>'}: Object-style dependency must have a 'git', 'path', or 'registry' field
```

Leaf packages install fine; only bundles with a `dependencies` array break.

## Root cause

`.apm/scripts/build-native-plugins.py` `_bundle_dependencies()` emits each first-party member as a bare `{"name": "<pkg>"}` object. apm's `DependencyReference.parse_from_dict` (apm-cli 0.22.0 **and** 0.23.0) rejects a name-only object — it requires a `git`, `path`, or `registry` source field (a bare `name` is only valid alongside `marketplace:`). So the generated native plugin manifests are unparseable and transitive resolution aborts.

This is the committed generator, run by `apm run build-artifacts` and gated by `check-native-plugins`, so the malformed shape reproduces on every regeneration — hand-editing the plugin.json files would not survive.

## Fix

Emit the object form `{git: srobroek/agentic-packages, path: packages/<name>}` (no `ref`, preserving the original "track whatever version the marketplace provides" behavior). Regenerates all 18 bundle `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` files.

## Verification (end-to-end, real git-backed marketplace)

- `build-native-plugins.py --check` (CI drift gate): **up to date** ✅
- Registered a marketplace from this branch and installed for real:
  - `core` → **EXIT 0**, 32 deps resolved, **lockfile has 0 duplicate identities**
  - `speckit`, `data-ai`, `language-typescript` → **EXIT 0**
- All 18 regenerated plugin.json parse via apm's real code path (0 failures)
- Commit scope is clean: generator + 18 plugin.json only

author: shreeve
body:
## Summary

A TypeScript-style `expr as Type` cast, implemented as **route A**: a minimal grammar production that gives **full narrowing for every expression form**.

- **No type syntax in the grammar.** The type rewriter collapses the `as Type` run into a single in-stream `CAST` marker token whose value is the **opaque type string** (types stay stripped to a string, exactly like all other Rip type code). The grammar reduces a structural postfix node `['cast', expr, typeStr]` — conceptually a marker like `!`/`?.`, not parsed type syntax. `parser.js` is a clean `bun run parser` regeneration (no hand-edits; `test:parser-fresh` passes).
- **Runtime-erased:** the emitted JS is exactly `expr` — zero trace of the cast, for **every** form (identifier, member, call, index, paren, chain).
- **Checker-only:** in the shadow-TS (`inlineTypes`) path it re-materializes as a real `(expr as Type)` assertion.
- **Full narrowing (the route-A win):** because the reduction fires *after* the full postfix expression is built, call results, index results, and parenthesized expressions **now narrow** — closing the old carrier gap.

### Narrowing matrix (all forms narrow now)

| form | example | erases | narrows |
|------|---------|--------|---------|
| identifier | `x as Foo` | ✅ | ✅ |
| member access | `obj.prop as Foo` | ✅ | ✅ |
| call result | `foo() as Foo` | ✅ | ✅ |
| index result | `arr[0] as Foo` | ✅ | ✅ |
| parenthesized | `(x) as Foo` | ✅ | ✅ |
| chained | `x as A as B` | ✅ | ✅ |

### Precedence / associativity (matches TypeScript)

`as` binds **looser** than member/call/index and arithmetic (`a + b as T` ⇒ `(a + b) as T`) but **tighter** than relational/comparison; chains are **left-associative** (`x as A as B` ⇒ `(x as A) as B`). The `CAST` precedence token is slotted between `SHIFT` and `RELATION`.

### Recognition / regression

An `as` is only a cast when it survives lexing as a bare identifier with a left token that can end an expression and a right token that can start a type, not after `.`/`?.`. `for x as iter`, `for x as! iter`, `import x as y`, `export x as y`, and `obj.as` are unaffected (verified by tests).

### ARIA cleanup — all three `any`s removed

With call results now narrowing, all three `@rip-lang/app` `get` helpers (`_ariaPopupDismiss` / `_ariaBindPopover` / `_ariaBindDialog`) drop their `any` return type. The `get(...) as AugmentedEl` call-result cast gives the result a concrete type (`AriaDismissEl` / `AriaPopoverEl` / `AriaDialogEl`, each adding the relevant `__aria*` expando), so closure capture no longer degrades to evolving-`any`. **None remain parked.** Public `AriaApi` unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Runtime erasure for every form (`echo '… as …' | ./bin/rip -c` → no cast trace): identifier, `foo() as Bar`, `obj.p as T`, `arr[i] as T`, `(a+b) as T`, `x as A as B`, `f(x as T)`, `[x as T]`, `x as Map<K,V>`.
- [x] Full narrowing matrix proven meaningful via `test/types/12-cast.{rip,ts}` (clean **with** the cast, `@ts-expect-error` **without**) — identifier, member, call, index, paren carriers, plus parity with hand-written TS.
- [x] Precedence/assoc + erasure codegen in `test/rip/cast.rip`.
- [x] `bun run test:all` green — including `test:parser-fresh` (clean regen) and `test:grammar`.
- [x] `rip check` clean on `@rip-lang/app`; all three ARIA `any`s removed.
- [x] Gallery boots (`bin/rip packages/ui/index.rip`, port 3005 IPv6) — index + `rip.min.js` + `/app` bundle all HTTP 200.
- [x] Tracked bundles rebuilt (`docs/dist/rip*`); docs + AGENTS tables updated (limitation note dropped).

**Held for review — do not merge.**

## Summary

Adds an `assistant_response` middleware seam that lets plugins validate, rewrite, retry, require tool evidence, or block a draft before it is committed to the user.

This is used by the Judgment Integrity plugin to catch unsupported reversals after weak user challenges, including Codex/Headroom Responses-style request payloads.

## What changed

- Add assistant-response middleware result normalization and runtime plumbing.
- Add core loop support for actions: `pass`, `rewrite`, `retry_with_feedback`, `require_tool`, and `block`.
- Add per-turn streaming buffering control so risky drafts are not streamed before validation.
- Route validator-requested tool calls through the existing tool execution path.
- Prevent rejected drafts from being replayed into retry context.
- Sanitize validator-provided replacement/block text before final delivery.
- Document the new middleware seam and observability behavior.

## Verification

- `8 passed` targeted post-review leak/fallback tests
- `105 passed` assistant-response/core focused tests

- deterministic Judgment Integrity heavy smoke: `85/85`

author: atomantic
body:
## Summary

#1770 federated the `musicVideoProject` **record** (metadata + beat-aligned scenes) but shipped an **empty asset manifest** — so a peer that subscribed to just one project received the scenes but none of the referenced media. Unlike the Creative Director store, a music video project has **no auto-linked media collection**, so the per-record manifest is the only channel that can carry those bytes.

This PR builds a real manifest:

- **Uploaded audio** — `uploadedAudioFilename` rides as a `music` entry hashed from `data/music/` (the same dir tracks use). A *track-linked* project stores `uploadedAudioFilename: null`, so its audio federates via the linked track and nothing double-ships.
- **Rendered scene clips** — each scene's `videoHistoryId` resolves through `video-history.json` to its `filename` under `data/videos/` (hashed as a `video` entry). Falls back to the `<id>.mp4` convention (`collectionVideoRefToFilename`) when the metadata row hasn't synced yet; a missing file is skipped so a wrong guess never forces a peer to re-request bytes the sender doesn't have.

Wired into both `buildIntegrityAssetManifest` and the `buildPushPayload` branch. Tombstones still ship `[]`. Entries dedup by `<kind>:<filename>` and are path-traversal-guarded + missing-file-skipped via the shared `hashSimpleAsset`. The push schema (`musicVideoProjectPushSchema`) already accepts `music`/`video` manifest entries through `peerSyncPushBase`, so only its stale comment changed — no schema-version bump needed.

**Deferred:** scene reference-frame images (`scene.referenceImageId`) are intentionally not hashed. The i2v render pipeline that populates them is **Phase 1b (unshipped)** and its reference-image store/dir convention isn't defined yet — federating them follows once that lands.

## Test plan

- `server/services/sharing/peerSync.test.js` — three new cases under `pushRecordToPeer`:
  - bundles uploaded audio (`music`) + both scene clips (`video`, incl. a `.webm`) and ships **no** image entry for the deferred `referenceImageId`;
  - falls back to `<id>.mp4` when a scene clip has no video-history row;
  - ships an empty manifest for a tombstone push.
- Full `peerSync.test.js` passes except the 5 pre-existing `getFullSyncCoverageForPeer` cases (real-Postgres reads, green in CI) — verified identical on the clean base. The 3 `musicVideo/projects.test.js` failures are the worktree's missing PG connection (`Music Video requires PostgreSQL`), also identical on base.

Closes #1772

author: lilan0125
body:
## What Problem This Solves

- When two Control UI deployments share one browser origin but use different base paths, a page with no current scoped settings could fall back to the legacy global settings entry from another base path.
- That stale legacy entry could carry another Gateway's `gatewayUrl`, so the page loaded from `/gateway-b/` could open its WebSocket against `/gateway-a/`.
- The review feedback also identified an upgrade-compatibility gap: intentional same-origin custom endpoints such as `/ws` must not be reset while fixing sibling base-path pollution.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `loadSettings()` now rejects a stale legacy sibling record as a whole when its absolute same-origin path differs from the current page-derived Gateway path.
- Root-relative legacy Gateway URLs and same-origin `/ws` endpoint paths remain migratable, preserving existing custom endpoint setups.
- `persistSettings()` now writes settings under both the Gateway scope and the current page-derived scope, then removes the shared legacy key so new saves do not keep refreshing the cross-base-path pollution source.
- Current scoped settings still take precedence, and legacy global settings remain an upgrade source only when they are compatible with the current page.

## User Impact

- Users opening a second Control UI base path on the same origin connect to the Gateway implied by that page URL, not a stale sibling Gateway URL.
- Existing browser profiles that intentionally saved same-origin `/ws` custom Gateway endpoints keep that endpoint on first load after upgrade.
- New custom Gateway URL saves survive page reload through the page-scoped settings key without relying on the shared legacy key.

## Evidence

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/ui/storage.node.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 1.14s
```

```text
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json ui/src/ui/storage.ts ui/src/ui/storage.node.test.ts
[plugin-sdk boundary dts] fresh; skipping
[plugin-sdk package boundary dts] fresh; skipping
[qa-channel boundary dts] fresh; skipping
[discord boundary dts] fresh; skipping
[slack boundary dts] fresh; skipping
[whatsapp boundary dts] fresh; skipping
[plugin-sdk boundary root shims] fresh; skipping
```

```text
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 ui/src/ui/storage.ts ui/src/ui/storage.node.test.ts
Checking formatting...

All matched files use the correct format.
Finished in 21ms on 2 files using 1 threads.
```

```text
git diff --check
```

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Two same-origin Control UI base paths no longer share stale legacy Gateway URLs, including sibling WebSocket endpoint paths, while root `/ws` custom endpoints are still migrated.
**Environment tested:** Linux, Node with `tsx`, local OpenClaw source checkout on branch `fix/97636-control-ui-basepath-settings`.
**Steps run after the patch:** Called the actual `saveSettings()` and `loadSettings()` functions from source, then started the actual `GatewayBrowserClient` with a WebSocket target recorder to capture the URL it would open for each loaded settings object.
**Evidence after fix:**

```text
two base path WebSocket targets:
  /gateway-a -> wss://example.com/gateway-a
  /gateway-b -> wss://example.com/gateway-b
  shared legacy key present: false
legacy sibling migration for wss://example.com/gateway-a:
  loaded gatewayUrl: wss://example.com/gateway-b
  websocket target: wss://example.com/gateway-b
  sessionKey: main
  shared legacy key present: false
legacy sibling migration for /gateway-a/ws:
  loaded gatewayUrl: wss://example.com/gateway-b
  websocket target: wss://example.com/gateway-b
  sessionKey: main
  shared legacy key present: false
legacy sibling migration for wss://example.com/gateway-a/ws:
  loaded gatewayUrl: wss://example.com/gateway-b
  websocket target: wss://example.com/gateway-b
  sessionKey: main
  shared legacy key present: false
same-origin custom endpoint migration for /ws:
  loaded gatewayUrl: /ws
  websocket target: /ws
  sessionKey: custom-ws-session
  page scoped key present: true
  shared legacy key present: false
same-origin custom endpoint migration for wss://example.com/ws:
  loaded gatewayUrl: wss://example.com/ws
  websocket target: wss://example.com/ws
  sessionKey: custom-ws-session
  page scoped key present: true
  shared legacy key present: false
```

**Observed result:** New saves for `/gateway-a` and `/gateway-b` produce separate WebSocket targets; legacy `/gateway-a`, `/gateway-a/ws`, and `wss://example.com/gateway-a/ws` sibling records loaded on `/gateway-b` resolve to `/gateway-b`; root `/ws` and `wss://example.com/ws` custom endpoints remain unchanged while migrating to the page-scoped key.
**Not tested:** A live Kubernetes or reverse-proxy deployment with two running Gateways was not exercised; the proof records the actual Control UI settings loader and GatewayBrowserClient WebSocket target locally.

## Impact Assessment

- Scope: Control UI browser settings load/persist behavior and storage regression tests.
- Downstream: `connectGateway()` continues to pass `host.settings.gatewayUrl` into `GatewayBrowserClient`; this patch changes which settings object reaches that call for legacy fallback data.
- Edge cases: current scoped settings, page-scoped custom Gateway settings, default scoped settings, legacy same-origin sibling paths, legacy sibling WebSocket endpoint paths, legacy cross-origin custom URLs, legacy root-relative `/ws`, and legacy absolute same-origin `/ws` are covered.
- Hard-coded values: no deployment-specific host or base path is hard-coded; the stale sibling check derives origin and normalized path from the current page and persisted URL. The `/ws` endpoint exception preserves an existing same-origin custom Gateway URL shape used by the UI.
- Existing fixes: related open PRs #97643 and #97665 were checked; this branch keeps legacy migration while adding same-origin custom endpoint coverage requested on this PR.

Closes #97636

author: aabhashrai13
body:
## What & why

The Register form only validated on submit (one snackbar), and the **Login form had no email-format validation at all** — it would happily submit `abc` as an email. This adds live, per-field inline validation to both, following the project's *logic-in-ViewModel / dumb-UI* convention.

## Changes

- **ViewModels own the form values** now (`LoginUiState` / `RegisterUiState` hold the fields), so validation lives in the VM.
- **Live per-field errors** via Material 3 `isError` / `supportingText`. Errors only show once a field is *touched* — a pristine form stays quiet.
- **Submit button gated** on a derived `isFormValid`:
  - Register: name + valid email + password ≥ 6 + matching confirm
  - Login: valid email + non-empty password (no length rule — the server judges the password)
- **Dropped the submit-only validation snackbars.** Snackbars now carry **server** results only (e.g. "Check your email…", auth errors).
- **Shared `isValidEmail()`** (`AuthValidation.kt`) uses a small regex instead of `android.util.Patterns`, so it's unit-testable in plain JUnit. Register was switched onto it too.
- **Tests:** updated `LoginViewModelTest` / `RegisterViewModelTest` to the new API + added validation coverage. All unit tests pass (`testDevDebugUnitTest`).

## Reviewer notes

- **Not a bug:** in the `dev` flavor, `FakeAuthRepository` accepts any email/password by design — real credential rejection only happens on `staging`/`prod`. Use `wrong@test.com` in dev to see the error path.
- `RegisterViewModel`'s email check changed from `Patterns` to the shared regex; behavior is equivalent for real emails (`abc` fails, `a@b.com` passes) and is now locked in by tests.

author: thearnavmenon
body:
## What

Adds **ADR-0030 (status: proposed)** — the plan of record for the program-generation redesign that came out of the multi-hat expert panel.

**Core decision:** make the program a **deterministic, committed artifact** — a repeating queue of day-slots with stable, named exercise identity — driven by the existing per-pattern trainee-model engine. Demote the LLM to exactly two jobs: block-commit exercise selection, and per-set weight (kept, now with a deterministic fallback). Kill the fake 12-week calendar; the per-pattern engine becomes the sole periodization clock.

## Why

The panel verified (against the code) that:
- `phase-advance.ts` cycles **every** user — hypertrophy included — into a strength "peaking" taper (no goal branch). A real bug.
- The macro LLM call is theater: its only consumed output is the training split; `phase`, `volume_landmark`, `periodization_model` are all discarded/overridden.
- The session prompt already tells the model to ignore the global phase → the macro arc is a dead clock.
- A second, dead macro path (`ProgramGenerationService`) is still wired.

## Supersession (on acceptance)
- **amends** ADR-0011 (goal-branch the phase cycle)
- **reaffirms** ADR-0002 (pure-queue model, implemented in full)
- **retires** the 2026-05-12 "Option 4" per-week-LLM memo
- **supersedes in part** ADR-0007 (deterministic per-set fallback, transient class only)
- **may amend** ADR-0005 §"Two-level muscle taxonomy" (conditional — only if leg disaggregation takes the enum-split form)

## Scope of this PR
Documentation only — no product code. Status is **proposed**; flips to accepted when the build is greenlit. The 15 tracer-bullet implementation slices are being tracked as separate issues (dedup against existing #321/#164/#279/#322 pending owner decision).
