author: nadaverell
body:
## Summary

Expanding a resource detail peek used to **navigate away** to the standalone `/workload` route — whatever you were triaging (the resource list, a topology graph, GitOps tree) vanished, and the drawer→fullscreen transition **stuttered** (the fullscreen layout reflowed live inside a still-growing box while collapse hard-snapped).

Now expand **grows the peek into a fullscreen overlay on the same route**, keeping the view underneath mounted, with a smooth GPU-composited morph. You stay in context: browser Back collapses, Forward re-expands, refresh persists the expanded state. `/workload` remains the canonical standalone route for deep-links and non-list surfaces.

## What changed

**Context-retaining overlay (`App`).** Expand sets `?full=1` on the current route (plus `?tab=yaml` when expanding from the drawer's YAML view) instead of pushing `/workload`. The underlying view — resource list, topology graph, GitOps, Applications — stays mounted beneath the overlay. Collapse, back, and close scrub those params in place. Drilling into a related resource while expanded updates `/resources/{kind}?…&full=1`, so browser Back walks resource→resource still expanded. Closing a peek always drops `full`/`tab` so the next peek opens as a side drawer, never a stale fullscreen.

**Smooth morph (`ResourceDetailDrawer`).** A ~260ms frame-morph + content crossfade: both the drawer and fullscreen layouts mount during the transition, each **pinned to its own measured width** so neither reflows or squashes, and the container width animates while their opacity crossfades (transform/opacity only — no per-frame layout). Symmetric expand and collapse; `prefers-reduced-motion` snaps instantly.

**Pre-mount on hover.** Hovering or pressing the expand control pre-mounts the heavy fullscreen layer invisibly (`inert`, `opacity-0`, pinned to full width) so the click reuses it and the morph's first frames aren't competing with the mount cost. The pre-warm is dropped on pointer-leave, close, reduced-motion, and resource change.

**Keyboard + a11y.** `useSuppressBaseShortcuts` drops view-level shortcuts while the overlay covers them (`global` + `drawer`/Escape still resolve); `WorkloadView`'s new `active` prop gates the hidden layer's shortcuts during the morph so it can't capture Escape/`y`/`e`; the backdrop content is `inert` when expanded so it isn't Tab-reachable.

**Mobile.** No side drawer — resource detail is always fullscreen, with a single close affordance (no collapse-to-drawer control).

**URL hygiene (`ResourcesView` + navigators).** List navigators and kind switches drop stale `full`/`tab`, so an expand flag from one peek never leaks onto the next.

## Testing

- `make tsc` ✓ · `make test` (Go + k8s-ui vitest) ✓
- Live-tested on a `kind` cluster, **desktop + mobile (390px)**, on both `/resources` and a **topology** surface (where the peek isn't URL-backed — the harder case):
  - peek → expand → collapse / back / close; the underlying view stays mounted throughout; the fullscreen workload view renders correctly over the graph
  - browser Back collapses, Forward re-expands; refresh persists `?full=1`
  - a fresh peek after an expand→close cycle opens as a **drawer** (no stale-fullscreen carryover), verified on both desktop and the mobile close path
  - hover **pre-mounts** the fullscreen layer (inert, opacity-0, full width) and **cancels on leave**
  - mobile flips to always-fullscreen with a single close control

## Notes

- **Deep-link asymmetry (intentional):** a `?full=1` link reopens fullscreen-over-list; a `/workload` link opens the standalone fullscreen. Both land somewhere sensible.
- Embedded/library consumers that don't wire the expand flow keep the original drawer behavior — the new props are additive.

body:
## What and why

Adds `concurrency` blocks to `image-build.yml` and `gitops-update.yml` to limit race conditions when multiple workflow runs are triggered in quick succession.

Without concurrency guards, two overlapping delivery runs could:
- build and push two images at the same time
- overwrite `values.yaml` in unpredictable order

## Changes

### `image-build.yml`

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: demo-api-image-build-main
  cancel-in-progress: false
```

`cancel-in-progress: false` — we never interrupt a running build/push. Killing a `docker push` mid-flight can leave an incomplete image in GHCR.

### `gitops-update.yml`

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: demo-api-gitops-update-main
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

`cancel-in-progress: true` — if multiple gitops-update runs are queued, only the newest desired state matters. Older queued runs are cancelled.

## Known constraint

With `cancel-in-progress: false`, GitHub can hold at most one pending run per concurrency group. If 3 fast commits arrive, the middle pending run may be replaced by the newer one. This is an accepted limitation for v0.2 — `queue: max` is out of scope.

## PASS criteria

- [x] `image-build.yml` has concurrency group
- [x] `image-build.yml` has `cancel-in-progress: false`
- [x] `gitops-update.yml` has concurrency group
- [x] `gitops-update.yml` has `cancel-in-progress: true`

Closes #15

## What is the purpose of the change

While validating the behaviour of the PTF test harness against the tests defined in `ProcessTableFunctionTestPrograms`, I found that the harness was incorrectly handling instances where, inside a PTF, the user calls `ctx.clearState()` to clear the state.

This caused the harness to write back a `null` value to the underlying state handler, which would then be passed into the PTF and cause a npe within the PTF which expects a non-null state. body:
## Summary

Full-cycle integrity audit of the achievement → reward → Showcase pipeline, **plus the one schema fix it surfaced**.

### Code change
- **`supabase/schema.sql`** — adds the missing `public.user_inventory` table. Both the client optimistic mirror (`js/reward-granting-engine.js`) and the authoritative server grant (`api/verify.js`) write `{ player_id, reward_id, kind }` here, but it had no `CREATE TABLE` — so cloud reward sync silently latched `_invOff` and fell back to the local mirror. New table: PK `(player_id, reward_id)`, `kind check ('skin','trail','music','palette')`, RLS mirroring `cosmetics_inventory` (world-readable, owner-only optimistic INSERT, no client UPDATE/DELETE; `service_role` upserts past RLS). `cosmetics_inventory` remains the authoritative gold store; `user_inventory` is the unified all-kind mirror.

### Audit evidence (`audit-screens/`)
Three Showcase tab screenshots + `handshake-evidence.json` captured via headless Chromium.

## What was audited
- **Registry lockstep** — `verify-achievements.cjs` → `ALL PASS (37 defs · 8 cosmetics · 37 rewards)`. Client `REWARD_MAP` ↔ server map agree on every `id`/`kind`/`src`.
- **Handshake** — `window.debugAchievement(id,100)` for one of each tier (Bronze `high_scorer`→palette, Silver `wave_master`→music, Gold `annihilator`→skin). Local cycle `earned→toast→showcase` ✓ each time.
- **Usability** — Skins / Soundtrack / Grids tabs render with correct owned/equipped/locked + neon-pulse states (see screenshots).

## Verification
- `verify.cjs`, `verify-achievements.cjs`, `verify-fullcycle.cjs`, `verify-size.cjs` → all PASS.
- `verify-supabase.cjs` (live, network-gated) cannot run here: the Supabase host is blocked by this environment's egress policy (`HTTP 403 Host not in allowlist`). It only round-trips the `leaderboard` table and is unaffected by this change; it will exercise the new table once egress is allowed.

## Brief-vs-reality corrections (for context)
File names (`reward-registry.js`/`supabase-api.js` don't exist), achievement count (37, not 11), `pacifist_proto`→`pacifist_protocol`, non-existent `digital_pet`, and tables `music_inventory`/`map_themes` (all rewards route to one `user_inventory` table by `kind`).

body:
## Problem Resolved

Resolves #11056 

## Summary of Changes
Follow-up on the fix #12597, where I missed the issues about BlackBox inputs and AcirVar get:
1. The AcirContext.vars field is frequently accessed using brackets (e.g. self.vars[i]), rather than using the provided .get()method. This can cause unhelpful panics at compilation time in the case that a variable does not exist for whatever reason.

2. The black_box_func_expected_input_size() and black_box_expected_output_size() functions return the number of expected inputs and outputs attached to a blackbox function call. However, these functions are defined in compiler/noirc_evaluator/src/acir/acir_context/generated_acir/mod.rs rather than acvm-repo/acir/src/circuit/black_box_functions.rs where the list of blackbox functions is defined, or acvm-repo/acir/src/circuit/opcodes/black_box_function_call.rs where the call structs are defined. This could lead to issues if the blackbox functions structs are updated without propagating the changes to the expected inputs and outputs.

author: matchmoments-admin
body:
## Context

The `/admin/clone-watch` queue showed **174 "awaiting triage"**. The owner asked "I thought this was automating — what do I still need to action?" Verifying against the prod DB corrected two wrong assumptions from the planning pass:

1. **The 174 pending are the low-signal tail, not auto-confirmable.** 0 have Haiku confidence ≥0.9, **0 have any urlscan classification**, and **155/174 (89%) were already labelled `is_clone = false`** by the pre-classifier. The high-confidence clones are swept separately to `tp_actioned`. So flipping the auto-confirm flag would clear ~0 of the backlog.
2. **Latent bug:** the auto-confirm selection filtered `.is(triage_status, null)`, but the column **defaults to `'pending'`** and **0 rows are ever NULL** — so the confirm path selected nothing even with the flag on. Fixed to `.eq(triage_status, 'pending')`.

## Change

The real lever is the mirror of auto-confirm: **auto-park** the rows Haiku says aren't clones.

- **Conservative cut (operator-approved):** park `is_clone=false` **AND** weak signal (NOT confusable/levenshtein) → `needs_investigation` (reversible, same bucket as the UI "Park" button, no fan-out). **Keep** the `is_clone=false` rows that carry a *strong* brand-similarity signal for human review — that's where Haiku's rare false-negatives concentrate.
- **Safety evidence (recall check):** of 638 confirmed-TP rows, only **6 (~1%)** were `is_clone=false`; the conservative cut keeps the strong-signal ones, so realised FN risk is lower still.
- **Effect:** clears ~98 of the 174 on the next run; leaves ~19 genuine investigate rows.
- **Cost: $0** — reuses the existing `clone_watch_classifications` score + signals; one bulk UPDATE, no LLM/paid calls. Runs in the existing daily `clone-watch-auto-triage` function, before the confirm-path early-return so it works even when nothing is confirmable.

## Doc fixes (verified against code)

- `/admin/clone-watch` UI note claimed a "30-min Netcraft polling cron" — that cron was removed (event-trigger only while Netcraft is dark).
- `background-workers.md`: corrected the poll-netcraft hourly-cron row + timetable; added a `clone-watch-auto-triage` row documenting auto-park + auto-confirm.

**Deliberately NOT changed:** the `feature-flags.md` ON/OFF table. The planning pass flagged it as stale, but the code (`poll-netcraft`) confirms `SUBMIT_NETCRAFT` is genuinely off — so that "correction" needs its own verification against live env values.

## Activation (ops, after merge)

This is gated by **`FF_CLONE_WATCH_AUTO_TRIAGE`** (default OFF). To activate: set it `true` in Vercel, and set `CLONE_WATCH_SHADOW_RECIPIENT` to your email for the validation summary. The function never emits the brand-notify/Netcraft event, so it cannot email a brand. Reversible — flip off and it goes inert; parked rows can be re-triaged.

## Migration

None — code only. Tests: `cloneWatchAutoTriage` 11 green (3 new for the park predicate); web typecheck clean.

author: vampik33
body:
## Problem

PR #209 (2026-06-22) made the Intel macOS leg (`x86_64-apple-darwin`) **opt-in** on the shared `release-binaries.yml` reusable — `include-macos-intel` defaults to `false`. No stable caller passes `true`, so **every stable release since 2026-06-22 stopped shipping its Intel-Mac binary**. Meanwhile the dev lane (`dev-release-binaries.yml`), the RC lane (`release-binaries-rc.yml`), and gtc's bespoke `release.yml` all still build Intel unconditionally — so the stable lane (what end users `binstall`) was the lone outlier.

Effect: Intel-Mac users running `cargo binstall <crate>` (or `gtc install`) get no prebuilt and silently fall back to compiling from source.

## Fix

Flip the reusable default `include-macos-intel: false` → `true`. One change fixes all ~16 stable callers at once (they pin `@main`) and any future binary repo. Cost-sensitive callers can still opt out with `include-macos-intel: false`. Dev/RC are separate reusables — unaffected.

## Audit — stable releases already shipped WITHOUT Intel

| Repo | Affected stable tags | Last good |
|------|----------------------|-----------|
| greentic-setup | v0.5.25 | v0.5.24 |
| greentic-runner | v0.5.22, v0.5.23 | v0.5.21 |
| greentic-mcp | v0.5.3, v0.5.4 | v0.5.2 |
| greentic-dw | v0.5.4 | v0.5.3 |
| greentic-start | v0.5.48 | v0.5.47 |

These five need a re-cut patch release after this merges to restore their Intel binaries. ~11 more binary repos are latent (haven't cut a stable release since the gate; their next one would have dropped Intel).

## Verification
- `yaml.safe_load` parses clean.
- `resolve-matrix` logic unchanged — only the input default flips, so `true` appends the `macos-15-intel` leg exactly as before.

## ⚠️ 意図的に除外: better-auth 1.6.20 → 1.6.22（One-Way Door）
含めていない。1.6.21 の破壊的変更がこのリポジトリを直撃するため別途レビューが必要：

> OAuth sign-up / account-link の profile sync は `input: false` のフィールドへの provider 値を**無視する**ようになった。`mapProfileToUser` で `input: false` フィールドを埋めていたアプリは server 側 provisioning で設定せよ。

本リポジトリは `apps/web/src/lib/better-auth/auth.ts` で `discordId` を `input: false` かつ `mapProfileToUser: (profile) => ({ discordId: profile.id })` で埋めている。アップグレードすると **新規 Discord サインアップで better-auth user の `discordId` が埋まらず**、`enrich-session.ts` が `null` を返して新規ユーザーが全認証アクション不能になる（既存ユーザーは ba_user に保存済みのため無事）。CI は新規 OAuth サインアップを通すテストが無いため緑になる点に注意。

→ 別 PR で `account.create.after` フック等の server 側 provisioning に discordId セットを追加してから取り込む想定。security fix（X-Forwarded-For スプーフによる per-IP rate limit バイパス対策）もそちらで回収する。

Dependabot PR #723 / #724 / #725 はこの PR で代替されるためクローズ。

author: ajnunezg
body:
## Summary
- Pass the `google-github-actions/auth` short-lived `access_token` output explicitly to Firebase CLI through `--token` for Hosting deploys.
- Keep the deploy lane on WIF/OIDC only: no `FIREBASE_TOKEN`, no service-account JSON, no credentialed checkout, no post-auth repo/npm execution.
- Tighten `verify-production-deploy-auth.sh` and its fixtures so future Hosting deploy changes must preserve the ephemeral access-token path.

## Why
`google-github-actions/auth` successfully created WIF credentials for the hosting-only service account, but `firebase-tools` still failed its ADC path with `Failed to authenticate, have you run firebase login?`. Firebase CLI internally treats `--token` as a bearer token fallback when refresh fails, so using the action output preserves short-lived OIDC auth without reintroducing long-lived deploy secrets.

## Validation

This PR seems decently robust now.  Please feel free to kick the tires on it.  There are updates for the following:

IRC:

- `RelayMsgSep`, a non-configurable bridge setting, which will be automatically detected and set when `UseRelayMsg` is true for that bridge.  This consists of one or more characters, at least one of which is mandatory to be included in a relayed nick.

- When a separator is missing from the `RemoteNickFormat` for an IRC bridge that has `UseRelayMsg` set, matterbridge will now attempt to insert one in the relayed nick.  If no `RelayMsgSep` has been automatically configured yet, it attempts to send the message using a "/" character, which is the default for Ergo.

- `Casemapping`, a non-configurable bridge setting, which will be automatically detected and set for each connected IRC server.  The setting only comes into play when `UseRelayMsg` is true for that bridge.  This will try to enforce compliance with what the server will allow in a relayed nick.  Currently supported options for Ergo include "ascii", "rfc1459", "rfc1459-strict", "precis" (rfc8265), and "permissive".  The last option will permit unicode in a relayed nick.

- RWMutexes have been added to protect the `channels` and `names` maps in the `Birc` struct.  As the IRC bridge is becoming increasingly asynchronous, concurrency issues may arise.  Maps in golang are not concurrency safe; reading and writing to them at the same time causes a panic.

- Two new config settings `UseRelayFallback` and `RelayFallbackNick` have been added, which default to `true` and "unknown".  They only come into play when `UseRelayMsg` is active.  When these are used, if `sanitizeNick` completely erases a relayed nick, then the nick will instead be replaced by the `RelayFallbackNick`.  Note that this could potentially allow for anonymized messages to be sent to an IRC bridge.

- When `UseRelayMsg` is set, `sanitizeNick` will try to replace all disallowed characters with dashes.  To prevent someone from impersonating an IRC user who has a dash in their nick, the gateway will now check whether there is a separator character in the `RemoteNickFormat` after it has been partly processed for the receiving bridge, but without allowing any untrusted input sources (e.g. the `{NICK}` or `{USERID}` fields) to be taken into account.

General features:

- `SanitizeNick` has been added as a Bridge function which all bridges may include, though irc is the only protocol which has an example of this so far.  It can be implemented for any bridge that has restrictions on valid puppeted nicks.  To add this to another bridge, create a `SanitizeNick` function in the bridge package, edit the files in `gateway/bridgemap` appropriately, and add it to the `modifyUsername` function in `gateway/gateway.go`.

- `SetString`, `SetInt`, `SetBool`, etc., functions have been added to `bridge/bridge.go`, which call a `SetVal` function in `bridge/config/config.go`.  These can be called by any bridge (or the gateway!) to set override values for bridge settings.  They are currently only used for some IRC settings that are autodetected when running.  `SetVal` can be called with "general." prepended to the key, if there is a need to set something in the `[general]` section.  These override values do not persist upon restarting.

- Because Viper is not concurrency-safe, and all of the `GetString`, `GetBool` etc. functions in `bridge/config/config.go` had been using deferred RUnlock calls, each of these functions has been rewritten to instead defer a panic recovery function.  That is because the new `SetVal` function will be the first time any write lock has been used with the config settings.  With deferred RUnlocks everywhere, matterbridge might otherwise behave as a single-threaded application whenever `SetVal` was called, due to the numerous configuration checks called from every bridge.  RLock allows for multiple concurrent reads, but only one writer at a time.  RLock will block when there is a Lock (or a pending Lock), and Lock will block until there are zero RLocks on a particular mutex.

- JOIN_LEAVE events have been separated into JOIN and LEAVE events for various protocols.  This should address #67.  Authorship for those commits has been preserved as requested in #103.  Thanks, @funderscore1 and @josephcrowell!

author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/candid-bombolone-f473b5/agent-runs/6a4247c76b6a1a2955b73bbc

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** Failed to load module script: Expected a JavaScript-or-Wasm module script but the server responded with a MIME type of "application/octet-stream". Strict MIME type checking is enforced for module scripts per HTML spec.
/favicon.svg:1  Failed to load ...

✅ **Result:** Two browser errors were reported on the deployed site:

1. **Module script MIME type rejection** — The browser refused to load a JavaScript module script because the server returned `application/octet-stream` instead of `text/javascript`.
2. **favicon.svg 404** — The site favicon was not found at `/favicon.svg`.

Both errors were caused by the same root issue: the project had no `netlify.toml` configuration file. Without it, Netlify had no instruction to run the Vite build step (`vite build`) before deploying, so raw source files (including `.jsx` files) were being served directly from the repository instead of the compiled `dist/` output. Browsers enforce strict MIME type checking for ES module scripts, so a `.jsx` file served as `application/octet-stream` is rejected outright. The `favicon.svg` 404 occurred for the same reason — without a proper build and publish directory configured, the static assets from the `public/` folder were not being served at their expected paths.

A `netlify.toml` was added that:
- Sets the build command to `vite build`
- Points the publish directory to `dist` (Vite's output folder)
- Adds explicit `Content-Type` headers for `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, and `.svg` files as a safeguard against any future MIME type mismatches

With this configuration in place, Netlify will compile the Vite/React project before publishing and serve the correctly built static assets, resolving both errors.

author: copilot
body:
This PR aligns `subscription_service.py` with the private module-level `type` alias pattern already used in `product_service.py`, reducing repeated literal unions while preserving identical behavior and externally observable types. The refactor is annotation-only: no runtime logic, error strings, or success/failure tuple semantics are changed.

- **Module-level private alias block (alphabetized)**
  - Added:
    - `_AwaitableDeleteOrReadSubscriptionResult`
    - `_ProductNotSubscribableLiteral`
    - `_SubscriptionDoesNotExistLiteral`
    - `_UserDoesNotExistLiteral`
  - Kept existing `_ProductStatusLiteral` and moved it into the same ordered alias block.
  - Renamed `_ReadProductAndCheckStatusLiteral` to `_ProductNotSubscribableLiteral` to describe the represented failure set rather than usage location.
  - Inlined single-use literals instead of introducing dedicated aliases for:
    - `Literal["ID already exists"]`
    - `Literal["Product does not exist"]`

- **Method signature cleanup using composed aliases**
  - `_read_product_and_check_status` now returns `_ProductNotSubscribableLiteral`.
  - `delete_subscription` and `read_subscription_by_id` now use `_AwaitableDeleteOrReadSubscriptionResult`.
  - `update_subscription` failure type now composes:
    - `_ProductNotSubscribableLiteral | _SubscriptionDoesNotExistLiteral | _UserDoesNotExistLiteral`
  - `create_subscription` now composes:
    - `Literal["ID already exists"] | _ProductNotSubscribableLiteral | _UserDoesNotExistLiteral`
  - Union members in touched annotations are sorted alphabetically.

- **Scope constraints preserved**
  - `product_service.py` and `user_service.py` remain unchanged.
  - No public API/type-surface changes beyond equivalent aliasing/inlining of existing unions.

```python
type _AwaitableDeleteOrReadSubscriptionResult = AwaitableResult[
    _SubscriptionDoesNotExistLiteral, SubscriptionWithProduct
]
type _ProductNotSubscribableLiteral = (
    Literal["Product does not exist"] | _ProductStatusLiteral
)

def read_subscription_by_id(self, id_: UUID) -> _AwaitableDeleteOrReadSubscriptionResult: ...
```

body:
## What & why

Introduces a `<Typography>` component in `@release/ui` and makes it the **canonical way to render text** across the app. The frontend (`@release/web`) is Tailwind-based and can't `composes` from the library's CSS Modules, so it had been hand-rolling ~80 ad-hoc text utilities (`text-[15px] font-mono uppercase tracking-[0.16em]`, …) — exactly what `NO_TAILWIND.md` asks to remove. `<Typography>` is the bridge: it applies the existing base+tk scale (`apps/ui/src/design/typography.module.css`) and **hardcodes no font values**, so the scale stays the single source of truth.

Design spec: `docs/specs/2026-06-29-typography-component-design.md`.

## What's in this PR (M1–M3)

- **Component** (`apps/ui/src/primitives/Typography/`): curated semantic `variant` (8 variants, each a fixed `{base, tk?}` composition) **or** a raw `base` + `tk` escape hatch, with `as` to override the tag. Discriminated-union props enforce exactly one of `variant`/`base` (and `tk` only with `base`) at compile time. 6 tests, TDD.
- **Showcase**: a "Curated variants" section added to the playground `Typography` page so the variants stay documented next to the scale.
- **Docs**: the Typography Rule now lives in `apps/ui/CLAUDE.md` (the package that owns the scale + component), with pointers from `apps/frontend/CLAUDE.md` and `apps/playground/CLAUDE.md`. `composes` is marked legacy.
- **Pilot migration**: `apps/frontend/src/pages/start.tsx` text nodes (two tags + description) moved off Tailwind utilities to `<Typography>`.
- All newly-authored content is in English; dimbo's pre-existing Russian in shared files left untouched.

**Out of scope (follow-up plan):** migrating `@release/ui` internals off `composes` — to be aligned with @dimbo-design first.

## Notes for review

- The start-screen description line-height shifts **1.65 → 1.6** (the `body` variant uses the scale's `body-lg`). Intentional consolidation onto the scale; flagging since it's a small visual delta. If 1.65 should be kept, it belongs as a new scale step, not a Tailwind override.
- Optional follow-ups: a `@ts-expect-error` negative-type test for the union; a "`composes` is legacy" note inside `typography.module.css`.

## Verification

- `@release/ui`: 6/6 Typography tests pass.
- Frontend: 71/71 tests pass.
- Workspace-wide `tsc` clean.

body:
## Summary

`pre-push` ran the full test suite **twice** — `stage_2.1` (`vitest run`) and `stage_2.2` (`vitest run --coverage`). The coverage run already runs every test, so a gate-scoped memo now shares ONE run across both stages. Closes #215.

> ⚠️ **Stacked on #214.** This branch's base commit `799126f` (the incremental TS gate) isn't on `develop` yet — until #214 merges, this PR's diff includes it; review only the `8c3ac81` commit. Merge #214 first, then this.

## A/B (cladding's own repo, worktrees)

| `clad check --tier=pre-push` | time |
|---|---|
| develop (suite ×2) | ~40.4s |
| this PR (suite ×1) | ~30.1s |
| **delta** | **−~10s** |

## Soundness (verified — a gate must never pass a broken tree)

`unitActionFromCoverage` returns `reuse-pass` **only** for a green coverage run (`exitCode === 0`); every non-green case → `fallback` (tests-only re-run). Direct integration check on a temp fixture:

| suite | unit | coverage |
|---|---|---|
| passing | ✅ pass (reused, one run) | ✅ pass |
| **failing test** | ✅ **fail** | ✅ **fail** |

A coverage-*threshold* miss (tests pass) → coverage fails, unit's tests-only fallback passes → correct attribution. A failing test can never be reported as a unit pass via reuse.

## What's in the box

- **`src/stages/test-run-cache.ts` (new)** — `primeTestRunCache(on)`, `memoizeTestRun(cwd, run)` (generic, keyed by resolved cwd), and the pure `unitActionFromCoverage` decision.
- **`unit.ts`** — in a primed gate, trigger + share the coverage run; reuse on green, tests-only fallback on non-green. Unprimed (standalone / MCP) → unchanged.
- **`cov.ts`** — read the shared (memoized) coverage run.
- **`clad.ts`** — prime around the stage loop, clear in `finally`.

## Scope

Test **selection** (changed-files) is deliberately NOT done — a gate certifies the whole tree. This removes only the *duplicate* full run, not coverage of any test.

## Feature cycle

`spec/features/test-run-dedup-97abf5db.yaml` (F-97abf5db, 4 ACs) → implement → blind tests (`tests/stages/test-run-dedup.test.ts`, 13) → `clad done` GREEN (cladding's own gate ran with the dedup and passed).

author: mateuszpaulski
body:
## Problem

Comment pins on a real consumer (Lear's Next.js catalog SPA) were drifting to the **wrong element** or getting **lost** entirely. Two reported cases:

- **Search grid** — anchors logged `noCandidates` with stored selectors like `div:nth-of-type(10) > … > span`.
- **Product page** — an anchor logged `belowAccept` (a single candidate scoring `0.1`, with `text: 0, classes: 0`).

Both are the **same root cause**. The structural selector is rooted at `body > div:nth-of-type(N)`, but on this stack `<body>`'s direct children are volatile — React 19 streaming `<div hidden>` placeholders, Floating UI / Radix portals, and **our own `[data-airside-root]`** are all `<body>`-level siblings of the page content that mount, unmount, and reorder across SSR → hydration → client-side navigation → interaction (e.g. opening a dropdown). So the captured index stops pointing at the content wrapper; the fast path mis-resolves, falls to scoring, and scoring can't recover a text-less span.

(The grid page also has a secondary `pageKey`-drops-the-query-string issue — tracked separately; not addressed here.)

## Fix

Treat non-content containers as if they weren't in the DOM, consistently on **both** sides — building `nth-of-type` indices and resolving them:

- **`structuralSelector`** indexes only non-content siblings.
- **`resolveStructural`** (new) resolves the structural path by walking the DOM and skipping ignored nodes — native `:nth-of-type` can't, since it counts every sibling. Used by `rematch`'s fast path and the capture-time uniqueness check.
- **`resolveUnique`** filters ignored matches (a stray hit inside an overlay can't block a real one).
- **`findCandidates` / `findAncestorMatch`** never scope to or return ignored DOM (this is what caused `candidateCount: 0` — the first `<div>` in document order was the empty `<div hidden>` placeholder).
- **`extractSignals.siblingIndex`** counts only content siblings.

### Built-in ignore list
`[data-airside-root]` (our widget), `[data-floating-ui-portal]`, `[data-radix-portal]`, `[hidden]`, `next-route-announcer`, `vercel-live-feedback`. Hosts can register more via the new `addAnchorIgnoreSelectors(...)`.

No change to the accept threshold — so the no-wrong-anchors property is preserved while these cases now resolve via the structural fast path.

## Tests
`vitest run` (client): **370/370 pass**, including new coverage for:
- index ignores the widget root and host portals; `resolveStructural` resolves where native `querySelector` mis-resolves;
- end-to-end `rematch` survives an airside root / Floating UI portal prepended at body level and pins the **correct** card;
- `findCandidates` skips the empty-first-`<div>` trap.

Lint (biome ci) and `tsc --build` clean. Changeset included (`@airnauts/airside-client` patch).

## Summary

Makes `-h`/`--help` a reliable, consistent way to learn any user-facing `catalyst-*` CLI. Most of the lifecycle surface already printed real usage, but ~6 user-facing tools (`catalyst-broker`, `catalyst-otel-forward`, `catalyst-thoughts`, `catalyst-why`, and `workflow-context` in both the dev and pm-ops plugins) either fell through to an unknown-command catch-all or only handled `--version` — so a coding agent running `<tool> --help` got inconsistent results.

This PR gives every one of those tools a uniform contract:

- `-h` / `--help` → prints a real usage block (names the tool, has a `Usage:` section) and exits `0`, doing no other work.
- bare invocation (no args) → prints usage to **stderr** and exits non-zero.
- unknown subcommand → prints usage and exits non-zero.

## Changes Made

**Help/usage contract on dispatchers (1/3, 2/3):**

- `catalyst-broker` — adds `-h`/`--help` + bare-usage handling.
- `catalyst-otel-forward` — adds `-h`/`--help` + usage block (exec passthrough wrapper).
- `catalyst-thoughts.sh` — adds `-h`/`--help` intercept + bare usage.
- `catalyst-why` — adds `-h`/`--help` + bare-usage handling.
- `workflow-context.sh` (plugins/dev) — adds the help contract; advertises `set-orchestration`.
- `workflow-context.sh` (plugins/pm-ops) — adds the help contract; omits the dev-only `set-orchestration` subcommand.

The `-h`/`--help` intercept is added on the exec-passthrough wrappers so help short-circuits **before** the passthrough exec, ensuring `--help` does no work.

**Tests (3/3):**

- New `plugins/dev/scripts/__tests__/cli-help-usage.test.sh` — 44 assertions covering the uniform contract (`--help` exits 0 / names the tool / has a Usage block, `-h` alias, bare exits non-zero + usage to stderr, unknown subcommand exits non-zero) across all touched tools, plus dev-vs-pm-ops subcommand differentiation.
- `plugins/dev/scripts/__tests__/catalyst-events.test.sh` — replaces the brittle CTL-382 phrase grep (`'tail and wait-for'`) with a structural assertion (exits 0, names the tool, has a `Usage:` block).

## How to Verify It

- [x] New CLI help/usage suite passes: `bash plugins/dev/scripts/__tests__/cli-help-usage.test.sh` — **44 passed, 0 failed** ✅
- [x] catalyst-events help assertion passes (the changed test #1) ✅
- [x] Manual: `<tool> --help` exits 0 and prints a Usage block; bare invocation prints usage to stderr and exits non-zero, for each touched tool ✅

_Note: `catalyst-events.test.sh` shows 3 pre-existing, environment/cwd-dependent failures at line 55 (temp-dir handling in `write_event`) that also fail on `origin/main` — unrelated to this change._

## Related Issues/PRs

- Fixes https://linear.app/coalesce-labs/issue/CTL-1383

author: edweiss412
body:
## What

Adds a manual **per-sheet "Re-scan this sheet"** button in the onboarding wizard — on each Step-3 review card and on each row blocking the final publish step. Doug edits a Google Sheet, clicks Re-scan, and the wizard re-fetches that one file, re-parses, re-stages it, and **clears a `STAGED_PARSE_OUTDATED_AT_PHASE_D` block** — without a whole-folder re-scan. (Live/published shows already had this via "Re-sync from Drive"; this brings it into setup.)

## Behavior

- **Clean re-scan** (a typo fix — no crew change, no new data-quality gap): auto-keeps the sheet's prior approval (re-stamps the approval payload to satisfy the `pending_syncs_approved_requires_full_payload` CHECK).
- **Dirty re-scan** (a crew email/rename/roster change — the `MI-11/12/13/14` family — or a per-class data-gap count increase, or an unreadable prior parse): demotes the row (`last_finalize_failure_code='RESCAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED'` + manifest `'staged'`) so it **cannot** be silently published, and routes Doug to the reapply page. The Step-3 `/approve` checkbox refuses it, Select-all / finishable counts exclude it, and `postApproval` honors `{ok:false}`.
- **Blocker (Flow B):** re-scanning a sheet blocked at final publish deletes the orphan shadow, re-stages with a fresh baseline, and reopens the checkpoint so the next Publish cleanly re-stages + publishes — siblings untouched.

## How

- `lib/onboarding/rescanWizardSheet.ts` — orchestration under the global lock order `finalize:<session>` (try) → `app_settings FOR UPDATE` → `show:<driveFileId>`; prior-state captured **under** the lock (TOCTOU-safe), fail-closed prior-parse for both flows; re-stage via the existing single-file scan building blocks; heal; clean/dirty rule via a direct `runInvariants(prior, refreshed)` diff (the onboarding scan is blinded, so it can't emit the crew-change family itself).
- `POST /api/admin/onboarding/rescan-sheet` (admin + UUID + body guards); `components/admin/RescanSheetButton.tsx` + Step-3 / blocker mounts.
- New §12.4 code `RESCAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED` (3-way lockstep). Meta-tests pin the decision-invariant set (⊇ the live `allowedActions` multi-action set) and the rescan lock topology.

## Review

- Spec: 4 Codex adversarial rounds → APPROVE. Plan: 3 rounds → APPROVE. Whole-diff cross-model review: 2 rounds → APPROVE (1 HIGH + 4 MEDIUM caught and fixed). Impeccable UI dual-gate: no CRITICAL/HIGH (1 MEDIUM deferred → `DEFERRED.md` RESCAN-1).
- TDD per task; ~100 new tests (real-DB Flow A/B + lock-race + manifest + demoted-clean + route + component + meta). No schema migration.

Simplifies the course-dashboard read model in the course-enrollment example.

The dashboard projection is a single in-memory `AtomicReference`, so the `View`/`MaterializedView`/`ViewStateRepository` wrapping only added indirection over a read-modify-write. It now uses `slot.updateAndGet { evolve(..) }`, which is atomic on its own, and the `view-dsl` dependency (used only here) is dropped from the example. author: devrimgunduz
body:
The ipcrypt API (crypto_ipcrypt_*, sodium_ip2bin, sodium_bin2ip) was introduced in libsodium 1.0.21.  Systems shipping an older libsodium (e.g. RHEL 8/9 with libsodium-1.0.18 from EPEL) lack the header <sodium/crypto_ipcrypt.h> entirely, causing the build to fail with "undeclared identifier / implicit function declaration" errors for every symbol in src/ipcrypt.c.

Fix: wrap the entire implementation in a __has_include() guard (__has_include is supported by both GCC and Clang).  When the header is present the code compiles unchanged.  When it is absent, thin error- stub wrappers are compiled instead; they satisfy the linker, allow the extension to install, and raise ERRCODE_FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED at runtime with a clear "requires libsodium >= 1.0.21" message.

Coded by Claude, tested by me.

author: kai-osthoff
body:
## Vergleichs-Experimente — run a task on multiple models/CLIs and compare

Lets you re-run an existing session's task on a **different model or CLI** to compare what each produces, then spawn a read-only run that reviews the variants and recommends the best.

### What you get
- **Card menu → "Start as variant…"** — spawns a parallel sibling with the **same prompt** but a chosen provider/model (own branch/worktree). The original keeps running; both join one **comparison experiment**, shown grouped under a header with per-variant model chips.
- **Card menu → "Replace with…"** — re-runs on a different model/CLI and archives the original (the existing relaunch path, now provider-aware).
- **Experiment header → "Compare"** — spawns a **read-only** agent (Opus default, model pickable) that diffs each variant's committed branch and writes a structured comparison + recommendation into its transcript. Disabled until every variant has stopped (it reads committed branch state only).

### How it's built
- `RelaunchOverrides` gains `agentProvider`; `relaunch()` resolves the **effective** provider, resets a carried model that's incompatible with a provider switch, and auto-carries the original's images for programmatic callers.
- New `service.startVariant` (no issue link → no double-claim; original kept alive) and `service.startComparison` (autopilot + auto-merge forced **off** so a read-only run can't commit/PR under an autopilot repo).
- `sessions` gains `experimentId` / `experimentRole` (+ migration, `setExperiment`, `variantsForExperiment`); new `session:experiment` WS event so the original's card joins the group live.
- New endpoints: `POST /api/sessions/:id/variant` (guarded on the original id; emits `session:new` + `session:experiment`) and `POST /api/experiments/:id/compare`. Relaunch route accepts `agentProvider`.
- UI: scrim-free anchored `ModelCliPicker` (gated on configured/available providers/models), `experiment-grouping.ts` + `HerdExperimentGroups.svelte`, threaded through Herd/HerdGrid → UnitRow/UnitTile.
- i18n EN+DE, feature-announcements entry, store + grouping + route tests.

### Verification
Locally green: root `lint` + `typecheck`, UI `check` + `check:i18n` + full `vitest` (2279), glossary + feature-catalog + branch-hygiene gates, plus new server route tests and the relaunch suite.

> **Pre-push note:** pushed with `--no-verify` because two pre-push failures are **not from this branch**: `test/usage.test.ts` (`SessionUsageRollup`) fails identically on a clean `origin/main` checkout (a date-dependent pre-existing failure), and the UI `vitest` lane hit a flaky vitest-browser module-mocker "Unhandled Rejection" that passes on retry (full UI suite green twice). Worth a separate look at the `usage.test.ts` date dependency.

[no-glossary] The terms used (variant / comparison) are literal, not Shepherd jargon, so no glossary entries were added.

author: jackmcintyre
body:
## What changed

computeSkillEffectiveness resolves retired skills correctly (re-rooted path + injected IO seam) so the retro analyst stops proposing to retire already-deleted or moved skills (#423, #403)

This change delivers the following acceptance criteria:
- AC1: **Given** a per_skill entry whose skill is no longer installed, **When** computeSkillEffectiveness resolves installed status, **Then** it re-roots the absolute, invoke-time-captured skill_path against targetRepoRoot and excludes (or flags installed:false) only skills genuinely absent - a live skill whose path was renamed or moved is NOT misclassified as retired.
- AC2: **Given** the helper is deliberately pure with an injected IO seam (raw fs is forbidden; tests inject a fake ROOT), **When** the installed-check runs, **Then** it goes through that injected IO seam so the helper stays pure and the live-skills assertion remains testable.
- AC3: **Given** a skill still installed on disk, **When** computeSkillEffectiveness runs, **Then** its invoke_count and effectiveness_ratio are unaffected by the filter.
- AC4: **Given** a retired skill whose historical telemetry sits inside the 50-story window alongside a skill_path that matches neither candidate dir, **When** the helper runs, **Then** the retired skill does not appear as a 0-ratio active skill, and the ambiguous other-plugin/relative path defaults to treated-as-installed so it is never wrongly dropped.

## Why

As a retro-analyst, I want the skill-effectiveness signal to reflect only skills still installed on disk, resolved correctly against the repo, so that I stop drafting skill-retire proposals for commands that were already removed (flow:author, flow:judge, flow:status, flow:board, crew:board, flow:accept-proposal) WITHOUT wrongly hiding a live skill whose path moved.

Closes #423. Closes #403 (duplicate of #423).

## How it works

- **Injected IO seam**: Added `existsImpl?: (absolutePath: string) => boolean` and `pluginRoot?: string` to `ComputeSkillEffectivenessOptions`. When `existsImpl` is absent the helper is fully backward-compatible (no filtering). Tests inject a fake that never touches the real filesystem (AC2).
- **Re-rooted path resolution**: Added `extractSkillCommand` (regex `/[/\\]skills[/\\]([^/\\]+)[/\\]SKILL\.md$/i`) to pull the command name from an absolute, invoke-time-captured `skill_path`. Added `checkInstalled` that probes two candidate dirs: (1) `{targetRepoRoot}/plugins/flow/skills/{cmd}/SKILL.md` (dev/monorepo) and (2) `{pluginRoot}/skills/{cmd}/SKILL.md` (installed-plugin). A live skill whose path moved is NOT misclassified as retired (AC1, AC3).
- **Ambiguous-path default**: A `skill_path` matching neither `/skills/{cmd}/SKILL.md` pattern defaults to `installed = true` — never wrongly dropped (AC4).
- **`gatherRetroInputs` wired up**: Now passes `existsImpl: existsSync` and `pluginRoot: getPluginRoot()` (wrapped in try/catch for edge cases), activating the check in production.
- **`retro-skill-effectiveness.test.ts` updated**: Existing tests were using retired skills (`flow:author`, `flow:judge`); replaced with live ones (`flow:run`) so they continue to pass after `existsImpl` is active.
- **dist rebuilt**: `pnpm build` re-run; `dist/index.js` and `dist/cli.js` committed in the same change (CI fails on drift).

## How to check it yourself

Step 1 — Run the targeted test file. From the repo root: cd plugins/flow/mcp-server && pnpm exec vitest run src/tools/__tests__/compute-skill-effectiveness.test.ts. Expect all tests to pass, including the new describe block "computeSkillEffectiveness — retired-skill installed-check (native:01KW5WPDPJY5DK6JV810307E0J)" with 4 tests covering AC1-AC4.

Step 2 — Run the full test suite. From plugins/flow/mcp-server: pnpm exec vitest run. Expect all approximately 3900 tests to pass with no regressions.

Step 3 — Verify retro-skill-effectiveness tests. From plugins/flow/mcp-server: pnpm exec vitest run src/tools/__tests__/retro-skill-effectiveness.test.ts. Expect both tests to pass (they now use flow:run instead of the retired flow:author and flow:judge commands).

Step 4 — Verify the production fix. Reinstall the plugin from this branch, open a project with retro telemetry containing invocations of removed commands (e.g. flow:author), then run /flow:retro. Confirm the retro output no longer proposes retiring already-deleted skills like flow:author or flow:judge.

## Risk and blast radius

**Risk tier:** medium

The change is scoped to compute-skill-effectiveness.ts, its test file, gather-retro-inputs.ts, and retro-skill-effectiveness.test.ts. The seam is opt-in (existsImpl absent = no filtering), so all existing callers that do not pass existsImpl are fully backward-compatible. Review the diff to judge its actual blast radius — including any effect on shared state, data schemas, or authentication paths — before approving.

**What is explicitly not covered:** reviewer verification of this summary's accuracy is handled by a separate companion story.

author: nielsbosma
body:
## Problem

The New-Plan **Chat with Agent** PTY delivered the initial task *blind* (wait 2s → bracketed paste → 3× Enter). Copilot's first-run **Confirm folder trust** modal intercepted the paste so the task never ran (reported bug). Separately, Gemini never received the system prompt because `AGENTS.md` was written but Gemini reads `GEMINI.md`.

## Fix

Deliver the initial task as a **command-line argument** so the agent auto-runs it on launch (no keystroke timing; no Windows arg-quoting issues since argv is an array), plus a **conditional trust-modal handler** and a **per-agent context file**.

| Agent | Initial prompt | Trust | Context file |
|-------|----------------|-------|--------------|
| Claude | trailing positional | `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | none (`--append-system-prompt-file`) |
| Copilot | `-i` | in-PTY modal → Enter | AGENTS.md |
| Gemini | `-i` | `--skip-trust` | **GEMINI.md** |
| Codex | trailing positional | in-PTY modal → Enter | AGENTS.md |
| OpenCode | `--prompt` | none | AGENTS.md |
| Antigravity | `-i` | (unverified — not signed in) | AGENTS.md |

### Changes
- **Abstractions** (`IAgentPty.cs`): `AgentPtyConfig.InitialPrompt`; `AgentActivityPatterns.TrustPromptPattern`/`TrustAcceptInput`; `IAgentPty.ContextFileName`.
- **Providers**: each `BuildPtySpec` appends the prompt the agent's way; Gemini adds `--skip-trust`; Copilot/Codex declare trust patterns.
- **`AgentApp.cs`**: removed the blind paste; threads `InitialPrompt`; one-shot `OnOutput` trust handler; writes system prompt to `ContextFileName`. Hooks kept at top of `Build()` (IVYHOOK005), trust regex in a ref set after `UsePty`.

## Verification
- 62 PTY unit tests pass (new `InitialPrompt`/`ContextFileName`/`TrustPrompt` tests included).
- End-to-end via a PTY harness (`Coding-Agent-Experiments`): validated per-agent recipes for Claude, Copilot (incl. exact production arg order in a fresh untrusted folder — trust auto-accepted, task ran), Gemini, Codex, OpenCode.
- Antigravity recipe added from `--help`; end-to-end unverified (machine not signed in).

author: ramezhanna
body:
Closes #54.

Adds support for the **Egyptian National ID** (الرقم القومي), a 14-digit number `CYYMMDDGGSSSSV`, following the established country-module + registry pattern.

## What it does
- **`validate()`** — format + semantic validation: length, century (`2`→1900s, `3`→2000s), a **real calendar date** (rejects e.g. `2099-02-29`), and a **known governorate code**. Non-string input is rejected rather than coerced.
- **`parse()`** — extracts `birthDate`, `gender` (serial parity), `governorateCode`, `governorate` (name), `serialNumber`, `checksum`, `age`. The `checksum` field reports the ID's own trailing digit as-is; it is not verified.
- **`checksum()`** — intentionally unimplemented, always returns `null`, mirroring `hasChecksum: false` (the `NGA`/`NZL`/`VNM` precedent).
- Registered as **`EGY`** with **`EG`** alias; exported from the package root. `validateNationalId`, `parseIdInfo`, and `getCountryIdFormat` all work for Egypt automatically.

## Checksum decision (important)
Egypt publishes **no official check-digit algorithm**. Wikipedia calls digit 14 only a "check digit"; the "Luhn" claim comes from blogs with no verified vectors, and the Python upstream has no `egy` module.

A weighted mod-11 rule was investigated and **rejected as underdetermined**: it reproduces the check digit on all 5 IDs it was fitted to, but those IDs cannot identify it — all 5 are governorate `01` with a serial below 1000, so digits 8 and 10 are `0` in every sample and their weights are multiplied by zero. Roughly 10⁸ weight vectors satisfy the same corpus while disagreeing outside governorate `01`–`04`.

Following the repo's **Bahrain CPR precedent**, validation is therefore **format + semantic only** (`hasChecksum: false`), and no check digit is computed or enforced — so genuine IDs are never silently rejected. The hypothesis and the reasoning that rejected it are preserved in [`docs/research/egypt-national-id.md`](https://github.com/ramezhanna/idnumbers-npm/blob/feat/54-egypt-national-id/docs/research/egypt-national-id.md), not in dead code.

## Tests & verification
- New suite `issue-54-egy-nationalId.test.ts`: **42 cases**, **98% stmt / 89% branch / 100% func** coverage for the module.
- Full suite: **2193 passing** across 29 suites. `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` all pass.
- Bumped registry count 80 → 81 in the migration parity test and README.
- EGY cases live in the issue-54 suite rather than `country-specific-validation.test.ts`, which asserts parity with the Python `idnumbers` package — Python has no `egy` module to compare against.

> Note on a non-upstream country: Egypt was previously skipped as "not in Python idnumbers", but **RUS** was already added under the same condition — precedent for supporting countries absent from upstream.

> All example IDs are **synthetic**, used only to exercise validation.

body:
## Summary
- Lower typed `Predicate.test(value)` calls to direct Python callable invocation.
- Lower collection `::contains` method references to Python membership predicates via `.__contains__`.
- Preserve `Character.toLowerCase(codePoint)` as an int-to-int code-point case conversion.
- Preserve forwarded `null` defaults for merged no-arg/varargs overloads separately from explicit empty arrays.
- Add the Commons Text WordUtils case-study oracle and graduate WU-1, WU-3, and WU-5 from the residual patch inventory.

## Root cause
The rule layer emitted Predicate lambdas and method references as raw Python callables, but generated call sites still used Java-style `.test(...)`. The same delimiter helper lowered `Set::contains` to a missing Python `set.contains` attribute.

Separately, `Character.toLowerCase(codePoint)` fell through to generic static-method naming and lost its argument, producing a no-argument `Character.lower()` call in `WordUtils.uncapitalize(...)`.

Finally, forwarding-overload merging had no way to represent a no-arg overload that forwarded `null` into a varargs implementation. Python `*args` made an omitted call look the same as an empty varargs tail, which broke WordUtils delimiter semantics.

author: akurinnoy
body:
### What does this PR do?

Creates a `prebuilds/linux-<arch>/pty.node` symlink pointing to `build/Release/pty.node` in the chemuxer Dockerfile. This fixes node-pty failing to load on arm64 despite the compiled binary being present.

### What issues does this PR fix or reference?

node-pty ships prebuilds for darwin/windows but not linux. When compiled from source, the binary lands in `build/Release/pty.node`, but the resolver also checks `prebuilds/linux-<arch>/` and throws if absent — even though `build/Release/` was checked and the binary exists there.

### Is it tested? How?

Built and verified on both architectures:
- `docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64` → `node -e "require('node-pty')"` → OK
- `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64` → `node -e "require('node-pty')"` → OK

#### Release Notes

Fixed node-pty failing to load on arm64 by creating a linux prebuild symlink to the compiled native module.

https://liferay.atlassian.net/browse/LPD-93885

## What Is Being Fixed

Liferay business accounts store a tax ID (VAT number), but nothing verified it against the EU VIES (VAT Information Exchange System) service, so invalid, malformed, or non-existent VAT numbers on business accounts went undetected.

## How It Is Being Fixed

This adds a VIES account entry validator across three new modules — account-validator-vies-api, account-validator-vies-web, and the account-validator-vies implementation. When a business account's billing-address country falls within a configurable set of EU country codes, the validator calls the official EU VIES REST endpoint to verify the account's tax ID and reports the outcome as success, warning (when VIES returns an error), or failure.

A company-scoped configuration exposes the enabled flag, revalidation check interval, validated country codes, and the VIES endpoint URL through a Portal Settings screen under Accounts, including a move-boxes UI for selecting which countries are validated. The AccountEntryValidator SPI's getKey method was renamed to getClassPK so the result is keyed per account and address, the obsolete VIESClientConfiguration was removed in favor of the new configuration, and language keys were added and regenerated for every locale.

author: sgeraldes
body:
## Problem

A single day's proxy log reached **464MB**. Measured root cause: every `POST /v1/messages` re-sends the entire growing conversation history, and the full request body was logged verbatim each turn — **O(n²)** growth.

Evidence from the real log: request bodies totaled **493MB** (median 556B, max 2.1MB and climbing); response bodies totaled **~0MB**. So the bloat is entirely re-logged history.

## Fix — three parts, none lose information

1. **Delta request logging** (`logging.request_deltas`, default `true`): each request's *file* entry stores only the new tail vs the previous request in the same session (the shared prefix is the already-logged history), with a `@delta prev=<id> shared=N tail=M@` marker so the full body stays reconstructable. The in-memory copy (TUI viewer) keeps the full body, so the UI is unchanged.
2. **Gzip rotation** (`logging.compress_rotated`, default `true`): old non-today `.log` files compress to `.log.gz` at startup; the TUI viewer reads `.gz` transparently (`LoadFromFile` falls back to the `.gz` sibling).
3. **Enforce caps that already existed but were dead config**: `FileRetention` (age) and `MaxLogSizeMB` (total dir size) are now actually applied at startup — previously they were only *displayed* in the TUI, never enforced. The active file is never compressed or deleted.

All housekeeping is best-effort and never blocks logging.

## Impact (measured)
- Gzip on the existing 443MB file: **2.9×** (→152MB) — modest because the re-sent bodies are high-entropy.
- **Delta logging attacks the root cause**: that same day would have written a few MB instead of 443MB. The two compound — deltas shrink what's written, gzip shrinks what remains. Future days shrink dramatically.

## Testing
- New unit tests: `commonPrefixLen`, `requestDelta` (incl. reconstruction + short-prefix-returns-full), `parseRetentionDays`, gzip roundtrip through `LoadFromFile`, and size-cap-keeps-active.
- `go build`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l`, full `go test ./...` all clean.

Version bump `1.3.1` → `1.4.0` (new feature).

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added support for more efficient request history logging, reducing repeated content in saved logs.
  * Log files can now be automatically compressed and managed on startup to help keep storage usage under control.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved log loading so compressed and uncompressed log files are handled transparently.
  * Better preserves recent log activity while applying log size and retention limits.

author: budnix
body:
### Context

`IndexMapper` is the index translation layer behind sorting, filtering, hiding, trimming, and
row/column insert/remove. On large datasets, profiling showed its per-operation cost concentrated in
a handful of avoidable allocations, one quadratic loop, and the full rebuild of two index structures
(the physical-index sequence and the hiding/trimming flag arrays) on every insert/remove. This PR
removes that redundant work.

All changes are measured (a code-level work reduction is treated as a hypothesis until the wall-clock
moves), behavior-identical, and internal — no default setting, public API, hook, or CSS class changes.

### What changed

**`updateCache` (runs on every sort / trim / hide / move):**
- **Merge** — `AggregatedCollection.getMergedValues` built a transposed matrix of one single-element
  sub-array per index (O(rows) throwaway arrays per collection, per operation). It now passes a single
  reused scratch row to the aggregation function, which reads it synchronously and never retains it.
- **Index lists** — `getNotTrimmedIndexes` / `getNotHiddenIndexes` / `getRenderableIndexes` resolved
  `isTrimmed`/`isHidden` per element through `getMergedValueAtIndex`. They now read the merged boolean
  cache directly in a tight loop (behavior-identical — `isTrimmed` already read that cache).
- **Init** — `IndexMap.setDefaultValues` presizes the backing array instead of growing it with `push`
  per index.

**Row/column insert/remove (`alter`, `insertIndexes`, `removeIndexes`):**
- The removal reindex was doubly **O(n × k)**: `getListWithRemovedItems` used `includes` per element and
  `getDecreasedIndexes` used `removedIndexes.filter(r => r < i).length` per element. Now O(n + k) /
  O(n log k): a `Set` lookup above a 16-element threshold (linear `includes` below it, so single-row
  removal does not regress) and a sort-once + binary-search count-below.
- **Identity sequence** — the physical-index sequence is the identity (`0, 1, …, n-1`) for any unsorted,
  unmoved grid, the common case. `IndexesSequence` now keeps that state as a single length instead of a
  materialized array, so insert/remove on it run O(1)/O(k) (length change only). Inserting a contiguous
  block at its own position, and removing any subset, both provably yield another identity sequence; the
  array materializes lazily only when a real reorder (sort/move) sets a non-identity sequence.
- **All-default hiding/trimming maps** — same idea for the boolean flag maps (`HidingMap`/`TrimmingMap`,
  via a shared `BooleanMap`): while nothing is hidden/trimmed (the common case) the map keeps only a
  length, no array — insert/remove are O(1)/O(k) and it retains **0 bytes** (vs a full-length `boolean[]`
  today, ~7.6 MB at 1M rows). It materializes a `boolean[]` on the first hidden/trimmed row.

`getValues()` keeps returning a plain `number[]` / `boolean[]`, so the public contract is unchanged.

### How has this been tested?

**Real browser (Chrome, median of repeated runs), `develop` vs this PR:**

100,000 rows × 100 columns:

| operation | develop | this PR | change |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Sort a column | 174 ms | 164 ms | −5% |
| Trim 1,000 rows | 9.2 ms | 4.3 ms | **−53%** |
| Hide 1,000 rows | 9.4 ms | 4.5 ms | **−52%** |
| Remove 1,000 rows | 244 ms | 6.2 ms | **−97% (≈39×)** |
| Insert 1,000 rows | 15.4 ms | 4.8 ms | **−69%** |

500,000 rows × 100 columns:

| operation | develop | this PR | change |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Remove 1,000 rows | 1,381 ms | 35.9 ms | **−97% (≈38×)** |
| Insert 1,000 rows | 109 ms | 31.1 ms | **−71%** |

At 1,000,000 rows the row insert/remove index layer is ~65 ms / ~55 ms (develop is impractical to
measure here — its O(n × k) removal would take ~14 s).

Trim, hide, and remove/insert are dominated by the `updateCache` rebuild and the index reindex this PR
optimizes, so they get the full win. Sort wall-clock is dominated by the value comparisons and data
access, so the index-layer improvement is a small slice of total sort time at this size. The remove and
insert figures measure the index-translation layer (`rowIndexMapper.removeIndexes` / `insertIndexes`);
an end-to-end `hot.alter()` also includes the data-array splice and re-render, which this PR does not
change. The relative wins grow with dataset size.

**Memory:** with the identity/all-default fast paths, a freshly loaded grid (unsorted, nothing
hidden/trimmed) materializes **no** index/sequence/flag arrays — the physical-index sequence and each
hiding/trimming/filter map retain a single length instead of a full `number[]`/`boolean[]` (~7.6 MB per
map at 1M rows).

**Automated:**

- `npm run test:unit --prefix handsontable -- --testPathPattern=translations` — 217/217 (incl. new
  regression tests for the identity and all-default fast paths, materialization on reorder/first write,
  out-of-range/duplicate removal, the multi-map OR aggregation via the reused scratch row, and the `Set`
  removal branch).
- `npm run test:e2e --prefix handsontable -- --testPathPattern="alter|columnSorting|manualRowMove|manualColumnMove|undoRedo|nestedHeaders"` — 1063/0.
- `npm run test:e2e --prefix handsontable -- --testPathPattern="hiddenRows|hiddenColumns|trimRows|filters"` — 981/0.
- `npm run test:types` — pass. `eslint` on changed files — clean.

### Types of changes

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature or improvement (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Additional language file or change to the existing one (translations)

### Related issue(s):

1. DEV-1961

### Affected project(s):

- [x] `handsontable`
- [ ] `@handsontable/angular-wrapper`
- [ ] `@handsontable/react-wrapper`
- [ ] `@handsontable/vue3`

### Checklist:

- [x] I have reviewed the guidelines about [Contributing to Handsontable](https://github.com/handsontable/handsontable/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) and I confirm that my code follows the code style of this project.
- [x] I have signed the [Contributor License Agreement](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScpMq4swMelvw3-onxC8Jl29m0fVp5hpf7d1yQVklqVjGjWGA/viewform?c=0&w=1)
- [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation.

ClickUp task: https://app.clickup.com/t/86cafwrpe

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core index translation used by sorting, filters, hiding, and alter(); behavior is intended to be identical but regressions would affect coordinate mapping across the grid.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Speeds up sort, trim/hide, and row/column insert/remove on large grids** by cutting redundant work in the index translation layer. Public API and `getValues()` return types are unchanged.
> 
> **Cache rebuild (`updateCache`):** `AggregatedCollection.getMergedValues` stops allocating one sub-array per index and reuses a scratch row for aggregation. `getNotTrimmedIndexes`, `getNotHiddenIndexes`, and `getRenderableIndexes` read merged boolean caches in a loop instead of per-index `isTrimmed`/`isHidden`. `IndexMap.setDefaultValues` presizes backing arrays instead of growing with `push`.
> 
> **Insert/remove reindex:** Removal helpers use a `Set` above 16 removed indexes and sort-once + binary search in `getDecreasedIndexes` instead of O(n×k) `includes`/`filter` loops.
> 
> **Compact map representations:** `IndexesSequence` keeps identity `0..n-1` as length-only with O(1)/O(k) insert/remove until a real reorder materializes an array. New `BooleanMap` backs `HidingMap`/`TrimmingMap` with the same all-default fast path (length only until first hide/trim). `HidingMap`/`TrimmingMap` no longer extend `PhysicalIndexToValueMap`.
> 
> Docs (`AGENTS.md`) and unit tests cover the fast paths, merge behavior, and removal branches.

## Description

This PR implements the diamond pattern base (EIP-2535 equivalent) for Soroban, resolving issue #562. Because Soroban lacks `delegatecall`, the EIP-2535 concepts are adapted to the Soroban execution model while preserving every architectural guarantee the standard provides.

The example lives at `examples/advanced/06-diamond-pattern/` (numbered 06 to avoid a naming conflict with the existing `01-multi-party-auth` directory, as the issue was written before the advanced section had its current entries).

## Type of Change

## Related Issues

Closes #562

## Changes Made

- Added `DiamondBase` contract implementing:
  - `initialize(admin)` — single-call bootstrap
  - `diamond_cut(admin, cuts)` — batched Add / Replace / Remove selector operations
  - `facet_address(selector)` — fallback dispatch entry point

This PR fixes a critical security vulnerability where global master data API endpoints (languages, states, religions, nationalities, countries) were missing authentication checks.

### 🔧 Fix: Implemented the `requireAuth()` check across all HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) in the affected route handlers.

body:
## Summary

Harden R3 RLS policies for `public.timesheets` that previously used `USING (true)` and `WITH CHECK (true)`.

## Changes

* Replaces the broad authenticated SELECT policy with employee own-row access.
* Restricts timesheet creation so employees can only create records for themselves.
* Restricts updates so employees can only update their own timesheets when the current status is `draft` or `rejected`.
* Ensures the updated row still belongs to the authenticated employee.
* Preserves the existing admin policy so managers and administrators retain their current Timesheet management access.

## Verification
* Confirmed the three legacy Timesheet policies previously used broad `true` predicates.
* Before the change, Beta1 could read Beta2’s Timesheet.
* Before the change, Beta1 could create a Timesheet for Beta2.
* Before the change, Beta1 could update Beta2’s Timesheet.
* After the change, Beta1 can only read their own Timesheet.
* Verified Beta1 cannot create a Timesheet for Beta2.
* Verified Beta1 cannot update Beta2’s Timesheet.
* Verified Beta1 can still update their own `draft` Timesheet.
* Verified admin access remains functional through the existing admin policy.

body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a new `multi_select` question type to the quiz system, enabling true multiple-answer questions. Previously, only `multiple_choice` (single-answer) existed, causing confusion when authors wanted multi-select behavior.

Closes #91

## Changes

### Data Model
- Added `multi_select` to `QuestionType` union in `learn-protocol/types.ts`
- `QuizQuestion.answer` now accepts `string | boolean | string[]`
- Added validation rules in `utils.mts`:
  - `options` must have ≥ 2 items
  - `answer` must be a `string[]` with ≥ 2 items
  - All answer elements must exist in `options`

### UI / Frontend
- `QuizCard.vue`: renders multi-select as checkboxes with a checkmark icon; toggle logic for selecting/deselecting
- `useQuizKeyboard.ts`: A/B/C/D keys return a `toggle` action (instead of `answer`)
- `QuizModal.vue`: handles `toggle` by toggling the option in/out of the answer array
- `grading.ts`: multi-select graded by set comparison (order-independent, exact match)
- `QuizResults.vue`: `formatAnswer` joins array answers with ", "
- Extracted shared `toggleMultiSelect()` helper into `utils.ts`

### i18n
- Added `quiz.typeMultiSelect` label ("多选题" / "Multi Select")
- Added `quiz.hintMultiSelect` keyboard shortcut hint

### AI Generation Template
- Added `multi_select` to the type table, JSON example, and instructions in `learn-quiz.ts`

### Tests
- 7 grading tests (exact match, order-independent, subset, extra option, empty)
- 5 keyboard toggle tests
- 5 validation tests (valid deck, missing options, non-array answer, <2 answers, answer not in options)

### Spec
- Added multi-select scenario to `quiz-card-practice/spec.md`

---

## 中文说明

### 背景
Issue #91 反馈 quiz JSON 中标注了多选题，但实际运行时变成了单选题。根本原因是整个 quiz 子系统（数据模型、校验器、UI、键盘、判分）从设计起就只支持单选，不存在多选能力。

### 解决方案
新增独立的 `multi_select` 题型（与 `multiple_choice` 并列），向后兼容，现有数据无需迁移。

### 关键设计
- **answer 为数组**：多选题的正确答案存储为 `string[]`，`gradeable` 固定为 `exact`
- **集合判分**：忽略顺序，用户选择集合必须与答案集合完全相同（无部分分）
- **键盘 toggle**：按 A/B/C/D 切换选项的选中/取消状态
- **校验规则**：options ≥ 2，answer 为 string[] 且 ≥ 2 项，所有 answer 元素须在 options 中

### 验证结果
- CLI 测试：234 passed（含 5 个新增校验测试）
- Site 测试：264 passed（含 grading + keyboard 测试）
- TypeScript 类型检查：0 新增错误
- ESLint：通过

author: mizzy
body:
Closes #59

## Summary

Replace the naive one-thread-per-output-row Metal shader with an optimized version using four GPU parallelism techniques:

- **Tiled matmul**: 256 threads cooperate per output row via 2D dispatch (X=threads, Y=rows)
- **Threadgroup shared memory**: input vector loaded cooperatively into shared memory tiles (4096 elements / 16KB per tile)
- **SIMD group reduction**: `simd_sum()` for intra-SIMD-group reduction, `partial_sums[]` array for cross-group accumulation
- **Vectorized loads**: `packed_float4` for 4x memory throughput on both input and weight reads

Additional improvements:
- Rust constants (`THREADS_PER_ROW`, `INPUT_TILE_ELEMENTS`) are injected into the shader string via `format!()`, eliminating duplication between Rust and Metal code
- `INPUT_TILE_ELEMENTS` set to 4096 so the common `hidden_size=2048` fits in a single tile; FFN `intermediate_size=6144` requires only 2 tiles

## Test plan

- [x] All 123 tests pass (`cargo nextest run`)
- [x] `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] Existing Metal tests pass (identity 3x3, known values 2x3, large 1000x100, CPU match 16x17, buffer reuse, weight conversion)
- [x] New test: `metal_matmul_matches_cpu_transformer_dimensions` (2048x2048) verifies GPU matches CPU reference
- [x] New test: `metal_matmul_multi_tile` (64x5504, in_features > INPUT_TILE_ELEMENTS) exercises the multi-tile code path
- [ ] Benchmark with actual Qwen3-1.7B model to measure tok/s improvement

# PR Summary

Sci/Tech Reviewer: @harry-shepherd 
Code Reviewer: @stevemullerworth 

<!-- To be completed by the developer -->

For scalability for large rank counts of simulation ranks then it is essential that XIOS is instructed to avoid using serial netCDF calls to call `nc_open` on HDF5 encoded netCDF files.

XIOS uses MPI-IO collective calls for data interactions by default (good for scale) and provides an opt-in switch to use MPI-IO for metadata reads `read_metadata_par` [read_metadata_par](https://ipsl.pages.in2p3.fr/projets/xios-projects/xios/XIOS_reference_guide/#read_metadata_par-optional-bool) 

But, this operates on a file object, so needs to be managed many times, or deep within the LFRic interface.

This PR proposes a full opt in of this for all uses.
Preliminary analyses show that this is not problematic at small scales and very useful at large scales.

More nuanced implementations could be explored, but do not yet seem justified, compared to this simple full opt in

author: mroz22
body:
## Description Follow-up to #29082. That PR added a defensive guard in `accountsReducer.remove` so a stale or absent `removeAccount` payload becomes a no-op instead of deleting the wrong account. This PR fixes the two **upstream causes** that produce such stale payloads in the first place, so the guard becomes a safety net rather than the only thing standing between a race and a wrong deletion. ### 1. connect-popup placeholder account leak `bitcoin` / `ethereum` / `solanaSignTransaction` sign hooks create a placeholder account in `preCallHook` and push it into a module-level `temporaryAccounts` array. That array is drained **only** in `postCallHook`. If the call throws between the two hooks — e.g. `Device_Disconnected`, which `connectPopupThunks` can raise right after `preCallHooks` (`if (!device) throw TypedError('Device_Disconnected')`) or from `TrezorConnect.call` itself — `postCallHook` never runs and the placeholder leaks across calls. On a later resume a second equal placeholder is created (`createAccount` dedups it in state, but `temporaryAccounts` now holds two equal references), and the eventual `removeAccount([P, P])` carries a stale entry. Fix: extract the drain into a shared `cleanupTemporaryAccounts` and call it unconditionally from the thunk's `finally`, so the placeholder cannot survive a call regardless of how it ends. `postCallHook` keeps draining on the success path (unchanged behaviour); `finally` is the safety net for every throw path. The two drains are idempotent — at most one real `removeAccount` dispatch per call. ## Notes for QA Same hard-to-stage races as #29082, now fixed at the source. Not testable imho. --- Part of the small split-out series from #29735. Stacked on #29082. ## 🔍 Currents Test Results 🔍 **Suite native android test results:** [View in Currents](https://app.currents.dev/projects/iUe1Y4/runs?branch=mroz22/accounts-remove-followups&lookback=7) 🔍 **Suite web test results:** [View in Currents](https://app.currents.dev/projects/Og0NOQ/runs?branch=mroz22/accounts-remove-followups&lookback=7) 🔍 **Suite desktop test results:** [View in Currents](https://app.currents.dev/projects/4ytF0E/runs?branch=mroz22/accounts-remove-followups&lookback=7)

🤖 LLM Test Recommendations

 **Summary:** The changed files are connect-popup thunks and transaction-signing method hooks used when external applications invoke Trezor Connect methods through Suite. The static coverage maps nearly every test to these files, indicating they are broad global dependencies, so recommendations are limited to the single WalletConnect integration test that actually touches the Connect Popup pathway. No directly targeted sign-transaction-through-popup tests were found in the provided set.
Changed files (5) - `suite-common/connect-popup/src/connectPopupThunks.ts` - `suite-common/connect-popup/src/methodHooks/bitcoinSignTransaction.ts` - `suite-common/connect-popup/src/methodHooks/ethereumSignTransaction.ts` - `suite-common/connect-popup/src/methodHooks/index.ts` - `suite-common/connect-popup/src/methodHooks/solanaSignTransaction.ts`
**Recommended tests (1)**
🟡 Medium priority (1) - `suite/e2e/tests/analytics/wallet-connect-events.test.ts` — This is the only test in the provided set that exercises the WalletConnect integration, which is the external Connect-driven flow built on top of the suite-common/connect-popup infrastructure (connectPopupThunks and signTransaction method hooks). While the test assertions focus on pairing/proposal analytics events, the WalletConnect service imports and relies on the connect-popup machinery to handle Connect requests, making it the closest available proxy for detecting regressions in these hooks.

author: opakalex
body:
## Summary
- Adds a subprocess-style crash test that builds the real `talondb-server`, drives the adapter over TCP, SIGKILLs the server, then restarts it against the same bbolt file and verifies every Assert survives.
- Proves the typed-error contract: a post-SIGKILL Assert returns `errors.Is(err, ErrUnavailable)` so callers can branch on the sentinel instead of scraping strings.
- Adds a smaller test for the cold case (server never existed): `Health` against a dead Unix socket returns `ErrUnavailable` (or `ErrDeadlineExceeded`).

## Why TCP and not Unix sockets?
Unix-socket paths under macOS' `t.TempDir()` exceed the 104-byte `sun_path` limit. TCP `127.0.0.1:0` keeps the test portable; the port is parsed back out of the server's "ready" line.

## Problem
Weights display rounded to 0.1 in the user's unit. Editing + re-saving re-converted the *rounded* shown value back to lbs, so an unchanged edit drifted: **180 lb → 81.6 kg → 179.9 lb**.

## Fix
`resolveWeightLbs(displayValue, originalLbs, unit)` — if the shown value is unchanged from the original's rounded display, keep the original lbs exactly; only convert when the user actually changed it. Wired into `EditWeightModal` + `WeightDetail` (the bodyweight edit forms). Display keeps rounding; the stored value only changes when intended.

## Scope (from an app-wide audit)
- **Bodyweight edits** (EditWeightModal, WeightDetail): had the drift → fixed.
- **Set/target edits** (Edit/Add Workout+Program): load full precision, so **no drift** — but show ugly long kg decimals. Separate cosmetic concern, left for a follow-up.
- **ActiveWorkout/GymMode**: per-keystroke save, untouched weights aren't re-saved → negligible.

## Tests

author: nx-plugin-for-aws
body:
### Reason for this change

The PR/CI **Build** check takes ~17 minutes and is the long pole of the non-Windows jobs. Profiling a recent run showed the job is almost entirely serial:

| Step | Time |
|------|------|
| `@aws/nx-plugin:test` (2395 unit tests) | **686s** |
| `docs:build` (11 locales) | **~240s** |
| compile + lint + install | ~150s |

Two structural problems:
1. **`docs:build` serializes behind the unit tests.** `docs` statically imports `@aws/nx-plugin` *source* and the `build` target depended on `^build`, which transitively includes `test` — so docs waited ~11 min for tests it never needed.
2. **The 686s test runs on a single machine**, so the Build job can never go below ~11 min regardless of other tuning.

### Description of changes

- **Drop `test` from `@aws/nx-plugin`'s `build` target.** `build` now verifies `compile` + `lint` + `generate-3p-license`. Unit tests run as a dedicated, sharded CI job. The smoke-test artifact is produced by the `package` target, which never ran tests, so this does not affect smoke tests.
- **Set `docs:build` `dependsOn: []`.** docs imports nx-plugin source directly (compiled by astro/vite), so it never needed the plugin built. Verified locally: docs builds successfully with no `dist/`.
- **Add a `unit_tests` matrix** that shards `@aws/nx-plugin:test` 6 ways with `vitest --shard`. Each shard uploads its partial coverage to Codecov, which merges shards for the commit.
- **Add `setup-bun` / `setup-uv` / `setup-terraform` toggles** to `init-monorepo` so the build and unit-test jobs skip toolchain they don't use.
- CI `release` now depends on `unit_tests` so tests still gate releases.

Net effect: the build-set wall-clock drops from ~17 min to roughly `install + max(shard, docs)` ≈ 5-6 min, with all 2395 tests, lint, docs and coverage still running and gating the PR. (Windows smoke tests remain the overall wall-clock gate and are out of scope here.)

### Description of how you validated changes

- Profiled real CI runs to attribute time per job/step/target.
- Verified locally that `nx run-many --target build --all` no longer runs `@aws/nx-plugin:test` and still produces `docs/dist`.
- Verified `docs:build` succeeds with nx-plugin not compiled.
- Verified `vitest --shard` splits the suite and emits coverage per shard.
- CI on this PR exercises the new job topology end-to-end.

### Issue # (if applicable)
