## Summary

Adds `tests/test_e2e.py` with a single integration test `test_happy_path_publish_deliver_inspect` that exercises the full publish → worker deliver → inspect flow entirely in-process. The test provisions a project and API key via the admin endpoints, registers a webhook endpoint (capturing the signing secret), publishes an event, runs the worker with an in-process mock HTTP transport, and verifies the outbound request body, HMAC-SHA256 signature, delivery status, and attempt record — all without external network access.

Closes #41

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A new file `tests/test_e2e.py` contains at least one test named `test_happy_path_publish_deliver_inspect`
- [x] The test exercises the full flow via the FastAPI `TestClient` and the worker's `run_once()`:
  1. Creates a project and API key via `POST /projects` and `POST /projects/{id}/api-keys`
  2. Registers an endpoint via `POST /endpoints` and captures the signing secret
  3. Publishes an event via `POST /events` (with an `Idempotency-Key` header) and asserts `queued_deliveries == 1`
  4. Calls `run_once(session, http_client)` where `http_client` uses an in-process mock transport that returns 200 and captures the request
  5. Verifies the outbound request body contains the correct `event_id`, `type`, and `payload`
  6. Verifies the HMAC signature in `X-Webhook-Signature` using the captured signing secret with constant-time comparison (`hmac.compare_digest`)
  7. Calls `GET /deliveries` and asserts one delivery with `status=succeeded`
  8. Calls `GET /deliveries/{id}/attempts` and asserts one attempt with `response_status=200`
- [x] No external network access occurs (mock transport only)
- [x] The test is deterministic and runs in CI without extra setup beyond the existing Postgres service
- [x] All four quality gates pass

```
$ python -m ruff format --check .

$ python -m ruff check .

...

The E2E test skips locally when Postgres is unavailable (consistent with all other integration tests) and will run in CI where the Postgres service container is active.

**Note:** `ruff format` and `ruff check --fix` were run to correct import sorting and remove the unused `hashlib` import before final commit.

## Scope

Change is limited to a single new file `tests/test_e2e.py`. No application code modified, no new dependencies added. The `_MockTransport` class and savepoint session fixture pattern are adapted directly from `tests/test_worker.py` and `tests/test_deliveries.py`.

author: greenheadhq
body:
## Summary
- `greenhead-minipc`의 ChatGPT mobile Codex remote-control app-server를 pinned standalone package와 systemd timer로 자동 복구한다.
- stale unmanaged app-server, socket/lock 잔재, standalone PATH shadow, 버전 drift를 좁은 조건에서만 정리하도록 회귀 가드를 추가한다.
- update/verifier/docs/fixture tests를 함께 갱신해 일반 Codex CLI는 계속 Nix-managed 경로를 사용하도록 고정한다.

## 기존 문제/배경

ChatGPT mobile 앱의 Codex session sync가 한동안 정상 동작하다가 끊겼고, 조사 중 현재 Codex CLI는 최신 버전인데 app-server는 오래된 unmanaged process로 남아 있는 상태가 확인됐다.

문제는 두 가지였다.

- 일반 CLI와 mobile remote-control app-server payload가 같은 PATH 표면을 공유하면 `~/.local/bin/codex` 같은 잔재가 Nix-managed Codex를 shadow할 수 있다.
- stale app-server socket/lock과 unmanaged daemon이 남으면 `remote-control start`가 managed daemon으로 복구되지 못하고 mobile app에는 offline/연결 실패처럼 보인다.

## CIR (Change Intent Record)

- **v1 (이번 변경)**: mobile remote-control app-server를 일반 Codex CLI와 분리된 standalone payload로 관리하되, 버전 소스는 기존 `codex-pin.json` 하나로 유지하기로 했다.
- **v2 (이번 변경)**: 매 실행마다 최신 릴리스를 가져오는 방식은 재현성, hash 검증, 무인 업데이트 위험 때문에 배제했다. 대신 `update-codex`가 CLI asset hash와 standalone package hash를 함께 갱신한다.
- **v3 (이번 변경)**: stale process 정리는 자동화하되, 같은 사용자 app-server이고 legacy Codex 경로라는 per-process 증거가 있을 때만 kill하도록 제한했다. 버전 drift만으로 임의 PID를 죽이는 방식은 배제했다.
- **v4 (이번 변경)**: app-server child가 workspace 파일을 써야 하므로 service hardening은 유지하되 home 전체 read-only 정책은 쓰지 않는다. system directory는 read-only로 두고 `KillMode=process`로 oneshot 종료가 app-server child를 죽이지 않게 했다.

**trade-off**: 완전한 supervisor나 dashboard 대신 작은 timer + shell CLI만 둔다. 관측성과 자동복구 범위는 제한적이지만, 이번 회귀의 원인인 버전 drift, stale socket, PATH shadow를 직접 막고 과한 상시 daemon을 추가하지 않는다.

## ADR

| 대안 | 설명 | 장점 | 단점 | 결정 |
|------|------|------|------|------|
| pinned standalone + systemd timer | `codex-pin.json`의 standalone package를 `~/.codex/packages/standalone/current`에 동기화하고 30분 timer로 확인 | 재현 가능, NixOS에 맞음, mobile app-server와 일반 CLI 분리 | Codex release asset hash를 pin에 추가해야 함 | ✅ |
| runtime latest install | timer가 매번 최신 Codex standalone을 설치 | 구현이 단순해 보임 | 무인 latest, hash/rollback 약함, 회귀 재현 어려움 | ❌ |
| generic supervisor/fleet manager | 별도 daemon, metrics, queue, dashboard까지 추가 | 장기적으로 확장 가능 | 현재 문제 대비 과함, 운영 표면 증가 | ❌ |
| strict home read-only hardening | systemd service에서 home write를 대부분 차단 | 표면 축소 | remote-control app-server가 workspace를 쓰는 실제 사용을 깨뜨림 | ❌ |

## 구현 상세

| 파일 | 변경 | 내용 |
|------|------|------|
| `modules/nixos/programs/codex-remote-control.nix` | 추가 | NixOS option-gated service/timer, pinned standalone package fetch, credentials, hardening 설정 |
| `modules/nixos/programs/codex-remote-control/files/codex-remote-control-maint.sh` | 추가 | `probe`, `ensure-standalone`, `ensure-running`, `repair-unmanaged`, `health-json` 구현 |
| `modules/shared/programs/codex/codex-pin.json` | 수정 | `x86_64-linux` standalone package asset/hash 추가 |
| `modules/shared/scripts/update-codex.sh` | 수정 | standalone package hash도 함께 prefetch/update |
| `scripts/ai/verify-ai-compat.sh` | 수정 | 일반 `codex`가 standalone으로 resolve되면 실패 처리 |
| `modules/nixos/options/homeserver.nix`, `modules/nixos/configuration.nix` | 수정 | `homeserver.codexRemoteControl.enable` option/import/enable wiring |
| `tests/suites/codex-remote-control.sh`, `tests/shell-script-tests.sh` | 추가/수정 | daemon JSON, auth, PATH shadow, stale PID, socket cleanup, version drift fixture coverage |
| `.claude/skills/configuring-codex/*` | 수정 | remote-control standalone 예외와 운영 확인 절차 문서화 |

### 핵심 코드

```bash
# 일반 CLI는 standalone payload를 shadow하면 안 된다.
if path_under "$NORMAL_CODEX_RESOLVED" "$STANDALONE_ROOT"; then
  LAST_REPAIR_REASON="normal-codex-resolves-to-standalone"
  return "$RC_NORMAL_CODEX_STANDALONE"
fi

# connected 상태만으로 healthy 처리하지 않고 pinned version 일치까지 요구한다.
remote_start_versions_current() {
  [ "$MANAGED_CODEX_VERSION" = "$DESIRED_VERSION" ] && [ "$APP_SERVER_VERSION" = "$DESIRED_VERSION" ]
}
```

## 참고 레퍼런스

- 해당 없음. 이 PR은 로컬 mobile remote-control 회귀 조사와 복구 작업에서 나온 NixOS 구성 변경이다.

## Human Test Plan

### 자동 검증

1. `bash tests/run-shell-script-tests.sh`를 실행한다.
   - **기대**: remote-control fixtures 포함 전체 shell suite가 통과한다.
   - **실패 시**: `tests/suites/codex-remote-control.sh`의 실패 fixture와 `status.json` assertion을 먼저 확인한다.

2. `nix develop -c nix build .#nixosConfigurations.greenhead-minipc.config.system.build.toplevel --no-link`를 실행한다.
   - **기대**: NixOS system build가 성공한다.
   - **실패 시**: `codex-remote-control.nix`의 `runtimeInputs`, `fetchurl` hash, systemd option type을 확인한다.

3. `./scripts/ai/verify-ai-compat.sh`를 실행한다.
   - **기대**: 일반 `codex`는 Nix overlay/store 경로로 resolve되고, standalone payload는 관리 경로 아래에만 존재한다.
   - **실패 시**: `command -v codex`, `readlink -f ~/.codex/packages/standalone/current/bin/codex`, `~/.local/bin/codex` symlink를 확인한다.

### NixOS 활성화 검증

4. `nrs`를 실행한다.
   - **기대**: system switch가 성공하고 `codex-remote-control-ensure.timer`가 로드된다.
   - **실패 시**: build preview와 agenix credential path를 확인한다.

5. `systemctl status codex-remote-control-ensure.service codex-remote-control-ensure.timer`와 `/var/lib/codex-remote-control/status.json`을 확인한다.
   - **기대**: service `Result=success`, `exitCode=0`, `authMode=chatgpt`, `managedCodexVersion/appServerVersion`이 pinned version, `remoteControlEnabled=true`.
   - **실패 시**: `journalctl -u codex-remote-control-ensure.service -n 80 --no-pager`와 `lastRepairReason`을 확인한다.

6. `codex app-server daemon version`, `codex login status`, `codex doctor --summary --ascii --no-color`를 실행한다.
   - **기대**: app-server와 CLI version이 일치하고 ChatGPT login이며 doctor fail이 없다.
   - **실패 시**: stale socket/lock, API-key auth, PATH shadow 여부를 확인한다.

### Mobile 확인

7. ChatGPT mobile 앱의 Codex 연결 목록에서 `greenhead-minipc`를 확인하고 새 prompt를 보낸다.
   - **기대**: offline이 아니며 mobile prompt가 이 machine의 Codex session으로 동기화된다.
   - **실패 시**: status JSON의 `remoteControlEnabled`, `serverName`, `lastRepairReason`과 timer journal을 먼저 확인한다.

author: lidor0691-debug
body:
Fixes the dormant adapter so a scheduled time is persisted as the **correct UTC instant**.

## Problem
`ParsedIntent.scheduled_at_local` is a **naive Asia/Jerusalem wall-clock** ISO string (e.g. `2026-06-30T10:00:00` = 10:00 in Israel). `insert_scheduled_message` wrote it as-is into the `scheduled_at` **timestamptz** column, so Postgres assumed UTC and stored `10:00+00` — i.e. **13:00 Israel** (off by the IDT/IST offset). Observed in the controlled persist test: `scheduled_at = 2026-06-30 10:00:00+00`.

## Fix (timezone-only, stdlib)
- New `_local_to_utc_iso()` helper attaches the Asia/Jerusalem zone (**DST-aware**) and converts to UTC before insert:
  - `2026-06-30T10:00:00` (IDT, +03) → `2026-06-30T07:00:00+00:00`
  - `2026-01-15T10:00:00` (IST, +02) → `2026-01-15T08:00:00+00:00`
- `None`/empty → `None`; already tz-aware → converted to UTC (never double-localized); unparseable → returned untouched (fail-safe).
- `insert_scheduled_message` now writes `_local_to_utc_iso(intent.scheduled_at_local)`.

## Scope / non-goals
- **No schema/migration** — column is already `timestamptz`; only the written value changes.
- **No dependency change** — `zoneinfo` is stdlib.
- No parser/prompt/contract changes; no Telegram route change; no Command Core behavior change beyond the corrected persisted `scheduled_at`. `related_event_date` is a `date` → untouched.
- No backfill: the only pre-fix row is the cancelled persist-test row (harmless; left as-is).
- Not in this PR: Anthropic SDK pinning, parser-failure observability, dispatcher.

## Tests
- `pytest tests/assistant/data -q` -> **28 passed** (+7)
- `pytest tests/assistant -q` -> **165 passed** (+7)
- full suite -> **336 passed, 8 errors** (only the known pre-existing `tests/test_agent_queue.py` errors)

New tests cover summer DST, winter, None/empty, already-offset (no double-localize), unparseable, and the end-to-end insert payload.

author: raquelhandb-spec
body:
## Por que este PR

A Morning Call estava saindo com **dados inventados** (ex.: Ibovespa 136 mil quando o real era ~173 mil; PETR4/VALE3 mostrados subindo quando caíam). Este PR conserta a causa raiz e garante a regra **dado real ou nada**.

## Causa raiz (encontrada na auditoria)

1. `send-morning-call.js` buscava o brapi, logava e **descartava** os números, enviando o texto estático do `.md`.
2. `generate-morning-call.js` tinha notícias e números **hardcoded** (saíam iguais todo dia).
3. O dólar usava ticker errado (`USDBRL=X`) no endpoint errado, falhando em silêncio.

## O que muda

- **`lib/market-data.js` (novo):** endpoints corretos do brapi (`/quote` para ações e `^BVSP`; `/v2/currency` para dólar), com **Yahoo Finance como fallback automático** por ativo (sem token; cobre também NY e commodities) e **Selic oficial via API do BCB** (série 432). Se um dado obrigatório não confirma em nenhuma fonte, **aborta**.
- **`lib/news.js` (novo):** manchetes reais do dia via RSS, priorizando Investing, InfoMoney, Bloomberg Línea e CNN Brasil. Nunca inventa notícia.
- **`send-morning-call.js`:** injeta os números reais no bloco `MERCADO AGORA` antes de enviar e **aborta** se o brapi/Yahoo não confirmarem os 5 ativos.
- **`generate-morning-call.js`:** remove todo dado hardcoded; usa dados e notícias reais.
- **Workflow:** novo modo `dry_run` (valida a busca real sem enviar ao grupo).
- **Constituição (`9pilla-orchestrator.yml`):** proíbe travessão em qualquer lugar, exige voz conversacional da Raquel e não listar fonte em toda notícia.
- **Conteúdo 29/06 (Edição #153):** reescrito com dados reais e Selic 14,25% (Ata Copom 279).

## Como validar antes de confiar no 09h09

GitHub → aba **Actions** → **Morning Call 9Pilla** → **Run workflow** → branch `claude/morning-call-dna-config-aone1i` → marcar **dry_run** → Run. O log mostra os 5 ativos reais, o bloco internacional, a Selic oficial e as manchetes, sem enviar nada ao grupo.

## Observação

Os testes de lógica (formatação, injeção, fail-safe, parser de notícias) passaram localmente. A busca ao vivo (brapi/Yahoo/BCB/RSS) roda no GitHub Action, que tem rede liberada; validar pelo dry-run acima.

author: piob-io
body:
## Summary

Reduces Docker build-cache waste on Blacksmith sticky disks by addressing two of the biggest sources of recompilation in the Rust image build. The two changes are independent: one makes the dependency compile durable, the other stops the two architectures from clobbering each other's compile cache.

This is a **draft against the fork** for review — not aimed at `chroma-core/chroma` yet.

## The two changes

**cargo-chef: dependency compile becomes a durable layer** (`rust/Dockerfile`)

`rust/Dockerfile` is split into `chef` (toolchain + protoc + cargo-chef) -> `planner` (emits `recipe.json`) -> `builder` (cook deps, then build workspace):

```
FROM chef AS planner
COPY idl/ Cargo.toml Cargo.lock rust/ ./
RUN cargo chef prepare --recipe-path recipe.json      # deps graph only

FROM chef AS builder
COPY --from=planner /chroma/recipe.json recipe.json
RUN cargo chef cook ... --recipe-path recipe.json     # deps -> image LAYER (keyed on recipe.json)
COPY idl/ Cargo.toml Cargo.lock rust/ ./
RUN cargo build --workspace ...                       # only first-party crates
```

The dependency compile is no longer kept in the volatile `--mount=type=cache,target=/chroma/target` dir (which a cold or contended builder wipes). It lands in a content-addressed **layer** keyed on `recipe.json`, so an app-only source change (the common commit) reuses it. The `target/` cache mount is removed from the compile steps; cache mounts are kept only for the crate **download** dirs (`registry`/`git`). Build flags (ASAN, AVX512, release) are mirrored across cook and build so cargo's fingerprints match and deps are actually reused.

Caveat: chef caches **dependencies**, not first-party crates. The first-party (workspace) compile still relies on the cache mount surviving — which is exactly what the per-arch keys protect. The two changes pair.

**Per-arch cache keys** (`.github/actions/docker`, workflows)

Upgrades `setup-docker-builder@v1 -> v2` and threads an explicit `cache-key` through the `docker` composite action and every build/test job. The multi-arch release-cli build keys on the platform (`chroma-release-cli-${platform}`), so `amd64` and `arm64` no longer share one sticky-disk lineage and stop discarding each other's architecture-specific compile cache. CI/test jobs share one warm key (`chroma-ci-amd64`, matching the `build-images` warm-cache job); release service-images and the manifest-merge job get their own keys. The release-cli build step switches to `docker/build-push-action@v6`, which uses the per-arch builder that `setup-docker-builder@v2` sets as default.

## Validation

- `docker buildx build --check` on `rust/Dockerfile` — clean (0 warnings).
- `docker buildx bake --print` for the default group — parses.
- All edited workflow/action YAML parses.

Not run here: a full image build and CI on the fork — left for review.

author: chaz-clark
body:
## Summary

`AGENTS.md` had grown to **182 KB / ~32k tokens** — past the 25k host-tool Read limit — because its **Active Context** section became an append-only release log (**86% of the file**). That violates `make_AGENTS` Principle #2 ("Concise — Project Context, Not Documentation"). This trims it back and adds a CI guard so it can't regress.

## Changes

**AGENTS.md → 2,459 → 569 lines (~10.5k tokens)**
- Active Context keeps only the **latest 5 entries** (v0.72.2 → v0.70.0) + a one-line pointer to CHANGELOG.

**CHANGELOG.md ← the history**
- Relocated **33 older entries** (v0.69.1 → v0.57.0 + dated sprint notes), **filling the prior 0.51–0.71 gap** (CHANGELOG jumped 0.72.2 → 0.50.1 before this).
- Dropped **2 entries** that duplicated existing `[0.36]`–`[0.50.1]` content; placed the 2026-05-26 QC note chronologically.

**CI guard (the rotating-latest-5 rule)**
- `lib/tests/test_agents_active_context.py` fails if Active Context exceeds 5 `### ` entries. Runs in the required `smoke-and-unit` job. Local enforcement of the threshold proposed upstream in [Make-AI-Agents#17](https://github.com/chaz-clark/Make-AI-Agents/issues/17).
- Release workflow going forward: add the new entry on top, rotate the oldest into CHANGELOG.

**Pointer + link fixes**
- README footer + AGENTS.md pointer now send release history to `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Fixed **17 outbound links** in `docs/grading_readme.md`, `docs/UPGRADING.md`, `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md` that broke in v0.72.2 when those files left the repo root (their root-relative links weren't re-pathed then — caught now by a full link sweep).

## Not in scope (flagged)
- 8 **pre-existing** broken links remain in `lib/agents/` (e.g. `AGENT_LAYERS.md → ../AGENTS.md`, `knowledge/README.md → canvas_grader.md`) — untouched by this work, predate the session. Happy to fix in a follow-up.
- No version bump / no new Active Context entry: a 6th entry would trip the new ≤5 guard, and this is infra/cleanup. Logged under CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest` — **606 passed** (+1 new guard test); 7 pre-existing live-Canvas failures unchanged
- [x] `pre-commit` (ruff) passes
- [x] AGENTS.md now ~10.5k tokens (readable in one pass); Active Context = 5 entries
- [x] Repo-wide broken-link sweep: 0 broken from this change (8 pre-existing flagged above)

author: aisraelov
body:
Fixes three Recorder miniapp issues from incident `55285e9b-c5cf-4559-9954-3c0bee6e7efc`.

## 1. Play button gets stuck after the first play (main bug)
**Symptom:** first play looks like it's playing; tapping play on a second recording just flickers pause→play and nothing plays. You have to kill + relaunch to play anything again. The logs show a storm of play requests each interrupting the previous after ~0.5s — a button that keeps reverting, mashed.

**Cause:** `RecorderController` mirrored `speaker.onStateChange("stopped")` into the UI "playing" state. That state is **global to the miniapp** with no per-clip correlation. Starting clip B interrupts clip A (`stopOtherAudio: true`), so the host emits `"stopped"` for A *while B is starting* → it clobbers B's just-set "playing" state. Row flips to "play", user taps again, repeat.

**Fix:** playback UI state is driven solely by `play()`'s own per-request promise, guarded by a monotonic `playSeq` token so an interrupted clip's resolution can't clear a newer clip's state. Removed the `onStateChange → setPlaying(null)` clobber.

## 2. Stray "trash + progress bar" above the search bar
The Header's storage row (clear-all trash + a quota-usage bar that reads like a stray playback bar). Removed it.

## 3. Delete UX too subtle
Replaced the two-tap "trash turns red, tap again" with an explicit confirm dialog (recording name + permanent-delete warning + Cancel / Delete).

## Note on "no audio" — separate, still-open (NOT fixed here)
This PR fixes the **state-machine storm**, not audio output. Investigation of this incident (no glasses connected):
- **Phone mic was OFF** — no recording happened this session, mic was set to `false` before the recorder opened, zero `audio_chunk` subscriptions. So the dev host-side fix (mic leaves the session in `.playAndRecord`) does **not** explain this incident.
- The active output route was the **phone Speaker** (`AudioMonitor: output count: 1, Speaker`), the app was **PLAYING** (`PhoneAudioMonitor: Own app audio -> PLAYING`), `.playback` was re-asserted, volume 1.0, and one clip ran a full **15.4s** with no expo-audio idle-failure — i.e. from the host's side it *did* play to the speaker.
- So "no sound" is an **output/recordings** question, not routing and not the storm. Most likely either the specific recordings are silent or a device-volume/iOS-26.5 issue. Needs a fresh on-device test (record speaking loudly with this build, play back uninterrupted) or capture-peak/playback-duration diagnostics to close. Tracking separately.

## Rollout
Bundle rebuilt against the SDK and **`com.mentra.recorder` 1.0.1 → 1.0.2** (`MantleManager` skips a bundle when that exact version is already installed). Repacked the zip and regenerated `bundledMiniapps.ts`.

## Test
`tsc --noEmit` clean; recorder + SDK bundles build clean; `wav.test.ts` 8 pass; verified the packed zip contains the fixes.

author: copilot
body:
Frontdoor only exposed `:80` and only allowed overlays to swap `rds/active.yaml`, which was too narrow for TLS, dynamic modules, and overlay-managed cert state. This change widens the seam without baking any ACME-specific behavior into `vm`: the base now binds inert HTTPS, exposes generic module/SDS/state paths, and keeps frontdoor overlay-driven.

- **Frontdoor HTTPS base posture**
  - Add a base `:443` listener alongside `:80`.
  - Terminate TLS via filesystem SDS from a well-known overlay path.
  - Ship a placeholder self-signed cert so Envoy starts and binds `:443` cleanly on every boot.
  - Keep HTTPS inert by default with a direct `503 TLS not yet configured` response.

  ```yaml
  - "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.config.listener.v3.Listener
    name: listener_frontdoor_https
    address:
      socket_address:
        address: 0.0.0.0
        port_value: 443
    filter_chains:
    - transport_socket:
        name: envoy.transport_sockets.tls
        typed_config:
          "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.transport_sockets.tls.v3.DownstreamTlsContext
          common_tls_context:
            tls_certificate_sds_secret_configs:
            - name: frontdoor_tls_certificate
              sds_config:
                path_config_source:
                  path: /etc/envoy/sds/active.yaml
  ```

- **Overlay seam widening**
  - Preserve the existing `rds/active.yaml` spigot unchanged.
  - Add `lds/active.yaml` as the live listener seam for overlays that need to replace listener/filter shape.
  - Add `bootstrap_extensions.yaml` as a dedicated bootstrap fragment seam.
  - Add `sds/active.yaml` and `modules/` as generic TLS/module drop-in surfaces.

- **Bootstrap wiring**
  - Keep `envoy.yaml` immutable in the repo contract.
  - Render the effective bootstrap at service start from the base template plus `bootstrap_extensions.yaml`.
  - Use rendered bootstrap for startup-only fields; keep live xDS reload on filesystem for LDS/CDS/RDS/SDS.

- **Systemd / container wiring**
  - Publish `0.0.0.0:443:443` on `botwork-envoy-frontdoor.service`.
  - Mount:
    - `/etc/botwork/envoy/frontdoor/modules` → `/etc/envoy/modules`
    - `/etc/botwork/envoy/frontdoor/sds` → `/etc/envoy/sds`
    - `/var/lib/botwork/frontdoor/acme` → `/var/lib/botwork/frontdoor/acme`
  - Set `ENVOY_DYNAMIC_MODULES_SEARCH_PATH=/etc/envoy/modules`.

- **Provisioned host paths**
  - Create frontdoor module and SDS directories in the image.
  - Generate placeholder TLS material under `/etc/botwork/envoy/frontdoor/sds/`.
  - Create `/var/lib/botwork/frontdoor/acme/` as the writable frontdoor state surface, owned by `101:101`, mode `0700`.

- **Contract / docs**
  - Update frontdoor README and base image README to document:
    - inert `:443`
    - the widened overlay contract
    - atomic-rename semantics for live filesystem xDS seams
    - restart requirement for `bootstrap_extensions.yaml`

- **Design choice**
  - `bootstrap_extensions` is handled by startup-time rendering, not filesystem xDS, because Envoy consumes top-level bootstrap extensions only at process start.
  - HTTP filter injection is handled by replacing `lds/active.yaml`, not a `filters.d` splice, because Envoy v1.38 does not provide a clean additive filesystem seam for appending HCM filters.

- **Goss / base assertions**
  - Assert `:443` is published.
  - Assert the new mounts and host paths exist.
  - Assert HTTPS handshake succeeds and returns the inert `503`.
  - Assert the ACME state dir owner/mode.

### Motivation
- Ensure the public `/e-proposal/:token` page displays the exact same currency, item grouping, line totals, subtotal, discount and grand total as the internal ERP proposal preview without reimplementing separate calculation logic.
- Avoid incorrect fallbacks (hardcoded `EUR`, duplicated/raw totals, or double-multiplied annual/one-time amounts) by reusing the same formatter and total-selection rules used by internal preview rendering.

- Replaced the public page's independent rendering with an embedded ERP preview by generating the same proposal HTML via `buildProposalDocumentHtml` and injecting it into an iframe on the public page, preserving public actions (accept/reject/print) while removing duplicated calculation code.

yvette-carlisle
body:
## Summary
- terminal-guard terminal-looking stale-active run statuses (`failed`, `interrupted`) before the final label-release safety check
- preserve the existing fail-closed release guards instead of path-based cleanup or ignoring old child/protocol telemetry
- document the recovery ownership handoff in the lane-control spec and runbook

## Research / architecture
The apply-time failure is not caused by stale worktree paths alone. Real release writes local cleanup/audit evidence, then performs a final refreshed stale-active diagnostic before mutating Linear labels. Persisted child/protocol/protocol-event summaries can still be visible at that point. The existing final reentry path already accepts old telemetry only when the same run is `terminal_guarded` and the release audit/worktree/lineage guards prove recovery ownership. App-server terminal-looking failures (`failed`, `interrupted`) were missing from the terminal-guard predicate, so final safety still treated their old telemetry as active progress.

The fix keeps all existing guards: run lease, shared claim, process liveness, worktree progress, private progress evidence, PR/review lineage, review-policy checkpoints, needs-attention labels, and tracker label readback. It only expands which stale attempt statuses can be converted to `terminal_guarded` after those guards are clean.

## Review
- read-only subagent review found one P3: add `interrupted` coverage alongside `failed`
- fixed by converting the regression into a two-status table test

## Validation
- `git diff --check`
- `cargo test -p decodex stale_active_release_terminal_guards_terminal_looking_run_before_final_safety_check -- --nocapture`
- `cargo test -p decodex stale_active_release -- --nocapture`

author: tranquil-flow
body:
## Summary

A profile-scoped cron job (`profile: <name>`) fires with profile-switched context, so `_get_hermes_home()` returns the profile-local home (`~/.hermes/profiles/<name>`). The script-path guard in `_run_job_script` only knew about `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/scripts/` and hard-rejected any reference to a shared script living in the canonical default-profile scripts dir (`~/.hermes/scripts/`) — for relative names, absolute paths, **and** profile-local symlinks whose realpath lands in the root dir. This is the inverse of #32091: routing `profile: <name>` jobs through the default scheduler narrowed script resolution to the profile-local dir, silently breaking every shared-script reference on every tick.

## Root cause

`cron/scheduler.py::_run_job_script` built a single `scripts_dir = _get_hermes_home()/scripts` and rejected any resolved path not `relative_to()` it. Under profile switch `_get_hermes_home()` is `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>`, so the canonical `~/.hermes/scripts/` was always "outside".

## Fix

Allow scripts that resolve within **either** the active (profile-scoped) scripts dir **or** the canonical root scripts dir (`get_default_hermes_root()/scripts`). Relative names search the profile-local dir first (per-profile overrides win), then the root dir. The resolved realpath (symlinks followed) is validated against **any** allowed root, so a profile-local symlink whose target is in the root dir is accepted while symlink-escape to outside both roots stays blocked. `get_default_hermes_root()` honours custom/Docker `HERMES_HOME` layouts and walks a profile home up to its root — more correct than hardcoding `Path.home()`.

### Behaviour table

| `script` field | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `collector.py` (relative, only in root dir) | ❌ Blocked | ✅ Runs |
| `/home/USER/.hermes/scripts/collector.py` (absolute, in root dir) | ❌ Blocked | ✅ Runs |
| `link.py` (profile-local symlink → root script) | ❌ Blocked | ✅ Runs |
| `dup.py` (in both dirs) | profile-local | profile-local (precedence preserved) |
| `/tmp/evil.py` (outside both) | ❌ Blocked | ❌ Blocked |
| `../../etc/passwd` (traversal) | ❌ Blocked | ❌ Blocked |

## How verified

- **RED phase**: 3 of 8 new regression tests FAIL on pristine upstream/main (commit 929dd9c0d), proving the bug.
- **GREEN phase**: all 8 pass after the fix.
- **Security regression**: all 9 existing `TestScriptPathContainment` tests still pass (absolute-outside, `/tmp`, `~` expansion, `~` traversal, `../../` traversal, subdirs, symlink-escape).
- 1 pre-existing failure (`test_script_timeout`) — conftest live-system guard blocks `os.kill`; identical on pristine upstream/main, unrelated to this change (touches only path resolution, before any subprocess/timeout logic).

```
tests/cron/test_cron_script.py: 44 passed, 1 failed (pre-existing test_script_timeout)
```

author: abdr007
body:
Closes the **top pre-mainnet blocker** flagged in the 2026-06 deep audit (`docs/PIN_AUDIT_2026-06.md`): the Pinocchio settlement path computed realized PnL / funding but never **materialized** them into spendable collateral. Faithful port of anchor's Phase-2g (mapped from `programs/flash-book/src/lib.rs`, not guessed). Edits the pin crate only.

## R1 — realized PnL → collateral (`b2bbc0a`)
- Each fill's realized-PnL delta is folded into the correct bucket (isolated=position / cross=trader_state, sampled pre-resize): **gain credits, loss debits**. Previously a closed loss never debited collateral (→ bad debt) and a closed gain never credited it (→ unwithdrawable).
- A loss beyond the bucket **drains it to 0 and draws the shortfall from insurance** (`balance -= covered`, `total_payouts += covered`), uncovered remainder → ADL — the anchor bad-debt waterfall.
- Fixed the latent **AUDIT-H-1** scaling bug: realized PnL now carries the `× tick_size` factor that unrealized PnL (`risk.rs`) + funding use (harmless before only because the field was never materialized).
- Fees reordered **before** the resize (anchor order) so a close-at-a-loss still pays its fee.

## R2 — funding settle-before-resize (`21dbf05`)
- Extracted the funding math into one shared `funding::settle_position_funding` helper (mark-priced notional, isolated/cross routing, residual move `Δcollateral == −Δresidual`, re-stamp, pay clamped to availability). `settle_funding` now calls it ⇒ the crank and the inline settle can't diverge.
- `apply_fill`/`apply_flp_fill` settle each leg's funding on its **pre-trade size** before the resize, gated on an **optional** trailing `haircut_state` account (mirrors anchor's `market_haircut.is_some()` gate). **Backward-compatible** — legacy 6/7-account callers are unchanged. Stops the post-add size being charged funding for the prior interval (phantom-funding).

## Verification
`cargo build-sbf` clean · **481 host + 68 integration + 25 Kani** all green. New tests:
- `route_realized_pnl_gain_loss_and_bankruptcy`, `realized_pnl_returns_delta_and_scales_with_tick`, `settle_position_funding_routes_and_restamps`
- e2e: `apply_flp_fill_materializes_realized_gain_into_collateral` (5000→5200), `apply_flp_fill_bankrupt_loss_drains_bucket_and_insurance` (bucket→0, insurance 100→50), `apply_flp_fill_settles_funding_before_resize` (funding on pre-add size 10 ⇒ 100, not post-add 20 ⇒ 200; residual moved by RISK-1)
- Kani: `route_realized_pnl_conserves` (`removed + shortfall == |loss|`) — 25th pin harness

Scope note: `flash-book-pin` remains devnet/WIP/UNAUDITED. This closes R1/R2; remaining downstream items (per-market FLP v3 par-redemption, dead `compute_shortfall`) are documented in `PIN_AUDIT_2026-06.md`.

💡 **What**:
- Cached intermediate resized `Image` objects in a dictionary keyed by `(w, h)` dimensions within `optimize_image.py`.
- Checked and reused the cached 1920px image for the fallback JPEG generation.
- Converted images to 'RGB' mode prior to saving as JPEG to prevent crashes for non-RGB images (e.g., RGBA).
- Broadened exception handling when opening the image file to properly catch `UnidentifiedImageError` and other potential corrupt file issues, rather than just `FileNotFoundError`.
- Fixed out-of-scope broken tests in `navbar.test.js` and `test_verify_frontend.py` to ensure local tests pass cleanly.
- Updated `test_optimize_image.py` to verify the reduced `resize()` call count and injected a `MagicMock` for `PIL` to prevent import failures in testing environments.
- Added a journal entry to `.jules/bolt.md` documenting these optimizations.

🎯 **Why**:
- Re-running `.resize()` with `LANCZOS` resampling on large images is computationally expensive. Re-using the previously calculated 1920xH image prevents duplicate work.
- The previous implementation would crash if the input image had an alpha channel when trying to save the fallback JPEG.
- More robust error handling prevents the script from crashing unexpectedly if a corrupted or non-image file is provided.
- Ensure the test suite always runs successfully.

📊 **Impact**: 
- Reduces the number of expensive `Image.resize()` operations from 5 to 4 for the 1920px fallback.
- Improves script reliability when handling various image formats.

🔬 **Measurement**: 
Run `python3 -m unittest test_optimize_image.py` and verify all tests pass, specifically confirming the `resize()` call count is exactly 4. Run `node navbar.test.js` and `python3 -m unittest test_verify_frontend.py` to ensure the entire local test suite is passing.

author: ronturetzky
body:
Closes #108.

A self-contained flow for ERC-20 reimbursements paid from the org's Safe multisig. Separate `safe_payouts` table — the existing `expenses` lifecycle and its IPC handlers are **untouched**. No approval tiers: the Safe signer threshold is the only approval; the agent is a **PROPOSER ONLY** (proposes, never confirms or executes), and chat merely mirrors observed on-chain state.

## What's in it
- **`src/safe/payout.ts`** — deterministic core (EIP-55 validation, ERC-20 transfer encoding, amount parse/format, idempotent mirror state machine, SafeWallet link) + unit tests.
- **`src/safe/proposer.ts`** — thin Safe SDK adapter (protocol-kit v8 / api-kit v5, dynamic-imported); the only code that touches the proposer key or network.
- **`src/safe/recipient.ts`** — resolve + validate payout address from member-profile frontmatter; refuse on missing/malformed.
- **`src/integrations/safe-payouts.ts`** — dormant-unless-configured reconcile loop; durability via the table + idempotent reconcile, not a sidecar.
- **`src/db.ts`** — `safe_payouts` table + helpers. **`src/profile.ts`** — `safe` config block (addresses from config; proposer key from `SAFE_PROPOSER_KEY` env/vault).
- **`ipc.ts` + agent-runner `request_safe_payout` MCP tool** — additive trigger.
- Docs/skill: `rules/finance/safe-payouts.md`, `expenses.md` cross-link, schema, container skill.

## Trust boundary
The proposer is a **non-owner delegate** — its signature does not count toward the Safe threshold and it can never call `confirmTransaction`/`executeTransaction`. Worst case if the key leaks is spam proposals the signers reject; it can never move funds. The key comes from env/vault, never config or git.

## Live verification
Propose + read-back validated end-to-end against a real Gnosis test Safe (`0xa612A2…403801`, threshold 1):
- Proposed `transfer(recipient, amount)` → accepted by the Gnosis Transaction Service; deterministic `safeTxHash` matches what the service indexed.
- Non-owner proposer `senderSignature` is accepted; `confirmations: 0` post-propose confirms the proposer signature does **not** count toward threshold (proposer-only).
- `fetchTxState` reads the tx back correctly, feeding the reconcile/mirror loop.

api-kit v5 requires either an explicit `txServiceUrl` or a Safe API key — for Gnosis we set `txServiceUrl: https://safe-transaction-gnosis-chain.safe.global/api` (works keyless).

## Rollout (host, gitignored)
Add a `safe` block to the active `profile.config.json` + `SAFE_PROPOSER_KEY` in the vault. Dormant until configured.

author: jakubanderwald
body:
<!-- drafto-factory-pr -->

Closes #551

## Summary

macOS notes opened blank in the editor even though their content was present and valid in the local DB. The content-load effect gated `setContent` on a hand-rolled poll of `editor.getJSON()` — but a resolved `getJSON()` only proves the WebView bridge can round-trip a message, not that the ProseMirror view is mounted and able to accept `setContent`. On macOS the gap between those two moments left the first `setContent` silently dropped, so the body rendered empty. This gates the load on tentap's real `isReady` editor-state signal instead. ([approved plan](https://github.com/JakubAnderwald/drafto/issues/551#issuecomment-4832408627))

## Parity report

Scoped to **desktop** per the issue's "Affected platforms" checkbox (web + mobile load content correctly today and are unchanged). The fix lives entirely in the desktop content-load path; the shared `contentToTiptap` / `resolveTipTapImageUrls` converters are unchanged, so there is no cross-platform blast radius.

- desktop — `apps/desktop/src/components/notes/note-editor-panel.tsx` + new `note-content-loader.ts` ✅
- web — no change (reference implementation for correct behaviour)
- mobile — no change (shares `db/` with desktop; loads correctly)

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @drafto/desktop test` — 294 pass (13 new in `note-content-loader.test.ts`)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @drafto/desktop typecheck` — passed
- [x] `pnpm --filter @drafto/desktop lint` — passed
- [x] `prettier --check` — passed
- [ ] **On-device (In Test gate):** open a pre-existing note with real content on a macOS build and confirm the body renders. The desktop app has no automated E2E, and the approved plan defines "done" as on-device observation — **please verify this in the In Test preview before approving.**

## Diagnosis notes (what the static analysis changed)

- The plan's *secondary* hypothesis — "a single `getSignedUrl` rejection blanks the whole note" — is **refuted by the code**: `resolveTipTapImageUrls` already wraps every URL in `Promise.allSettled`, so a failed image URL keeps its `attachment://` src and cannot reject the load.
- The schema-mismatch hypothesis is **mostly refuted**: the tentap WebView bundle registers `image`/`table`/`taskList`/`heading`/lists. (`codeBlock` is genuinely absent from the bundle — a narrow edge intentionally **not** touched here, since stripping nodes would risk the data-loss invariant.)
- The remaining, strongest cause is the readiness gate, which this PR fixes.

## Data-loss invariant (preserved)

The gated `catch` in the load effect — which keeps the autosave gate (`loadedNoteIdRef`) **closed** on load failure so an empty bootstrap `onChange` can never overwrite real DB content (the 2026-04-24 / 2026-04-27 incidents) — is **unchanged**. The new image-resolution fallback only degrades images to a placeholder; `attachment://` is the canonical stored form, so the unresolved doc round-trips without corruption.

## Drift vs. approved plan

Matches the plan's "Files to touch" (`note-editor-panel.tsx`, with `resolve-urls.ts` inspected-only and left unedited). One addition beyond the listed files: a new pure helper `apps/desktop/src/components/notes/note-content-loader.ts`, extracted so the content-load branch is unit-testable without the WebView bridge (the plan explicitly anticipated a content-load-branch test). `note-editor.tsx` was inspected but needed no change — the readiness fix lives in the panel's gate, not the WebView mount.

body:
## Fix: md-health false-positive on the generated `sessions/INDEX.md`

The eq-context `health` check has been **red on every PR and the nightly cron** — a permanently-failing signal that trains everyone to ignore it.

### Cause
Rule 17.4 (`.github/workflows/md-health.yml`) requires every `sessions/*.md` to match `YYYY-MM-DD[-slug].md`. But `sessions/INDEX.md` is the session index **generated by `scripts/generate_session_index.py`**, not a session log — so it's flagged as non-canonical.

### Fix
- `md-health.yml` rule 17.4 — allow `INDEX.md` in the regex.
- `scripts/md-health-daily.py` — the same check is duplicated here with an even stricter regex (`^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\.md$`, no `-slug`), so it was **additionally** over-flagging legitimate suffixed logs like `2026-05-20-part-b.md`. Aligned it to the workflow's pattern.

### Verification
- Full md-health rule set run locally: **0 violations, "All MD health checks passed."**
- Regex matches `INDEX.md`, `2026-05-20.md`, `2026-05-20-part-b.md`; rejects arbitrary names.
- This workflow self-runs on the PR — expect `health` finally green.

author: sdomit
body:
## Mini Controller

A small always-on-top "desk knob" window: two knobs (default **Speaker** + **Mic**) with **center-press mute**, quick-switch of the OS default device, summoned by a global shortcut (**Ctrl+Shift+P**), plus a phone remote. Plan + critique live in `docs/PLAN-mini-controller.md`.

> **Stacked on #83** (Phase 13/14/16) — this branch was based on that tip, so the base here is `claude/pedantic-clarke-9c58f3`. GitHub auto-retargets this to `main` when #83 merges. Review here is the 14 Mini Controller commits only.

### Phases
- **MC-1** OS endpoint control — Core Audio `IAudioEndpointVolume` + the undocumented `IPolicyConfig::SetDefaultEndpoint` (hand-declared COM vtable). Free functions, no `AppState`.
- **MC-2** `Knob` + `MiniPanel` (arc dial, center mute zone).
- **MC-3** always-on-top pop-out window (`#mini` route, runtime `WebviewWindow`).
- **MC-4** global shortcut — Ctrl+Shift+P, fallback chain, `get_mini_hotkey` so the overlay shows the real combo.
- **MC-5** phone remote — additive signaling protocol (`SetEndpointVolume/Mute`, `RequestEndpointState`, `EndpointState`), strictly gated on an **accepted** session.
- **Redesign** (live feedback): separate-window-only, center-press mute, draggable title bar, tighter UI.

### Live-verified on Windows 11 (real hardware)
- Builds + launches clean (capability config valid).
- **COM layer non-destructive smoke** (`cargo test -- --ignored endpoint_ctl_smoke`): enumerated 7 render + 4 capture endpoints, read real volumes, and every write returned `Ok` — **including `IPolicyConfig::SetDefaultEndpoint`** (called with the already-default id → no system change). Clears the feature's #1 risk.
- Global hotkey registers live (Ctrl+Shift+P).
- **Center-press mute + window drag** confirmed in the running app.
- 294 Rust tests + 205 frontend tests green; `tsc` / `cargo check` / `build:phone` clean.

### Known limitations (from self-critique)
- Endpoint state is **polled, not pushed** — `IAudioEndpointVolumeCallback` is the v2 efficiency follow-up. Mitigated (hidden-window guard, 250ms, drag-race guard).
- Phone can **volume/mute only** (no default-device switch — deliberate), strictly accepted-gated.
- Phone remote **not yet device-tested end-to-end** (needs a paired phone + firewall 47800-47809).

### Reviewer / acceptance checklist
- [ ] 🎛 (bottom-right) or **Ctrl+Shift+P** opens the always-on-top window
- [ ] knob ring drag / wheel = volume; **press the center** = mute that channel
- [ ] drag the **title bar** to move the window
- [ ] default-device dropdowns switch the OS default speaker/mic
- [ ] phone: pair → accept → "Desktop volume" panel drives this PC

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary
Consolidation + a faithful backup of the **two live production servers** + one real production fix.

### 1. Consolidation (non-destructive monorepo)
Each source repo → its own self-contained folder under `apps/` (nothing overwritten/cross-merged). Only git-tracked files copied; excluded committed `node_modules` (~205 MB) + 3× 51 MB junk PDFs. Adds root `.gitignore` + master `README.md`.

### 2. Live server backups → `live-server/srv1148455/` + `live-server/srv1782156/`
Both VPS run a **much newer/larger Oscar** than `apps/` (live `chat_server.py` ≈ **9,514 lines** vs **531** in the repo). Pulled the real running source into the repo so the master reflects what's actually deployed. Per server: `code/{oscar,intel,royalty-app,halito-chat,www-goat}` + `systemd/` units + `nginx/` configs (+ prod `docker/traefik/`).
- The two servers' Oscar is **byte-identical**; `srv1782156` ("staging") additionally has a more developed Halito chat (`command-center.html`, `pilot.html`, `prototype.html`).
- **Scrubbed before commit:** a live **xAI API key** in `intel/local_keys.json` → `.example` (⚠️ rotate it); `intel/fans.db` (PII); `oscar/chat_data/` (private chats); `__pycache__`/caches/backups and a 36 MB `.mp4`. Final `git diff` secret-scan = 0 hits.

### 3. Production fix: killed the Traefik crash loop (`srv1148455`)
Ingress is **nginx**, not Traefik. The Traefik container had restarted **66,870×** (couldn't bind :80/:443 — nginx owns them) and routed nothing. **Stopped it + set `restart=no`** — no downtime; sites verified still serving (`goat` 200, `anigoalley` 301, `casino` 200), Oscar healthy (`/api/stats` 200). (`srv1782156` has no Traefik — nothing to fix.)

### On the earlier Oscar "bug fixes"
They targeted the **old 531-line** `apps/` Oscar. The **real 9,514-line** Oscar already has a configurable Ollama host and robust `realpath`+`commonpath` traversal guards with private-dir denial — those bugs **don't exist** there. All 4 services on both servers are healthy (0 error restarts), so I deliberately **did not churn the working production code**.

## Verification
- `apps/` deep sweep: `bash -n` 139 `.sh` + 10 `.command` → 0 errors; `py_compile` all `.py` → 0 errors.
- Real Oscar `py_compile` OK; reviewed routing + static-file serving (secure).
- Both servers inspected; only change applied = stopping the dead Traefik container on prod.

## Notes
- Plain file copy — per-repo git history not preserved.
- `live-server/` is a point-in-time snapshot (2026-06-29); redeploying to a server is a separate deliberate step.

author: cph5236
body:
Implements the **local/reversible** half of the [d1-sharding-kv-cache plan](docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-24-d1-sharding-kv-cache.md). Live provisioning and the prod data move are deferred to a runbook (irreversible, human-run).

## What's in this PR (code/config only)
- **`wrangler.toml`** — replaced the single `DB` binding with four domain D1 bindings (`DB_HEAP` / `DB_SCORES` / `DB_REWARDS` / `DB_TELEMETRY`) + a `CACHE` KV namespace. **IDs are placeholders** (`<heap_core-id>`, etc.) until provisioning.
- **Migrations** — per-DB `migrations/<db>/0001_init.sql` with consolidated final-state DDL. Legacy flat migrations moved to `migrations/_legacy_heap/` (now unreferenced; kept for the retiring `heap` DB).
- **Schema** — split into `server/schema/<db>.sql`; `schema.sql` is now an index pointing at them.
- **Cache decorators** — `CachedHeapDB` + `CachedScoreDB` wrap the existing repo interfaces: cache-aside reads (`waitUntil` populate), write-through invalidation (D1 first, then synchronous KV delete). No route/test changes.
- **`index.ts`** — four-DB `Env` + `CACHE`, `ctx.waitUntil`, composes decorators; telemetry + reward codes stay D1-direct.
- **CI** — `migrate-d1.yml` loops all four databases.
- **Runbook** — `docs/superpowers/runbooks/d1-sharding-kv-cache.md`: `wrangler d1/kv create`, gated prod data move (row-count check before retiring `heap`), manual KV verification.

## Deferred to the runbook (NOT in this PR)
- Creating the real D1 databases / KV namespace and pasting in IDs.
- The one-time production data export/import + retiring the old `heap` DB.

## Deliberate deviation from the plan
`CachedScoreDB` caches the **top-N (50) per heap under a single key** and slices to the requested limit, instead of the plan's literal `cache:scores:{heapId}:top:{limit}`. KV has no cheap prefix-delete, so a per-limit key can't be fully invalidated on write; the single-key approach keeps writes consistent with one delete. Limits > 50 bypass the cache.

## Verification
- `npm run build` (CI gate) — green.
- `cd server && npm test` — 195/195 passing (decorators sit behind unchanged interfaces; mocks unaffected).

author: zauni1984
body:
Multi-agent code review pass (3 parallel reviewers: backend auth/posts, backend services/e2ee, frontend) + a daily test-bot system.

## Bug fixes

### Permanent posts (root cause of "shows in global feed, not on Permanent page")
- **Frontend**: the 📌 button opened an *NFT price modal* and only set `is_permanent` as a side effect of `_postIsNFT`, so a post the user marked permanent usually went out as a normal 24h post and never appeared on the Permanent Posts page. It is now a dedicated `_postIsPermanent` toggle with clear on/off feedback on the actual button.
- **Backend** `create_post` bound the raw `is_permanent` while deriving the 100‑year `expires_at` from `is_permanent || is_nft` — so NFT posts lived forever in the feed but were invisible to the permanent list. Now binds the computed value; mirrored in `scheduled_posts` + the publish job.
- **Migration 0036** backfills existing `is_nft` posts to `is_permanent = TRUE`.
- `get_permanent_posts` now also filters `deleted_at IS NULL`; the feed `total` count now matches the list query's permanent‑24h window.

### Wallet auth resolution (wallet users got 401 / silent no-ops)
- `permanent.rs` parsed a `0x` address as a UUID → `update_post_visibility` / `repost_post` always 401'd for wallet users. Now resolves via DB.
- `unlike_post` fell back to `Uuid::nil()` for wallet users (could never unlike). Now resolves via DB.
- `verify_signature` validates the address shape before the `&address[2..10]` byte slice (latent panic).

### Security / correctness
- **Stored XSS**: escape user-controlled `display_name`/`username` in feed + profile post rendering (a crafted display name like ``'<img src=x onerror=…>'`` executed for every viewer).
- Session restore reads `yeet_jwt`/`yt` too, not just `yeetToken` (wallet logins looked logged-out on reload).
- Post/comment length checks count characters, not UTF-8 bytes (emoji/umlauts were rejected well before 280 visible chars).
- `batch_rewards` builds recipients/amounts/actions in one pass (can't desync) and only marks the ids actually included in the tx as minted; guards the `f64 -> u128` wei cast against non-finite/negative.
- `e2ee` `get_prekey_bundles` no longer burns a one-time prekey for a device with no active signed prekey (OTP-pool drain).
- `cache.incr` re-arms the TTL every hit (an INCR-without-EXPIRE crash could otherwise leave a key with no expiry → permanent rate-limit lockout).

Clippy `-D warnings` passes locally; backend compiles clean.

## Test bots (`bots/` + `.github/workflows/bots.yml`)
Deterministic HD-wallet bots (25 personas) that authenticate via the wallet flow (no email needed), post a daily message (~15% permanent), and interact — like ~3, comment ~1, follow up to 2 other bots. Runs daily at 09:13 UTC + manual dispatch. `BOT_SEED` secret pins private identities; falls back to a built-in test mnemonic out of the box. See `bots/README.md`.

## Test plan
- [ ] Mark a post permanent with 📌 (button highlights, "Permanent post set" badge shows) → post appears under Permanent Posts.
- [ ] Existing NFT/permanent posts appear under Permanent Posts after migration 0036.
- [ ] Wallet user can change permanent-post visibility, repost, and unlike.
- [ ] A display name containing HTML renders as text, not markup.
- [ ] Trigger the bots workflow manually → bots post + interact on justyeet.it.

author: rgx01
body:
## [3.0.4] — 2026-06-29

*Completes the Intelligent dispatch API migration begun in 3.0.3. No change to how charges are priced for current setups — the same smart-charge slots are detected, now via Octopus's current API.*

### Changed

- **Migrated Intelligent planned dispatches to `flexPlannedDispatches`** — Octopus deprecated the `plannedDispatches` field (scheduled for removal) in favour of `flexPlannedDispatches`, which is keyed by the charge-point device rather than the account and reports `type`/`energyAddedKwh` in place of `meta.source`/`delta`. EMT now discovers the charge-point device id and queries the new field, mapping it back to the same internal shape. Verified against live data (planned-slot and smart-slot counts matched the old field exactly through a real charging schedule) before the old field was removed.
- **Smart-charge detection now recognises both API vocabularies** — the dispatch source is matched against `smart-charge` (legacy) and `smart` (flex), so detection is correct regardless of which spelling Octopus returns. Boost/bump dispatches (`bump-charge`/`boost`) remain excluded from off-peak, as before.
- **Dispatch slot times moved to `start`/`end`** — off the deprecated `startDt`/`endDt` fields (same values, current field names).

### Fixed

- **Deprecation self-check no longer over-reports on generic field names** — fields like `id` exist on nearly every schema type, so name-only matching flagged unrelated deprecations (ledgers, payments) EMT never uses. Generic names are now matched only on the specific types EMT actually reads them from, so the count reflects fields EMT genuinely depends on. With this migration complete, EMT uses no deprecated API fields, so the deprecation notification clears itself.

body:
## Description

This PR contains the scripts and modifications for the kickoff iterations study. These include:

- A yml file with the parameters (kickoff_iterations_params.yml)
- A modified control strategy yml that is more aggressive (cstrat_nfov_band1.yaml)
- A script for generating comparison plots (CompareRunResults.py)
- Modifications to nulling_gitl.py to apply DM PMN creep and hysteresis and to calculate and apply Z6 to a DM
- Modifications to run_corgisim_nulling_gitl.py to incorporate the arguments for the kickoff iterations study

The kickoff iterations study currently includes DM PMN creep, DM hysteresis, 30 nm focus on the primary, 2.5 nm Z6 on DM1, 2.5 nm Z6 on DM2, LS misalignment, FSAM misalignment, and source/FPM shifts.

An example contrast vs. iteration plot is provided below.

## Summary

- **TerminalSize**: Reports terminal dimensions (columns × rows) via `ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)` on Linux/macOS; falls back to `$COLUMNS`/`$LINES`. Returns nothing when stdout is not a TTY (piped output).
- **DNS**: Parses configured nameservers from `/etc/resolv.conf` (Linux/macOS); PowerShell `Get-DnsClientServerAddress` on Windows.
- **WM**: Detects the active window manager by scanning `/proc` for known Wayland compositor and X11 WM process names. Suppressed from output when it would duplicate the Desktop field (case-insensitive match).
- **Shell fix**: Shell detection now walks the process tree first to find the *running* shell, falling back to `$SHELL` (login shell) only when the scan yields nothing. Previously `$SHELL` was always used, which reports the login shell regardless of what's actually running.
- **Desktop fix**: Desktop detection now tries `XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP` and `GDMSESSION` as additional env var fallbacks, normalizes DE names to canonical casing (e.g. `gnome` → `GNOME`), and falls back to scanning `/proc` for known DE processes (e.g. `gnome-shell` → `GNOME`) when no env var is set. Fixes missing Desktop field in terminals that don't inherit the full session environment.

author: emson
body:
A four-agent review (core/concurrency, security/side-effects, rendering/hot-path, docs) found a set of issues. This PR applies only the **significant** ones (real bugs, an invariant violation, and clean consistency/robustness wins) and skips the marginal.

## Bugs fixed
- **`pomo log open` crash** on a missing or multi-word `$EDITOR` (e.g. `code -w`): it emitted an unhandled `'error'`. Now degrades to printing the path.
- **`dateOf` threw** on a record with a missing/garbage `started` (`new Date(NaN).toISOString()`), crashing `pomo status`/undo. Now a total function.
- **`readState` could leak `NaN`** from a valid-but-partial state. Now merged over `IDLE_STATE` defaults.
- **Help/log/restore columns misaligned on a color TTY** (`row()` measured invisible ANSI bytes). Fixed with a visible-width measure.
- **`statusline` with empty `COLUMNS=''`** computed `NaN` and silently dropped the bar/dots. Guarded.
- **macOS notification lost** when a label contained a newline. Control chars are now stripped.

## Invariant fix (significant)
- **`pomo uninstall` left a running timer orphaned** — the detached worker kept firing and (in auto mode) auto-cycling forever, and could even resurrect the data dir after `--purge`. Uninstall now disarms first (idle + `alarm_seq` bump) so workers self-exit. Upholds the "no orphaned processes after uninstall" non-negotiable.
- **`setup` could make uninstall un-cleanable**: re-running after a lost manifest captured Claudoro's *own* statusLine as `previous`. Now self-recognized; also reports honestly (no false success) when `settings.json` is unparseable.

## Consistency / robustness
- One shared `formatFocusMin` feeds both the terminal stats panel and the HTML dashboard (they were forked); `foldRecords` no longer derives a divergent, unused cycle position (`deriveCadence` is the single source).
- `kill-all`: tightened the `pkill` pattern (anchored on `node ... _alarm-worker.js`, so it can't kill an editor/grep open on the file) and honest Windows messaging.
- New `pomo version` / `--version` / `-v` (also fixes the bug-report template).
- Docs sweep: published-state wording, `note`/`tag`/`label`/`version` verbs + `CLAUDORO_EMOJI`/`CLAUDORO_LINKS` documented, unimplemented `CLAUDORO_MOTION` removed, D-001..D-012 range, `plugin.json` version synced, release workflow `checkout` aligned with CI, hyphen changelog headings.

## Deliberately skipped (not significant / risk>reward)
- Extracting color primitives out of `output.js` to keep it off the hot path — **measured at ~1ms** of a ~40ms tick (Node startup dominates); not worth the cross-file churn.
- Making `appendRecord` async+locked — the detached worker relies on its synchronous nature; converting it would risk a lost-record bug for a rare concurrency gain. Fixed the *misleading comment* instead.
- The stale-lock TOCTOU (needs a >10s critical section; ops are sub-second), cosmetic heatmap/status-word differences, astronomically-rare record-id collision.

## Test plan
`npm run check` green: lint, format, typecheck, **318 tests** (+11). New tests cover `dateOf`/`foldRecords` no-throw, `readState` merge, uninstall disarm, setup self-recognition, and `pomo version`.

Changes are under `[Unreleased]` (no version bump) per the "apply to a branch" request.

body:
## Summary
Two features for the BMO Discord social-bot music system.

### Feature 1 — Autoplay "radio" on empty queue (default ON)
When the visible queue runs dry, BMO fills the dead air with a related track.
- Radio picks live in an **invisible reservoir** (`MusicQueue.autoplay_pool`), are **never** added to `queue.tracks`, so they never appear in the queue display and are never persisted (e.g. `/playlist save`).
- `_on_track_end` drains real user requests (`queue.next()`) **before** consulting the reservoir, so autoplay can never preempt or jump ahead of a requested song.
- Toggle via `/autoplay` or the new panel **Radio** button. Default ON.

### Feature 2 — Fast queue-clear / jump (no more 50× Skip)
- `/clearqueue` + panel **Clear Queue** button: empty the upcoming queue in one action; current track keeps playing.
- `/playnow <query>`: play a song immediately, jumping ahead of the queue.
- `/removerange <start> <end>`: drop a contiguous block of tracks.

### Tests
`tests/test_social_music_queue.py` — invisibility, request-priority, off-switch, command + panel surface.

Local: ruff clean, print/literal ratchets pass, full `pytest tests/` = 1399 passed / 6 skipped.

## Summary

Follow-up fix to PR #512. The custom Cooldown Manager frames (Trinket Slot 1, racial/placeholder, item presets, and custom spells) did not behave correctly with the **Tooltip → Anchor to Cursor** option:

- Their tooltips bypassed the global **Show Tooltips** mode (showing/hiding inverse to the setting, e.g. visible on "Never" and hidden on "Always").
- With "Anchor to Cursor" enabled, the trinket tooltip frequently failed to render at all because `SetInventoryItem`/`SetItemByID` do not auto-show under `ANCHOR_NONE`, and the cursor-tracking frame was not yet positioned when content was set synchronously.

## Changes

**EllesmereUIBlizzardSkin**
- Added `PositionCursorFrameNow` to immediately position the cursor-tracking frame when shown/repointed (instead of waiting for the next `OnUpdate`).
- Exposed `EllesmereUI._repointTooltipAtCursor(tooltip)` so custom frames can reliably re-anchor `GameTooltip` to the cursor after setting content.

**EllesmereUICooldownManager (CdmHooks)**
- All four custom CDM frame `OnEnter` handlers now respect `EllesmereUI._tooltipSuppressedByMode` so they honor the global Show Tooltips setting.
- Trinket frame now uses `SetItemByID` (avoids equipped-item comparison conflicts with `ANCHOR_NONE`).
- Added explicit `GameTooltip:Show()` where missing and a call to `_repointTooltipAtCursor` after setting content so the tooltip reliably renders at the cursor.

author: mefenemer
body:
Automated fix for reported issue #9.

**Location:** assistant-detail

**Reported description:**
On the Dashboard page in the users workspace, it states "welcome back", when you first go whereas it should just state "Welcome". there after completing the assistant details, it should say welcome as it is the first time of being there. 

**AI summary:**
---

**Root cause:** The dashboard heading was hardcoded as "Welcome back." in `dashboard-content.html` with no logic to differentiate first-time from returning users. The `firstLoginWelcomeSeen` flag already existed in the database/API (returned by `update-profile` GET) but was never used on the frontend to control the greeting.

**What changed:**

- **`dashboard-content.html`** — Added `id="dashboard-welcome-heading"` and `id="dashboard-welcome-subtext"` to the heading elements so JavaScript can update them at runtime.

- **`workspace.html`** (two places):
  1. In `loadHeaderProfile()`, stored `profileData.firstLoginWelcomeSeen` into `window._firstLoginWelcomeSeen` so it's available without a second fetch.
  2. At the top of `_renderDashboardEngagement()`, added logic that reads `window._firstLoginWelcomeSeen` (falling back to a fresh `update-profile` fetch if the profile hasn't loaded yet). If the flag is `false` (first visit ever, or after a new subscription), the heading is changed to "Welcome." with a first-time subtext, the in-memory flag is set to `true` immediately (prevents a flash on re-render), and a fire-and-forget POST marks it seen in the database. On all subsequent dashboard loads the flag is `true` and "Welcome back." remains.

author: zi7fa159
body:
I have implemented a complete, modular, and scientifically rigorous autonomous agent for discovering previously uncataloged variable stars. 

The framework, housed in the `discovery_agent` package, performs the following workflow:
1. **Target Selection**: Autonomously selects sky regions using a mix of random coordinates and curated scientifically interesting areas (e.g., Galactic Center, Orion).
2. **Data Acquisition**: Uses `lightkurve` to download TESS Full Frame Image cutouts (TPFs).
3. **Source Detection**: Employs `photutils` to detect stars within the images.
4. **Photometry & Analysis**: Extracts light curves with background subtraction and applies multiple independent algorithms (Lomb-Scargle and Box Least Squares) to detect periodicity.
5. **Multi-Catalog Validation**: Promising candidates are automatically cross-matched against AAVSO VSX, SIMBAD, and Gaia DR3 catalogs via `astroquery` to ensure they are previously uncataloged.
6. **Operational Safety**: The agent follows a strict 'pause' rule, halting automation immediately when a high-confidence discovery is made to allow for manual review.

During verification, the agent identified a high-confidence uncataloged variable candidate at **RA=231.62081, Dec=4.01137** with a period of ~12.29 days, demonstrating the effectiveness of the system.

author: daifmx
body:
## XMGPLAT-10687 — AI Chat Feedback Metadata

Adds an optional HTTP **metadata enrichment endpoint** that is called on every feedback submission. The returned JSON object is stored verbatim in a new `FeedbackEntry.entry_metadata` field, letting host applications attach domain-specific context (tenant, RBAC roles, experiment flags, IdP attributes) to feedback without baking it into the generic plugin.

### Changes
- **config** (`config.py`): four `AUTOCHAT_FEEDBACK_METADATA_ENRICHMENT_*` fields (`url`, `timeout`, `fail_on_error`, `max_bytes`) plus a `field_validator` rejecting non-HTTP(S) schemes (SSRF guard).
- **model** (`models.py`): `entry_metadata: Dict` field on `FeedbackEntry`.
- **handler** (`websocket_handler.py`): `_fetch_feedback_metadata` helper — builds the AC3 session payload field-by-field (no `to_dict()`, no credentials), POSTs with a per-request timeout override, enforces the response size cap, validates a 200 + JSON-object body, and applies `fail_on_error` semantics; wired into `_handle_feedback_message` (no-op when the URL is unset).
- **db schema/stores**: idempotent `entry_metadata` column migrations for Postgres (`JSONB`) and SQLite (`TEXT`), with read/write support in both stores.
- **tests** (`test_feedback_metadata_enrichment.py`): 14 tests covering AC14 (a)–(h) — payload contract, per-request timeout, response size cap, non-object/non-200 handling, `fail_on_error` branches, and SQLite/Postgres round-trips.

### Security
- URL is operator-supplied and validated at config load (rejects `file://`, `gopher://`, etc.).
- Session payload excludes `credentials`/`auth_handler`; only the seven AC3 fields are sent.
- Response body is size-bounded (default 64 KB) to prevent storage amplification.

### Testing
Full suite: **159 passed**.

## Summary

After ZTP builds a device (Day-0 mgmt + Day-N production), operators need to push **subsequent targeted changes** to already-live devices — a BGP policy, a firewall policy, an ACL, a VLAN, a static route. An audit confirmed this "incremental policy push" was the one **missing** Day-2 capability: `policies.ts` renders full-config placeholder snippets (no rollback, not parameterized) and drift remediation is reactive-only. This adds a **proactive, parameterized, per-vendor, reversible** change-push tool.

- **`CHANGE_CATALOG`** of parameterized change ops:
  - **bgp-neighbor** (peer IP / remote-AS / in+out policy)

- `buildChangeSet(op, params, devices)` scopes the change to the **selected live devices**, marks each `supported` by role + family, summarizes byFamily; `changeSetToScript` / `changeSetRollbackScript` produce push + rollback runbooks; `validateChangeParams` flags missing required fields.

author: dangause
body:
## Summary

Deep dive into the ALMA archive's full VO footprint, verified end-to-end against the live service (`ivo://jao.alma/tap_na`, SIAv2, DataLink) and the official ObsCore example queries. Encodes the findings into the two knowledge layers and prioritizes ALMA in the registry.

Two commits:
1. **Deepen ALMA TAP/obscore knowledge + prioritize it** — ALMA moves above NRAO (DataLab still first), so it becomes the 2nd TAP endpoint example shown to the LLM. ALMA `usage_notes` 3 → 8, and a first `SCHEMA_KB` entry for `ivoa.obscore`.
2. **Add ALMA SIAv2 + DataLink + source-catalogue knowledge** — `sia_url` set, DataLink download indirection documented, and a `SCHEMA_KB` entry for `sourcecatalogue.source_cone_search`.

## Key corrections / additions (all verified live)

- **Removed an empirically false note.** The old entry claimed `CONTAINS(POINT, CIRCLE)` geometry "fails or hits timeouts" and advised a `target_name LIKE` fallback. In reality both `INTERSECTS(CIRCLE, s_region)` and `CONTAINS(POINT, CIRCLE)` return in **sync** in well under a second.
- **Sync vs async routing:** filtered (cone / proposal / author) queries run fine in sync; unfiltered full-table scans/aggregates time out → `async`/`auto`.
- **Granularity:** rows are per-spectral-window × execution. `member_ous_uid` is the dataset key (`SELECT DISTINCT member_ous_uid`, not `GROUP BY t_min`).
- **Controlled vocabularies** (full-table verified): `scientific_category` (9 values), `dataproduct_type` {cube,image}, `data_rights` {Public,Proprietary}, `science_observation`/`qa2_passed` {T,F}; `band_list` token semantics (1,3–10; `LIKE '%1%'` also matches band 10).
- **SIAv2 service** (`https://almascience.nrao.edu/sia2`) — verified live, returns the same extended-obscore columns; `vo_sia_search` now reaches it and ALMA leads the SIA endpoint examples too.
- **DataLink downloads:** `access_url` points at `.../datalink/sync?ID=<uid>` (indirection, like CADC); `access_format` is truncated to 9 chars (`applicati`), so don't rely on it.
- **`sourcecatalogue.source_cone_search`:** calibrator/source flux catalogue — filter on `m_ra`/`m_dec` (the `s_ra_deg`/`s_dec_deg` columns are nullable → `CONTAINS` raises `ORA-13032`).
- **Bibliography/PI discovery:** `pi_name`, `first_author`/`authors`, `pub_title`/`pub_abstract`/`publication_year`/`bib_reference`, `proposal_abstract` — enables "find the ALMA data behind paper X / by PI Y" directly in ADQL.

## Tests

`known_archives.py` ordering invariant flipped (ALMA before NRAO), `vo_archive_list` second-entry assertion updated, plus new ALMA usage-note, SIA-endpoint, and `SCHEMA_KB` lookup tests. **289 passing**, ruff + pyright clean.

## Live verification

Every encoded fact is backed by a live query (HL Tau dataset enumeration via `INTERSECTS`+QA filters; DSHARP `proposal_id` + bibliography; `first_author LIKE 'Andrews%'`; 3C 273 calibrator fluxes on `m_ra`/`m_dec`; the `ORA-13032` negative case on `s_ra_deg`; SIAv2 image discovery with DataLink `access_url`).

author: samggreenberg
body:
## What went wrong (the reported failure)

On an AWS **g4dn.4xlarge running genuine, unregistered RHEL 9**, `bash scripts/install.sh` → `[i]` install-driver dead-ended. Every dnf route to the NVIDIA driver was exhausted:

1. `cuda-drivers` is hidden behind a DNF module (`filtered out by modular filtering`).
2. The `*-dkms` streams can't get `dkms` — it lives in EPEL, and on an unregistered RHEL box the EPEL/base repos are dark (`This system is not registered with an entitlement server`), so `nothing provides dkms >= 3.1.8`.
3. The precompiled kABI streams don't resolve either: `nvidia-driver:latest` offers only the filtered-out `-dkms` kmod as a provider of `nvidia-kmod`, and `nvidia-driver:open` is a `missing module`.

Previously the installer just printed the package-manager error and gave up.

## What this changes

Adds a **universal last-resort fallback**: NVIDIA's self-contained `.run` installer — the route [AWS documents for EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/install-nvidia-driver.html). It needs no CUDA repo, no DNF module, no EPEL, and no `dkms`; it compiles the kernel module in place against the running kernel (only `gcc`/`make` + kernel headers, installed best-effort first).

- New `vts_install_driver_runfile()`. The `.run` URL resolves from `$VTSEARCH_NVIDIA_RUNFILE_URL` if set (pin a version, or point at the public Tesla compute driver), else the latest driver in AWS's **public, credential-free** `ec2-linux-nvidia-drivers` S3 bucket (plain HTTPS, no AWS CLI).
- `vts_install_nvidia_driver()` now tracks a `pkg_ok` flag across the apt/dnf branches and falls through to the `.run` installer whenever the package path didn't complete, instead of returning early. The unrecognized-distro branch now also tries the `.run` path.
- Installer runs `--silent --disable-nouveau --no-cc-version-check`; a reboot then loads the freshly built `nvidia` module (the existing post-install `modprobe`/`nvidia-smi` check and reboot guidance still apply).

## Docs

`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` gains the fourth RHEL failure mode, the `.run` fallback behavior, the `VTSEARCH_NVIDIA_RUNFILE_URL` override, and manual `.run` steps.

## Testing

Change is isolated to the shell installer + docs (no Python/frontend coverage). Verified with `bash -n` (syntax OK) and `shellcheck` (clean apart from pre-existing SC1091 source-file infos). The `.run` install path itself requires a real RHEL GPU host and can't be exercised in CI/the cloud container.

author: koh0920
body:
## Real `FirecrackerBackend` (x86_64, File memory) — M0 GO

Replaces the Firecracker skeleton with a working backend behind the **unchanged** `SnapshotBackend` contract. Gated on the M0 feasibility spike, which passed on real KVM hardware.

### Summary of implementation
`crates/snapshot/src/firecracker.rs` (+ `firecracker/kvm_tests.rs`):
- **`probe()`** — detects `/dev/kvm` + `firecracker --version`; `available` iff both; reports the full capability facets (`MicroVm` / `memory_snapshot` / `Block` / `Minimal` / `gpu_mode=None` / `MicroVm` isolation / `supports_seal_before_bind` / `supports_disposable_overlay`).
- **runner_class** — `runner_facts()` starts from `RunnerClassFacts::from_host()` and overrides the backend-supplied facets: `vmm=firecracker`, `vmm_version`, `snapshot_format=fc-full-file-v1`, `cpu_template`, `guest_kernel_id=blake3(kernel)`, `rootfs_base_id`, `device_profile`, `network_model`. Build stamps `runner_class_id`; **restore fails closed on mismatch** (host class self-determined when not supplied).
- **`build_ready_state()`** — boot microVM → wait healthcheck (secret-free seal point) → `PATCH Paused` → `CreateSnapshot` (Full, File mem) → **all-layer no-secret scan** (fs + vmstate + memory; high-entropy advisory, provider/declared/env fail-closed) → store every layer via CapsuleFS → `ReadyStateManifest` + `NoSecretProof` + receipt. (rootfs bytes = boot disk; vmstate/memory inputs are *produced* by the snapshot.)
- **`restore()`** — runner-class gate → rehydrate layers into a **fresh disposable overlay** → `LoadSnapshot` (File mem) → resume → TAP up → wait health → `RestoredSession` (+ `restored_bytes`); session pid/tap/sock persisted for `stop()`.
- **`stop()`** — kill the VMM, tear down the TAP, remove the disposable overlay; teardown receipt; no orphan firecracker/tap.
- Dependency-light: a tiny **HTTP/1.1-over-unix-socket** client (no new crate); shells out to `firecracker`/`ip` (**no embedded sudo** — the host process must hold the caps). New additive `SnapshotError::Backend` for VMM runtime failures.
- UFFD unsupported (fail-closed); GPU out of scope; **legacy cold path untouched**; everything behind the existing availability gate.

### M0 spike result (reference)
**GO, 2026-06-29**, GCP `n2-standard-4` (Intel Cascade Lake, x86_64), nested virt, Firecracker **v1.16.0**, guest `vmlinux-5.10.223` + `ubuntu-22.04.ext4`, File mem:
cold boot 2146 ms · snapshot create 2579 ms (mem 512 MiB) · **restore→health 20/20, median 95 ms / p95 99 ms** · state-leak PASS · no-secret PASS · clean teardown. Full receipt in the implementation plan §6.1.

### Tests
- **KVM-free:** `cargo test -p snapshot` → 52 pass, 6 ignored; `cargo clippy -p snapshot --all-targets` clean. Probe availability matches host; build/restore return `Unsupported` without `/dev/kvm` (legacy behavior preserved).
- **KVM-gated** (6 `#[ignore]` tests, self-skip without `/dev/kvm`/config): probe-available, build→restore roundtrip, **20× restore latency (<3 s SLO)**, runner-class mismatch fail-closed, **state-leak regression**, **no-secret invariant**.

#### KVM-gated test instructions
On a KVM host with the repo checked out and the M0 stack present:
```sh
sudo -E env \
  ATO_FC_BIN=$PWD/firecracker \
  ATO_FC_KERNEL=$PWD/vmlinux \
  ATO_FC_TEST_ROOTFS=$PWD/rootfs.ext4 \
  cargo test -p snapshot --release -- --ignored --test-threads=1 --nocapture fc_kvm
```
> **Note:** these Rust KVM-gated tests were **not** executed on the GCP spike host — shipping the private repo to the agent-provisioned VM was blocked by a data-exfiltration guardrail. The equivalent flow **was** validated end-to-end by the throwaway bash spike (`spikes/firecracker-m0/m0_full.sh`, GO), which exercises the **same Firecracker API sequence** this backend issues. The Rust tests are ready to run on a trusted KVM CI runner / the host directly.

### Exact host requirements
x86_64 Linux · `/dev/kvm` (KVM enabled; on GCP a non-E2/AMD/Arm Intel shape with `--enable-nested-virtualization`) · `firecracker` binary on `PATH` (or `ATO_FC_BIN`) · a guest `vmlinux` (`ATO_FC_KERNEL`) · a bootable rootfs with a `/health` endpoint · `CAP_NET_ADMIN` + `kvm` group (tests run as root) · `ip`/iproute2.

### Out of scope (unchanged)
aarch64 (separate OCI bare-metal / ARM KVM pass before any aarch64 commitment) · UFFD memory backend · GPU · jailer hardening · new user-facing commands · publish/registry/PWA · wiring into `ato build`/`ato run`.

### GO/NO-GO for wiring into `ato build`/`ato run`
**GO, after backend review.** The contract held unchanged against a real VMM; restore is fast (p95 ~100 ms) and both security invariants (no cross-restore leak, no secret in snapshot) hold on hardware. Next: review this backend, then wire it as the selected backend in the E/F engine (#830) so `ato build`/`ato run` use it when `ATO_SNAPSHOT_BACKEND=firecracker` and `/dev/kvm` is present — keeping the legacy cold path as the default fallback.

author: mansiag05
body:
OOT accelerators that use device="meta" as an eager shape oracle cannot run bincount on meta tensors because the output size depends on max(input), which is unavailable without real data. This adds an optional output_size keyword argument that lets callers specify the expected number of bins explicitly, following the same pattern already established by repeat_interleave(output_size=...) and nonzero_static(size=...).

When output_size is omitted, behavior is unchanged. When provided on a real tensor it is validated against the actual bin count; when provided on a meta tensor it is used directly as the output shape.

Part of #188370.

A final job reports every PR for maintainers to review and merge manually (the workflow never merges).
