author: alexey-milovidov
body:
Add a per-column color coding switch to the Web UI (`play.html`).

A 🌈 toggle appears at the right of each column header on hover (or, on touch devices, while the header is pressed) and cycles the column's visualization mode:

- Numeric and `Date`/`DateTime` columns: `bar` → `heatmap` → `categorical` → `none`.
- Other columns: `none` ↔ `categorical`.

`heatmap` colors the whole cell background by the value scaled between the column's min and max. `categorical` hashes the value to a hue. Both use `oklch` with only the hue varying, while the lightness and chroma are fixed per theme so the cell text stays readable. `Date`/`DateTime`/`Date32`/`DateTime64` columns are colored by their time value (default `none`), and their `bar` mode spans the min..max range instead of a meaningless zero baseline.

In `categorical` mode, selecting a cell emphasizes the other cells that share its value with a heavier font and a full-contrast text color (pure white in the dark theme, pure black in the light theme); the active cell itself is left unemphasized. The emphasis is debounced by 100 ms and uses an O(1) fast path when only the value-preserving active cell moves.

The chosen modes are remembered per column in the URL and browser history, so reloads, shared links, and back/forward keep them (default modes are not stored, to keep the URL and state compact). Heatmap/categorical backgrounds fill the whole cell even when a row is taller than one line, and the vertical (transposed) single-row layout shows no color coding.

### Changelog category (leave one):

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Web UI: added a per-column color coding switch (the 🌈 icon in a column header) to toggle between bar, heatmap, categorical, and no visualization. The selected modes are remembered in the URL and browser history.

author: darcyparker
body:
`NetworkAdapterInterface.connect()` is typed to return `void`, but nothing prevents a custom adapter from implementing it as an `async` method that returns a `Promise`.

In `NetworkSubsystem.addNetworkAdapter`, `connect()` was invoked as a bare statement inside the `peerMetadata.then(...)` callback. For a Promise-returning `connect()` that detached the returned promise: a rejection escaped as an unhandled rejection rather than reaching the adjacent `.catch`, which only ever caught synchronous throws.

Returning `connect()`'s result from the `.then` callback chains its rejection into that `.catch` (which logs it). For a spec-compliant `void` `connect()` this is a no-op. The change is one line; the rest is a clarifying comment.

       Links:

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The Google Cloud Model Armor guardrail only sent text extracted from user messages to `sanitizeUserPrompt`, so harmful content inside attached PDFs, Office docs, and CSVs reached the LLM unscanned. A file-only message had no extractable text, so the pre-call and moderation hooks returned early and the document was never submitted to Model Armor at all.

Reproduced and verified against a real proxy on `localhost:4000`, real Postgres, and Google's live Model Armor API (template with an RAI "dangerous" filter). The test document is a small PDF containing explicit bomb-making instructions; the safe document is benign meeting notes.

Config (`pre_call` mode):

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-3.5-turbo
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
guardrails:
  - guardrail_name: model-armor
    litellm_params:
      guardrail: model_armor
      mode: pre_call
      template_id: <model-armor-template>
      project_id: <gcp-project>
      location: us-west1
```

The request attaches the PDF inline as an OpenAI `type: file` block:

```bash
curl -s -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-3.5-turbo","messages":[{"role":"user","content":[
        {"type":"text","text":"Summarize the attached document."},
        {"type":"file","file":{"file_data":"data:application/pdf;base64,<harmful.pdf>","filename":"harmful.pdf"}}]}],
      "guardrails":["model-armor"]}'
```

Before the fix (harmful PDF):

```
HTTP 200
{"choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"..."}}], ...}
```

Proxy log shows Model Armor received only the text, never the document bytes:

```
userPromptData': {'text': 'Summarize the attached document.'}
# byteItem submissions to Model Armor: 0
```

After the fix (same harmful PDF):

```
HTTP 400
{"error":{"message":"Content blocked by Model Armor","code":"400",
  "...":{"model_armor_response":{"sanitizationResult":{"filterMatchState":"MATCH_FOUND",
    "filterResults":{"rai":{"raiFilterResult":{"matchState":"MATCH_FOUND",
      "raiFilterTypeResults":{"dangerous":{"confidenceLevel":"HIGH","matchState":"MATCH_FOUND"}}}}}}}}}}
```

Proxy log shows the PDF bytes are now submitted to Model Armor's document API:

```
byteItem': {'byteDataType': 'PDF', 'byteData': '<base64>'}
```

After the fix (safe PDF) passes through and is still scanned:

```
HTTP 200            # benign meeting-notes PDF
# byteItem submissions to Model Armor: byteDataType PDF, filterMatchState NO_MATCH_FOUND
```

Coverage across every supported document type, run live against the real Model Armor API (each harmful file is blocked pre-call with the correct `byteDataType` submitted; the safe PDF is accepted, and safe non-PDF files are rejected by OpenAI's own file-type limit, not the guardrail):

| attachment | byteDataType submitted | harmful | safe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PDF | PDF | HTTP 400 blocked | HTTP 200 |
| CSV | CSV | HTTP 400 blocked | NO_MATCH (OpenAI rejects non-PDF) |
| TXT | TXT | HTTP 400 blocked | NO_MATCH (OpenAI rejects non-PDF) |
| DOCX | WORD_DOCUMENT | HTTP 400 blocked | NO_MATCH (OpenAI rejects non-PDF) |

Edge cases verified live:

```
data:application/octet-stream;base64,<pdf> + filename "sneaky.pdf"  -> HTTP 400 blocked   # MIME resolved from filename
harmful PDF padded to > 4 MB                                        -> HTTP 400 "Attachment exceeds Model Armor's 4 MB scan limit and was blocked"  # never submitted
```

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Changes

The pre-call and moderation hooks now resolve inline document and file attachments to bytes and submit them to Model Armor's byte API before the request reaches the LLM. A new pure module `file_scanning.py` walks message content blocks, handles the OpenAI `type: file` shape (`file_data` as a data URI or raw base64) and the Anthropic `type: document` shape (inline base64 `source`), maps the MIME type to a Model Armor `byteDataType` (`PDF`, `WORD_DOCUMENT`, `EXCEL_DOCUMENT`, `POWERPOINT_DOCUMENT`, `CSV`, `TXT`), and skips inline content it is not meant to scan (images and other unsupported types). Anything the guardrail cannot scan is treated as a scan failure and blocks the request unless the operator sets `fail_on_error: false`: a `file_id` or remote (`gs://` / `http(s)`) reference with no inline bytes, a document over the 4 MB limit, or more attachments than the per-request cap. A transient scan error on one attachment is isolated so the remaining attachments are still scanned.

The per-request attachment cap is a fixed limit of 10 for now. Making it configurable would mean threading the value through the guardrail initializer and `litellm_params`, so it is left as a follow-up rather than exposing a setting that is silently ignored. Each resolved attachment is sent through the existing `make_model_armor_request(file_bytes=..., file_type=...)` path, and a `MATCH_FOUND` blocks the request the same way text findings already do. A recognized document that exceeds Model Armor's 4 MB byte limit cannot be inspected, so it is blocked by default and only allowed through when the operator has set `fail_on_error: false`.

Resolving a bare `file_id` to bytes needs a Files-API fetch the guardrail cannot do synchronously, so that case is skipped rather than treated as scanned; this matches the existing Prompt Security guardrail, which also only handles inline bytes. Post-call and streaming hooks scan response text and carry no file attachments, so they are unchanged.

Tests extend the existing mapped file `tests/test_litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/test_model_armor.py` and cover a blocked PDF and a safe PDF through both the pre-call and moderation hooks, an Anthropic document block, a text-plus-file message, and the skip paths (`file_id`-only, unsupported type, oversize). The five core tests fail when the wiring is reverted and pass with it in place.

> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a gap where **Model Armor** only sanitized message text, so inline PDFs/Office docs could reach the LLM without a byte scan (file-only prompts skipped the guardrail entirely).

body: ## What Replaces agent-relay's stringly-typed `spawn('relayfile', …)` + parse-stdout bridge with a **typed client over relayfile's control-plane unix socket** (`relayfile control-plane serve`). Integration ops (connect/bind/list/unbind/resolve/writeback) now go over a versioned, schema-checked wire instead of argv-as-request / stdout-as-response. This is the relay half of the control-plane RFC. The relayfile half (daemon + OpenAPI + `@relayfile/client` package + `0.10.17`) is a paired PR on the relayfile repo. ## Why The CLI-as-RPC contract produced a recurring class of compile-time-preventable bugs that only surfaced at runtime (e.g. `flag provided but not defined: -json`, `pathGlob` vs `resource`, native-resource passed as a VFS glob). The socket contract is version-negotiated via `/v1/hello` and the request/response types are generated from the OpenAPI, so field drift is a **compile error**, not a runtime surprise. ## Changes - **`relayfile-client.ts`** — typed control-plane client: HTTP/JSON over `http.request({ socketPath })` (zero deps), `X-Relayfile-API-Version` handshake, daemon auto-start (one lifecycle launch) + `RELAYFILE_REQUIRE_DAEMON=1` strict never-spawn mode, typed methods aliasing the generated schemas. - **`defaultRelayfileBridge` swapped onto the client; `runRelayfile`/`spawn` deleted.** The `RelayfileBridge` interface is unchanged — subscribe/unsubscribe callers are untouched. - subscribe/unsubscribe **canonicalize the native `--resource` to relayfile's stored path-glob** via `resolve-path` before keying find/unbind (fixes the silent native-vs-glob mismatch). - Types generated from a **vendored copy** of relayfile's `openapi/relayfile-control-plane-v1.openapi.yaml` (`npm run codegen:relayfile`, reproducible). `*.gen.ts` lint-ignored. - Tests: real-daemon contract test (boots the daemon, drives the bridge over the socket) + client lifecycle units (require-daemon error, version-incompat gate, no-cache-on-failure, auto-start). ## Verification - **447 cli tests pass** (real-daemon contract tests run when `RELAYFILE_BIN` is set, skip otherwise), tsc + eslint clean, codegen reproducible. - Verified end-to-end against a real `relayfile control-plane serve` daemon built from the paired relayfile branch. ## ⚠️ Merge ordering / follow-up - **Requires relayfile ≥ 0.10.17** (carries the control-plane + `--version`). The relayfile PR must publish first; the compat gate intentionally blocks older daemons. - The vendored spec + in-repo client is the **interim**. Before merge I'll push a commit swapping the import to the **published `@relayfile/client`** package and deleting the vendored spec/codegen (the package is built + green on the relayfile side; @worker owns its publish). - Follow-up: CI step to build/install relayfile and set `RELAYFILE_BIN` so the contract tests run in CI (deferred until `0.10.17` is on npm). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: darcyparker
body:
`Repo.find()`, `DocumentQuery.whenReady()`, and the internal `pause()` helper all accept an `AbortSignal`. When it fired they rejected with a fresh `AbortError`, discarding any reason passed to `controller.abort(reason)`.

They now reject with `signal.reason`, so a custom abort reason is propagated end to end. `find()` and `whenReady()` use `signal.throwIfAborted()` on the already-aborted fast path; `pause()` builds its promise synchronously, so it rejects with `signal.reason` directly rather than throwing.

`find()` and `whenReady()` also gain `@remarks` documenting that the signal cancels the wait, not the underlying load or sync (which may still be serving other concurrent callers).

Tests assert the rejection is abort-like across JS environments (a bare `controller.abort()` yields a platform `DOMException` named `AbortError`, not an instance of this package's `AbortError` class) and that a custom reason is preserved.

author: lenaxia
body:
## Summary

Closes #456.

`Chart.yaml` version is pinned at `0.1.0` (consumed from Git, not a registry). FluxCD `source-controller` caches the packaged chart keyed on the chart version; with the **default** `reconcileStrategy: ChartVersion`, the artifact is built once and re-used forever. Every `helm upgrade` after the first renders against a stale snapshot — new templates, new migration ConfigMap keys, new RBAC never reach the cluster.

This caused the 2026-06-29 incident (migrations ConfigMap held only `000001` after #451 added `000002`–`000004`) and masked #455's new migrate-Job args.

## Fix (option 1 from the issue)

- **`README.md`**: added a prominent `## ⚠ GitOps deployment (FluxCD / Argo CD)` section immediately after the intro (before Prerequisites) with a copy-paste `HelmRelease` spec setting `reconcileStrategy: Revision`, the Argo CD equivalent, and the long-term OCI-registry alternative.
- **`Chart.yaml` `description:`**: extended so `helm show chart` warns consumers before they clone.
- **`chart_gitops_doc_test.go`** (new): doc-presence regression tests so the section cannot be silently deleted — which is exactly how `reconcileStrategy: Revision` was lost in `talos-ops-prod` `1d6975f9` for 2.5 days.

## Why a doc-presence test

Documentation is the deliverable, but an unguarded doc section can be silently deleted (the talos-ops-prod regression proves this). A test that fails if the section is removed makes the documentation a first-class contract — mirrors how the codebase pins dashboard UIDs.

## Tests

```
go test -timeout 180s ./charts/llmsafespaces/                            # PASS (full suite)
go test -timeout 120s -run 'TestChart_' -v ./charts/llmsafespaces/        # 2/2 PASS
helm lint ./charts/llmsafespaces                                         # 0 failed
gofmt -l / go vet ./charts/llmsafespaces/                                 # clean
```

## Related

- Companion PR: #457 (migrate Job CLI args — masked by this bug).
- Long-term option 2 (OCI publish / CI version-bump) tracked as a follow-up in #456.

author: darcyparker
body:
`foreverPromise` is a module-level promise that never settles. Racing it (`Promise.race([foreverPromise, x])`, or wrapping it in `abortable(foreverPromise, signal)`) appends a reaction that is never released, so the race and everything it captures are retained for the whole session.

This marks `foreverPromise` `@deprecated`: a never-settling promise is undesirable, and its only user, the already-`@deprecated` `DocHandle.whenReady`, will be removed together with it.

The `@remarks` document the footgun and the alternative: to make a wait cancelable, derive the promise from the signal (reject with `signal.reason` from a `{ once: true }` `abort` listener, handling the already-aborted case) so it can settle, then remove the listener once the wait resolves. `abortable()` applies this to a single promise; `withTimeout()` bounds a deadline.

Documentation only; no runtime change.

## #594 — the Harness Compiler is itself an OHM v1.1 Team Harness (ADR-047)

A prose objective compiles to a **runnable OHM v1.1 Team Harness** via a 4-member ACYCLIC team —
planner → capability-surveyor → manifest-drafter → reviewer — built AS a Team Harness (ADR-047
decision 2). Per **CTO decision A**: the repair loop is the **reviewer's IN-HARNESS tool-use loop**
(its single dispatch iterates validate→fix→validate via the `manifest-validate` tool, bounded by its
iteration cap + the #585 pool), so the team is a plain linear chain with **NO team-level loop and
ZERO engine change** — the ADR-043 conductor is untouched.

### What ships
- **`packages/ohm/compiler/`** — the greenfield ohm surface:
  - `validate.py` (`validate_draft`): the reviewer's deterministic gate — peels the drafter's JSON
    out of the LLM's prose/```json fence (#599), diffs each member's `tools[]` against the surveyed
    catalog (a hallucinated tool → blocking `F-CAPABILITY-MISSING`, ADR-032 — the assembler would
    otherwise synthesise a ref), and runs the SAME `assemble_and_report` dry-run the importer uses
    (#593, one validator two on-ramps). Returns a CODED `would_block` verdict, never the model's
    opinion (ADR-043 invariant). `_tool_slug` normalises a tool NAME and a full REF to one slug.
  - `prompts.py` — the 4 member sub-harness bodies; the reviewer iterates validate→fix→validate.
  - `team.py` (`build_compiler_team`) — the 4-member linear acyclic team + 4 sub-harnesses; slice-1
    bakes the prose objective into the planner's sub-goal + the seeded catalog into the surveyor's
    (no engine wiring — a member's sub-goal renders as its harness `Objective:` line).
- **`manifest-validate` connector** (capability-registry) — the reviewer opts into
  `core/manifest-validate@1` (slug == NAME, like `core/read@1` — the synthesized ref resolves); a
  keyless in-process InternalTool wrapping `validate_draft`. **THE DETERMINISTIC REGISTRY-DIFF**:
  unions the relayed catalog with the live plugin registry so a registered tool always passes even
  when the reviewer (an LLM) doesn't relay the catalog verbatim; a tool neither surveyed NOR
  registered still blocks. capability-registry now depends on `oraclous-ohm` (the shared kernel).

### Deployed proof — real BYOM through `:8006`, no fakes (DoD 1b/1c)
`tests/e2e/test_compiler_prose_to_team_gateway_e2e.py`, run locally on the deployed stack:
```
tests/e2e/test_compiler_prose_to_team_gateway_e2e.py::test_a_prose_objective_compiles_to_a_runnable_team PASSED [ 50%]
tests/e2e/test_compiler_prose_to_team_gateway_e2e.py::test_the_capability_absence_gate_blocks_on_the_deployed_registry PASSED [100%]
======================== 2 passed, 1 warning in 23.86s =========================
```
- **prose → runnable team**: a prose objective runs the 4-member compiler end-to-end (real
  OpenRouter; the reviewer validates via the manifest-validate connector); the reviewer's compiled
  team passes the SAME `assemble_and_report` dry-run → `would_block` False → runnable.
- **capability-absence (deterministic, no LLM)**: a draft naming an unsurveyed/unregistered tool
  blocks `F-CAPABILITY-MISSING` on the deployed registry, through the gateway.

### Pre-PR adversarial review (two rounds, folded before opening)
A multi-lens adversarial review over the full diff caught — and this PR fixes — two real gate defects
the green unit tests missed, plus a fail-closed belt:
- **HIGH — namespace bypass / slug divergence**: the capability-absence gate stripped *any*
  namespace, so a bogus `evil/web-research` (and, found in the second verification round, any
  emoji/punctuation/CJK namespace like `😈/web-research` or `.../web-research` that the slugifier
  would erase) collapsed to the surveyed `web-research` and slipped past the gate. `_tool_slug` now
  strips a trailing `@version` and ONLY the canonical ascii `core/` namespace, and marks any other
  `/`-bearing identifier `ns--…` so it can never collapse to a bare slug — while the legit
  `core/web-research@1.0.0` still → `web-research` (passes). 8 parametrized regression cases.
- **MEDIUM — empty-slug wildcard**: an empty-slug catalog entry (`""`) is dropped (never a wildcard),
  and an empty-slug drafted tool (`"@"`, `"/"`) fails closed.
- **fail-closed belt**: the connector returns `would_block: True` if the validator itself ever raises.
Every fix ships with regression tests, was re-proven on the deployed stack (no false-block of legit
tools), and the closure was confirmed across **three** adversarial verification rounds (the 2nd and
3rd each found and drove a deeper namespace edge to ground). Final round: 300k fuzzed inputs vs a
canonical catalog → **0** capability-absence breaks / **0** false-blocks; the `ns--` namespace
encoding is structurally disjoint from a bare slug.

**Known accepted LOW (not reachable from normal operation):** within the foreign-namespace (`ns--…`)
space, two distinct hyphen-spellings of a `/`-bearing name can slug-collide (`a-b/c` vs `a--b/c`).
It requires the *catalog itself* to carry a `/`-bearing entry — which the canonical survey output and
the registry-augment (all clean ascii slugs, no `/`) never produce — and it cannot impersonate a bare
surveyed tool. Documented for the CTO; a fast-follow if the live `capability-survey` ever emits refs.

### Gates
28 unit tests green (compiler + connector); `ruff` + `ruff format` + `mypy` (590 files) +
`pytest --collect-only` + `lint-imports` (5/5) all clean; the broader ohm (331) + capability-registry
unit (301) suites pass (no regression). capability-registry image rebuilt + recreated + verified
carrying the code before each deployed run.

### Scope / fast-follow
Slice-1 seeds the catalog deterministically; the live `capability-survey` connector is the
fast-follow (per the CTO). Chain B continues with #595 (NL refine), #596 (seed defaults),
#597 (eval-set).

body:
Extends the single-front-door funnel (PR #14/#15). Products and Ingredients **detail** pages now feed the landing Yuri widget, the same way blog posts do.

## What it does
A contextual nudge that:
- **References the specific product/ingredient** ("Want to know if {product} actually fits your skin?")
- **Routes to the landing widget** with the question prefilled (`/?ask=<question>&from=product|ingredient`)

## Best-practice guardrails (NOT a spammy popup — protects the honest-insider brand)
- **Engagement-triggered**: appears after 40% scroll OR 18s dwell (whichever first), never on instant arrival
- **Inline slide-in card**, not a blocking modal
- **Dismissible**, and stays dismissed per page-type for the session
- **One per page**, references what they're viewing

## Respects Yuri Sole Authority
The nudge is a Yuri-conversation **entry point with context**, NOT a standalone recommendation. It doesn't tell the user what to do with their skin — Yuri does, after they land. (Acceptable pattern per CLAUDE.md.)

## Measurement
New `yuri_nudge_shown` / `yuri_nudge_click` GA4 events (with `kind`). Combined with `yuri_prefill_arrived(source)`, this measures the full feeder funnel: shown → click → arrived → first message.

## Scope
Detail pages only (high intent) this pass. Browse/list nudges + A/B timing deferred. Plan: `PHASE-4-CONTEXTUAL-YURI-NUDGE.md`.

## Gates
- AI-First check: PASS (incl. Yuri Sole Authority)
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `npm run build`: clean

author: mattmre
body:
## Summary

Phase II **H4 "make cycles compound" branch** — the `compound_cycles` capability. H4 is "make
cycles compound, OR characterize why one-shot is the fixed point." The *characterize* branch is
done (paper §5.2: one-shot is a designed fixed point because compounding overshoots). This adds
the *compound* branch, which had **no code**: the supervised cycle only ever applied the trained
adapter to the FIXED pre-drift snapshot (the idempotent one-shot).

`DriftRecoveryConfig.compound_cycles` (default `False`): when `True`, `_supervised_anchor_cycle`
applies the adapter to the **LIVE** (already-mutated) store each cycle (`original_points=None`)
instead of the fixed snapshot, so corrections **stack** across cycles. The metadata reports the
flag. Default `False` preserves the idempotent one-shot **exactly** (apply target unchanged), so
the existing C3a idempotency/determinism tests are byte-unaffected. The post-bank conditions
(C5/C5s/C5r, a different apply path) are untouched.

EVIDENCE: implementer-captured run — `python -m unittest test_run_drift_recovery_experiment` → 25/25 OK (no regression); `ruff` clean. The new test (`test_compound_cycles_diverges_from_the_one_shot_fixed_point`, C4a × 3 cycles) proves it via the per-cycle correction NORM (ndcg@10 on the 4-doc stub is rank-coarse): one-shot's norm is FLAT across cycles (`os_norms[0] == os_norms[-1]` — the idempotent fixed point); compound's CHANGES (`cp_norms[0] != cp_norms[-1]` — stacks on the live store). It discriminates in BOTH directions — if `compound_cycles` were ignored both would be flat and the compound assertion would fail; if one-shot accidentally compounded the flat assertion would fail.
SMOKE: floor-tier — `python -m unittest test_run_drift_recovery_experiment` → 25/25; `ruff` clean. No GPU.

## Brutal Honesty

- **L1 stubs / L2 escape / L3 mocks-in-prod:** none. The new branch (`original_points=None`) is
  exercised by the new test; the default branch by the existing C3a/C4a fire tests.
- **L4 partial-as-complete:** this adds the **capability + a discriminating test**. The actual
  GPU ablation — does compounding overshoot, and by how much — is DEFERRED and explicitly stated
  in the test docstring ("the overshoot magnitude is the GPU ablation's job, not asserted here").
  No claim that compounding helps or hurts by any amount.
- **L9 fabricated result / L13:** the overshoot figure `0.136→0.497→0.443` in the config comment
  cross-references the existing in-code Tier-B finding and is framed as PRIOR recorded evidence,
  not a new measurement.
- **L5/L8 untested:** both apply branches exercised. **L11 broad-catch:** none.
- Minor (non-blocking, per Tier-B): the compound discriminator compares correction norms at
  8-decimal rounding — spurious equality is highly unlikely (cycle-1 mutation magnitude > 0.01),
  acceptable for a capability test.

BHS_SELF_DRAFT: 100
BHS_SELF_DRAFT_AGENT: Claude Opus 4.8 (implementer)
BHS_TIER_B: 100
BHS_TIER_B_AGENT: fresh adversarial reviewer (full-source trace — verified the compound semantics (live store via original_points=None vs fixed snapshot), default-False byte-equivalence (no regression), two-directional test discrimination (fails if the flag is dead OR if one-shot compounds), C5/C5s/C5r isolation, and that the cited overshoot figure is prior evidence not fabricated; suite not re-run due to broken session-wide subagent Bash; implementer captured 25/25 + ruff)
BHS_TIER_B_SEVERITY: none
BHS_OFFICIAL: 100
CARRY_FORWARD: the GPU ablation — run `compound_cycles=True` vs `False` and measure the overshoot trajectory to empirically confirm/refute the one-shot-fixed-point characterization (the paper notes this as a small future experiment).
DEFERRED_SCOPE: the real-data compound-vs-one-shot ablation (overshoot magnitude).

author: jkwak-work
body:
## Motivation

The GitHub workflow directory had several inconsistent file names that made it harder to distinguish reusable CI components, standalone scheduled nightly jobs, and maintenance/regeneration workflows. For example, nightly jobs used names such as `coverage-nightly.yml`, `ci-agentic-tests-nightly.yml`, and `vk-gl-cts-nightly.yml`, while related reusable CI workflows used a separate naming style.

## Proposed solution

Rename workflow files and update their callers and documentation references while keeping the existing workflow behavior intact. In particular, the nightly jobs remain standalone scheduled workflows rather than being consolidated into a single nightly fanout.

## Change summary

- Rename reusable CI workflow files such as `ci-compile-test.yml`, `ci-benchmark-test.yml`, `ci-slang-coverage.yml`, and `ci-trigger-slangpy.yml`, and update the `ci.yml` callers.
- Rename standalone scheduled nightly workflows such as `ci-agentic-tests-nightly.yml`, `coverage-nightly.yml`, `vk-gl-cts-nightly.yml`, `compile-perf-nightly.yml`, the RTX Remix workflow, and the Sascha Willems shader workflow.
- Rename maintenance workflows for IR version comments, SPIR-V Tools checks, and formatting regeneration.
- Update references in README and related workflow/tooling documentation so badges and local reproduction notes point at the new workflow filenames.

## Process report

This change is intentionally limited to workflow file organization. The scheduled nightly workflows continue to own their own `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` triggers, and reusable CI workflows still live directly under `.github/workflows` so GitHub Actions can call them with `workflow_call`.

The MaterialX workflow remains part of `ci.yml`: the caller now points to `ci-materialx-regression-test.yml`, reflecting that MaterialX is the external integration surface and the workflow is a regression test rather than an MDL test.

The CI caller job IDs and reusable workflow job IDs that can feed required status checks are intentionally kept at their previous names. For example, `ci.yml` still exposes `test-materialx-windows-release`, `test-compile-regression`, and `test-benchmark`; this keeps branch-protection status identities stable while only the workflow filenames change.

The former agentic nightly is intentionally named `nightly-slang-test.yml` with the display name `Nightly Slang Test`. Under the selected workflow naming pattern, this is the default Slang nightly test workflow rather than a separate named suite; the `agentic-tests` job name and workflow comments keep the generated-test implementation detail visible.

The compile-perf workflow remains a standalone nightly publisher under `nightly-mdl-perf-test.yml`; the separate release sweep workflow is left outside the nightly rename set because it has a different cache/history-population purpose.

The `docker/linux-clang-ci.Dockerfile` comment that mentions the future coverage workflow is intentionally left unchanged. This repository treats any Dockerfile edit as a container image input change and requires an image tag bump, which would be unrelated to this workflow-file rename PR.

author: charlesbaynham
body:
Follow-up onto **PR #39** (r1's analyze() NaN-guard), into `feature/diagnostics` (rolls into PR #37). Makes the default-submit `ClockRabi*` diagnostics produce clean data and persist a **physical pi-time** — the P5 automation goal. Implements job card `2026-06-inverted-rabi-flop-fit`.

## (a) Velocity-slice decoupling
`CompensatedClockSpecMixin` derived `T_sel = spectroscopy_pulse_time * pulse_ratio` — the slice algorithm assumes the spectroscopy pulse is a **pi pulse** (Charles confirmed). A Rabi flop sweeps `spectroscopy_pulse_time` through many non-pi values, so the slice width varied ~60x across the scan, selecting a different velocity class at every point and **washing out the flop**. Added `selection_time_override` (0 = old proportional behaviour, **unchanged for spectroscopy/LMT**); the Rabi diagnostics fix it to the nominal shelving duration so only the interrogation pulse varies. Likely THE contrast fix.

## (b) Inverted dead-time fit
Readout is **inverted** (survival): flop starts HIGH, **dips** at pi, and starts **~10 us late** (real dead-time, measured on RID 75720: free `t_dead` improves first-arm RMS 16x; present on up beam, onset ~same on down — not a down-beam OPLL-jump effect). Analysis now fits `1 - excitation` with `t_dead` **free** so persisted `t_max_transfer` lands on the dip; averages `num_repeats` duplicate x (the int(inf) crash source) and drops survival>1 outliers.

`make_dataset_fit_analysis` gains opt-in `y_transform`, `y_valid_range`, `average_repeats`.

## Tests
Synthetic clean inverted+dead-time flop: persisted `pi_time` lands on the dip within fit error; duplicate-x crash avoided; outliers dropped. PR #39's NaN-guard tests still pass. All 10 `test_dataset_fit_analysis` green; 4 changed Fragments compile clean.

## Scope / honesty
Validated on a **synthetic** flop, not the contrast-starved real RIDs — on the current rig the flop doesn't recover (clearout/contrast/survival-norm physics, **out of scope**). (a) is the likely contrast fix; a fresh default-submit run is the acceptance test. If contrast is still inadequate after (a), the automation is blocked on that physics → separate item.

body:
## Qué hace

Wirear el portero del checkout (`services/checkout/`) al transporte HTTP. Dos endpoints nuevos:

### `POST /api/checkout/validar`

```json
// Request
{ "session_id": "<uuid>", "session_confirmed": false }

// Response — misma lista que muestra la UI
{ "listo": true, "faltan": [] }
{ "listo": false, "faltan": [{"check": "tyc", "mensaje": "...", "accion": "aceptar_tyc"}] }
```

- Requiere sesión cliente (`require_cliente`)
- Computa `firma_ok = has_recent_stepup() OR session_confirmed` (passkey step-up si existe, fallback "Confirmo" por sesión)
- Delega toda la validación al portero (`validar_checkout`)

### `POST /api/checkout/aceptar-tyc`

Registra la aceptación de la versión actual de T&C (`v1`) para el cliente. Idempotente (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`).

## Cambios

- `backend/routes/checkout.py` — router nuevo con los dos endpoints
- `backend/main.py` — `include_router(checkout_router, prefix="/api")`

## Plan de prueba

En staging (logueado como cliente con staging-login):

```bash
# 1. Aceptar T&C
curl -X POST https://<staging>/api/checkout/aceptar-tyc \
  -H "Cookie: session=<cookie>"
# → {"ok": true}

# 2. Validar checkout con un carrito activo
curl -X POST https://<staging>/api/checkout/validar \
  -H "Cookie: session=<cookie>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"session_id": "<uuid-del-carrito>", "session_confirmed": true}'
# → {"listo": false, "faltan": [...]} o {"listo": true, "faltan": []}

# Sin sesión → 401
curl -X POST https://<staging>/api/checkout/validar \
  -d '{"session_id": "..."}' 
# → 401
```

## What & why

Second booking-funnel wedge. When a visitor books a real availability slot, the booking is confirmed on the spot and the thanks page says "You're booked!" — but it gave them **no way to put the session on their own calendar**. The appointment already exposes a public `.ics` route (`/book/{token}/calendar.ics`, used by the portal); this just surfaces it at the moment of booking.

## How it works

- The booking confirmation page now shows an **"📅 Add to calendar"** link for a confirmed slot booking — `appointment_ics_url(...)` for the new appointment's token.
- A **proposed** request (no fixed time yet) doesn't get one — there's nothing to add until the studio confirms (the confirmation email handles that path).
- The link is only rendered on the no-deposit confirmed path (a deposit booking redirects to pay); the token is the visitor's own appointment token, so it's theirs to use. No migration.

## Tests

`test_confirmed_slot_booking_offers_calendar_link` (in `tests/test_booking.py`): sets up availability, books a real open slot through the public route, and asserts the confirmed thanks page shows "You're booked!" and the "Add to calendar" `.ics` link. author: oalders
body:
## Problem

The roster only shows the **leading fragment** of a session id (the id column is clipped to `fc49…` by `overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis`), but `clodhopper end --session` required the **exact full UUID**. So the one identifier the dashboard hands you couldn't be used to reap a stuck session — you had to dig the full id out of SQLite to run e.g. `clodhopper end --session fc49d0c6-f945-470b-8568-a2d054917ff2`.

## Change

- **`--session` matches by prefix** — `clodhopper end --session fc49` now resolves the session whose id starts with that fragment. LIKE wildcards in the input are escaped so the fragment is matched verbatim.
- **Ambiguity fails closed** — a prefix that resolves to 2+ live sessions writes no `SessionEnd` and returns an `*AmbiguousSessionError` listing the candidates (exit 2), so a too-short fragment can never end the wrong agent. An already-ended session sharing the prefix is not a collision, so a single live match still resolves cleanly.
- `--branch` / `--cwd` stay bulk selectors (unchanged).
- Help text (`end.go`, `main.go`) and README updated.

## Verification

```
end --session fc49   → ended 1 live session(s)                    exit=0
end --session ab     → "ab" matches 2 live sessions… (lists both) exit=2
end --session abcd1  → ended 1 live session(s)                    exit=0
```

Three new tests in `store_test.go` (prefix resolves, ambiguous prefix errors and ends nothing, already-ended session sharing a prefix is not a collision). Full suite green; `precious lint --all` clean.

## Not included

An interactive picker for `clodhopper end` with no selector supplied was discussed but left out — it would add a TUI dependency to an otherwise dependency-light binary, so it's better as a separate decision.

author: sarneijim
body:
### ✅ Checklist

- [x] `npx changeset` was attached.
- [x] **Covered by automatic tests.**
- [x] **Impact of the changes:**
  - Content card / banner impression analytics on the Portfolio (carousel layout)
  - `InViewContext` visibility tracking and de-duplication of `contentcard_impression` events
  - Any consumer of `useInViewContext` that re-subscribes on re-render

### 📝 Description

**Problem**: `contentcard_impression` events were being logged twice for the same card. The `InViewContext` stored a card's "is in view" memory in a `WeakMap` keyed by the per-subscription `WatchedItem` object. Consumers such as the carousel (`contentCards/layouts/carousel`) pass a non-memoized `items` array, so `useInViewContext` re-subscribes on every re-render, creating a brand-new `WatchedItem`. Because the new key had no prior visibility entry, an already-visible card was treated as newly in-view and `logImpressionCard` fired again — producing duplicate impression analytics.

**Solution**: Key the visibility `WeakMap` by the stable `target` ref (`RefObject<View>`) instead of the ephemeral `WatchedItem`. The visibility memory now survives re-subscriptions, so a card that is still in view does not re-fire its impression after a re-render.

Before:

```ts
const watchedItem = useRef(new WeakMap<WatchedItem, boolean>());
// ...
const threshold = watchedItem.current.get(item) ? outOfViewThreshold : inViewThreshold;
if (entry.isInView === watchedItem.current.get(item)) return;
watchedItem.current.set(item, entry.isInView);
```

After:

```ts
const visibilityByTarget = useRef(new WeakMap<RefObject<View | null>, boolean>());
// ...
const threshold = visibilityByTarget.current.get(item.target) ? outOfViewThreshold : inViewThreshold;
if (entry.isInView === visibilityByTarget.current.get(item.target)) return;
visibilityByTarget.current.set(item.target, entry.isInView);
```

A new unit test (`InViewContext/index.test.tsx`) reproduces the bug deterministically: it forces a re-subscription of an item that is still in view and asserts the in-view callback fires only once (it fired twice before the fix).

author: bdcdo
body:
## Contexto

PR 3/3 da #306, a maior frente. Liga `PTH` (flake8-use-pathlib) no `select` e zera os **137 achados** em `src` (87) e `tests` (50): migração de `os.path`/`open`/`glob`/`os.makedirs` para `pathlib`. É a única frente que mexe em **I/O real** — criar diretórios, abrir/escrever/remover/listar arquivos de download.

> **Stacked PR.** Base = `chore/ruff-perf` (#322). Mesclar #320 → #321 → #322 → este, nessa ordem. O diff aqui mostra **só** as mudanças de PTH.

Nota: o Ruff 0.15.x **não autofixa** as regras PTH (são display-only), então a migração foi **manual**, arquivo a arquivo — concentrada em TJSP download/parse, na família `_esaj`, nos clients TRF e nos testes que exercitam I/O.

## Conversões (comportamento preservado)

- `os.path.join` → `Path(a) / b` (com `str(...)` onde o consumidor exige str: retornos tipados `-> str`, f-strings, logging `%s`).
- `open(p, ...)` → `Path(p).open(...)`.
- `os.makedirs(p, exist_ok=True)` → `Path(p).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` (**`parents=True`** preserva a recursividade do `makedirs`).
- `os.path.isdir/isfile/exists` → `Path(p).is_dir()/is_file()/exists()`.
- `os.path.dirname/basename/getsize` → `Path(p).parent` / `.name` / `.stat().st_size`.
- `os.unlink` → `Path(p).unlink()`; `os.listdir` → `Path(p).iterdir()`.
- `glob.glob(join(d, '**/*.html'), recursive=True)` → `Path(d).rglob('*.html')` (ordem de filesystem idêntica; `+is_file()` defensivo onde aplicável).

Critério `Path` vs `str`: onde o glob alimentava slicing/`endswith` de string, mantido `str(...)`; onde o consumidor só itera/abre, mantido `Path`.

## Verificação

- `uvx ruff@0.15.12 check src tests --select PTH` → **All checks passed!**
- `uvx ruff@0.15.12 check src tests` (todas as famílias) → **All checks passed!**
- `pre-commit run mypy` (arquivos alterados) → **Passed** (sem `Path` vazando onde `str` é esperado)
- `pre-commit run ruff/isort/flake8` → **Passed**
- `uv run pytest` → **1755 passed, 29 skipped** (inclui testes de download/parse que exercitam I/O real)

Sem entrada no CHANGELOG (tooling, sem efeito na API pública).

Refs #306.

author: wmdebrito
body:
## Description
<!--- Provide a general summary of your change in the Pull Request title above -->
<!--- Describe your change in detail here. -->
The per-NAL raw_data buffers used to build the codec extra data were only 64 bytes. Some SPS with full VUI/HRD parameters can exceed that (e.g. Wowza-originated HLS), so the SPS was silently dropped (raw_data_size reset to 0) and the H.264 extra data ended up empty.

Kodi then rejects the video stream with "Codec id 27 require extradata" and disables it, leaving an audio-only stream that immediately hits EOF.

Increase the SPS/PPS raw_data buffers to 256 bytes so that for some large SPS extra data is built correctly.

Also extra_data was increase from 512 to 1024 to accommodate rare situations.
NAL buffers are now 256 bytes each, so a single legitimate SPS+PPS can be up to 4+255+4+255 = 518 bytes. With only 512, the guard I added would correctly refuse to overflow — but it would then drop a valid PPS, silently reintroducing a decode failure. 1024 ensures the destination can hold whatever the 256-byte NAL buffers can legitimately produce. The guard prevents the crash; the 1024 prevents truncation.

## Motivation and context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. -->
Fix some streams that are not playing due to small buffer size.

## How has this been tested?
<!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your change. -->
<!--- Include details of your testing environment, and the tests you ran to -->
<!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. -->
Tested on Kodi 21 with a custom IA build. The falling stream was now able to be played. No regression on other streams

author: chrisrohn
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to the DCI season-schedule import fix. Production was running stale function code because the `default` codebase deploys never updated the isolated `functions-scraper` codebase, and the admin "Refresh Schedule" action reported a misleading "0 scraped" because all scraper failures were silently swallowed. This PR makes the scraper deploy with every normal deploy and makes failures actionable.

## Changes

**`.github/workflows/deploy-functions.yml` — deploy the scraper codebase**
- The `all` target only deployed the `default` codebase in batches and never touched `functions-scraper`, so the DCI events scraper went stale after normal deploys.
- Added a `firebase deploy --only functions:scraper` step after the batches, tracked in the failure summary so a scraper-codebase failure fails the job. (The job already installs `functions-scraper` deps, so no other changes were needed.)

**`functions/src/helpers/season.js` — stop swallowing scraper failures**
- `scrapeUpcomingDciEvents()` previously caught every failure (missing config, unbound/empty `SCRAPER_INVOKE_KEY`, transport error, non-2xx, unsuccessful response) and returned `[]`, making real infrastructure failures indistinguishable from "0 events scraped."
- It now **throws** on infrastructure failures and returns `[]` only for a genuinely successful empty result.
- Caller behavior is preserved: `startNewLiveSeason` still degrades gracefully (its caller catches and continues with an empty schedule, so season start never breaks); `refreshLiveSeasonSchedule` re-throws so the cause propagates.

**`functions/src/callable/admin.js` — relay the real error**
- `manualTrigger`'s catch dropped `error.message`, so the admin only ever saw a generic message. It now includes `error.message`, so a failed refresh shows the actual cause (e.g. `Scraper request failed: 404 ...`).

## Testing
- `node --check` passes for both changed JS files; YAML validated.
- Functional verification requires a deploy: run the `all` target, confirm the new "Deploying scraper codebase" group is green alongside the batches, then trigger admin "Refresh Schedule" and confirm the log shows `[Season] Scraper returned N events.` (or a now-actionable error message).

body:
## Summary

Fixes **XPOMGMT-745** — unsafe `eval()`/`exec()` on data sourced from external benchmark datasets, allowing RCE via a poisoned dataset (HuggingFace/git supply-chain). Both affected adapters (`ds-1000`, `evoeval`) are live in `registry.json`, so these code paths execute on real benchmark runs.

## Changes

**EvoEval** (`adapters/evoeval/templates/tests/test_outputs.py`, `test_outputs_external.py`)
- Replace `eval(input_str)` with `ast.literal_eval(input_str)`. Test-case inputs are plain Python literals, so this is a safe drop-in that cannot execute arbitrary code.

**DS-1000** (`adapters/ds1000/template/tests/run_test.py`)
- Replace in-process `exec(test_program, env)` with subprocess execution of the rendered test program under:
  - a **restricted, allowlisted environment** that withholds secrets (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_API_KEY`/cloud creds) to block exfiltration,
  - a **300s timeout** to bound runaway/malicious code.
- `reward` is derived from the subprocess return code; best-effort `expected_result`/`result` repr dumps are preserved via a footer appended to the test program (runs inside the subprocess on success).

## Notes
- stdlib only (`ast`, `subprocess`); no new dependencies.
- Tasks already run inside a Docker container; the restricted env + timeout close the secret-exfiltration and runaway vectors. Subprocess isolation does not add a filesystem/network sandbox — the container remains the outer boundary.
- These are verifier/template files rendered into task environments, so no unit tests exercise them directly. A functional run of a DS-1000 / EvoEval task is worth doing before merge to confirm rewards still resolve.

author: neclor
body:
For NinePatch, UV is computed in the fragment shader, unlike regular rects where UV is computed in the vertex shader alongside the flip. 
This caused a double-flip for NinePatch when `src_rect.zw` was negative.
The fix skips the vertex shader flip for NinePatch since the fragment shader already handles it.

Part of fixing #120501

author: rodrigo-rodrigues-pc
body:
## Description

Durable agent execution built the LLM prompt by calling `llmPrompt()` **without** the
model's `supportedUrls`. As a result, file/image URLs that a provider can fetch
natively (e.g. Vertex `gs://`, Bedrock `s3://`) were treated as assets to download and
inline. They either failed with `Failed to download asset` or were corrupted into a
malformed `data:<mime>;base64,<url>` data URI before reaching the model.

This fix resolves `currentModel.supportedUrls` (awaiting it when it's a `PromiseLike`,
as with `ModelRouterLanguageModel`) and forwards it to `llmPromptForModel(...)` in the
durable LLM-execution step — bringing it in line with the standard agentic-execution
path (`loop/workflows/agentic-execution/llm-execution-step.ts`), which already does
this. With the model's supported schemes known, those URLs pass through to the provider
as references instead of being downloaded or base64-wrapped.

**Files**
- `packages/core/src/agent/durable/workflows/steps/llm-execution.ts` — resolve and pass
  `supportedUrls` to the prompt builder.
- `packages/core/src/agent/durable/__tests__/durable-agent-images.test.ts` — regression
  test: streams a `gs://` image through a durable agent whose model declares `gs://`
  support and asserts the reference reaches the model intact (not downloaded /
  base64-wrapped). Verified the test fails on the pre-fix code.

## Related issue(s)

Fixes #18648 

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Test update

## Checklist

- [x] I have linked the related issue(s) in the description above
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation (if applicable)
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] I have addressed all Coderabbit comments on this PR

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## ELI5
Durable agents were treating some “native” cloud links (like `gs://` and `s3://`) as if they had to download the image themselves. Now, if the model says it supports those URL schemes, the durable step forwards the original reference to the model—so it can fetch the asset in the provider-native way.

## Summary
- Fixed durable LLM prompt construction to respect the model’s `supportedUrls` by resolving `currentModel.supportedUrls` (including Promise-like values) and passing the resolved result into `llmPromptForModel(...)`.
- Added a regression test that streams a durable agent run containing a `gs://` image and asserts the prompt preserves the original `gs://` reference (not converted to a downloaded asset or `data:` URI).

## Impact
- Prevents durable runs from incorrectly downloading and corrupting `gs://`/`s3://` references into `data:` URIs.
- Aligns durable agent execution with the standard (non-durable) agentic path regarding `supportedUrls` handling.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

author: killer23d
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent a restore-supplied Age key from overwriting or leaking into the live operational SOPS key used by backup/pre-restore snapshot code, which caused pre-restore emergency snapshot decryption failures.
- Make the Age key prompt UX obvious (Enter = use live operational key) and add a targeted preflight so the safety snapshot fails with a clear, actionable message when current `secrets.yaml` is not decryptable with the live key.

### Description
- Introduce a restore-scoped variable `RESTORE_DECRYPT_AGE_KEY_FILE` to hold the selected-backup decrypt key and stop using `AGE_KEY_FILE` for this purpose inside `utilities/restore-run.sh`.
- Capture the live operational SOPS key as `OPERATIONAL_SOPS_AGE_KEY_FILE` and do not export or assign the restore decrypt key to the operational key variables used by SOPS tooling.
- Add `_preflight_operational_sops_key_for_snapshot()` to verify that the current `secrets.yaml` decrypts with the live SOPS key before creating the pre-restore emergency snapshot, and print a clear explanation including the `--no-backup` escape hatch if it fails.
- Ensure the emergency snapshot invocation explicitly runs with the live operational key, e.g. `SOPS_AGE_KEY_FILE="$operational_sops_age_key_file" utilities/backup-run.sh run emergency --quiet`.
- Update the interactive Age prompt text to state that for normal same-server restores the operator should press Enter to use the currently configured key and only paste an `AGE-SECRET-KEY-1...` line when restoring a backup encrypted with a different/offline key.
- Adjust rekey/update flows to use the correct restore-scoped key where appropriate and add/modify local state initialization to set `RESTORE_DECRYPT_AGE_KEY_FILE` empty until resolved.
- Add/extend `tests/test-restore-run-followup.sh` to assert the new variable usage, prompt text, explicit operational-key pass to `backup-run.sh`, and the preflight diagnostic text.

### Testing
- Ran the modified follow-up test: `bash tests/test-restore-run-followup.sh`, which passed (`ok` for the new assertions).
- Verified script syntax: `bash -n utilities/restore-run.sh` (no syntax errors).
- Ran repository checks: `git diff --check` (no trailing-whitespace/index issues reported against the change).
- Attempted to run the entire `tests/test-*.sh` loop, but the run stopped on an unrelated pre-existing test failure in `tests/test-config-systemd-followup.sh`; this failure is not introduced by these changes and pre-existed the fix.
